articles.title: Maleficent Makes Her Debut in ‘Sofia the First: Royal Magic’ (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All November 12, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ariel Winter as the titular character in 'Sofia the First: Royal Magic' Courtesy of Disney Maleficent is making her debut in the Sofia the First franchise. The iconic Sleeping Beauty villain will appear in the Sofia the First: Royal Magic holiday special, titled “Holiday at Charmswell,” premiering Nov. 26, Thanksgiving Day, on Disney Jr. and Disney+. In the holiday special, Sofia (voiced by Ariel Winter ) and Aurora (aka Sleeping Beauty) work together when the evil Maleficent comes to Charmswell during the festive holiday of Wassailia. “After years of bringing classic Disney princesses into Sofia’s world, it was exciting to finally incorporate a classic Disney villain,” said Craig Gerber , creator and executive producer of Sofia the First: Royal Magic . “Weaving Maleficent into the story of Miss Nettle, a former villain who now runs Sofia’s school, not only made for an entertaining holiday episode but also enabled us to address what seems to be Maleficent’s core reason for her evil ways — not being invited to a party.” Related Stories TV Inside Disney's New 'Sofia the First' Series With New (and Familiar) Faces, Twice the Songs and an Adorable Puppy-Corn Movies Ariel Winter's Friends Start to Vanish in Trailer for Thriller 'Don't Log Off' (Exclusive) The cast of Sofia the First: Royal Magic also includes Nate Torrence as Pepper, Sofia’s adorable, yet mischievous pet puppy-unicorn, along with Mela Pietropaolo, Kai Harris and Aaliyah Magcasi as the voices of Layla, Zane and Camila, Sofia’s new school friends. Since debuting in May, Sofia the First: Royal Magic ranks among the top 10 series for girls 2-5 in views, while driving a 77 percent increase in overall hours watched across the Sofia the First library content, according to Nielsen Media Research. Watch Maleficent in Sofia the First: Royal Magic below. THR

articles.title: YouTube’s Wildest Golf Tournament Mints Star Creators. Its Founder Explains How It Really Works
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All November 12, 2026 8:44am Add us as a Google Preferred Source YouTuber Big John putting at the 2026 Internet Invitational. YouTube If you haven’t been watching the 2026 Internet Invitational , consider this your formal invitation. It’s also something of a condemnation, because with all due respect to midseason NFL games, the best on-screen sports event right now may be a pre-taped, months-old amateur golf tournament on YouTube. The second-annual Internet Invitational, the team-based YouTube-creator golf tournament from Barstool Sports and Bob Does Sports , has taken over nearly every algorithm I have, and that is in no way a complaint. The final round, filmed in August in Missouri and furiously protected by NDAs, premieres at 1 p.m. ET on the Bob Does Sports YouTube channel. Will it be Big John, Salim the Dream and former NHL player Ryan Whitney who each leave the Ozarks with $1.33 million, or will the fat prize package go to Fat Perez, Riggs and Bobby Ray? The Internet Invitational is Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy’s creation and financial burden. But his YouTube Golf gang, Fore Play Golf (689,000 YouTube subscribers), cannot do it alone. Enter: Robby Berger , the “Bob” of Bob Does Sports (1.56 million subscribers), another huge YouTube Golf success story, and its most likable personality this side of Good Good Golf’s (2.17 million subscribers) Tom “Bubbie” Broders. (How big has YouTube Golf become? Big enough to be a proper noun in our book.) Berger, the popular genre’s glue guy, spoke with The Hollywood Reporter from his Jupiter, Florida home the day prior to (the premiere of) the Internet Invitational’s final round. Our Q&A is below. But first, more numbers. The 2026 Internet Invitational teed off on the internet on Oct. 26 with 64 of the golf-iest YouTube Golf golfers. Why say it that nonsense way? Well, they’re definitely not the 64 best golfers on YouTube. They’re not the worst 64 either (but shoutout here to The Duke ). Some are pros and some are amateurs, but it isn’t a pro-am per se. And somehow, despite streaming nowhere near live, it all works. As of this writing, the first five episodes (of six) of the tournament have amassed a combined 40 million views across 17 days of staggered Monday/Thursday releases, with the highly-anticipated final round still to go. While there is no real apples-to-apples ratings comparison with the PGA Tour’s biggest events, it is fair to say the Internet Invitational is pushing its way into major-tournament territory. This year’s Masters tournament averaged 7 million viewers per round, per Nielsen; the U.S. Open averaged 3.9 million viewers (not including round one), the PGA Championship averaged 3.2 million viewers and the British Open brought in 2.5 million viewers. (It is important to note here that a YouTube view is tallied after just 30 seconds of consumption and duplicate views count toward the total; Nielsen reports the average minute audience of television programming.) Without further delaying the pace of play… Alright Robby, I am loving every minute of this tournament. We’re speaking hours ahead of you filming the Bob Does Sports Thanksgiving episode and a day ahead of the Internet Invitational’s finale, so I appreciate the time. No, I appreciate it. Thanks for your interest, and I’m glad to hear you’ve been enjoying it. Tell me about the joint venture structure: Portnoy puts up the money, what’s your official role? It’s a full 50-50 partnership. We went in on it together. Dave had the idea, put up the money as well. For so long it had been talked about — people have tried to get all of these personalities in the same room at these tournaments, and it just didn’t make sense for everybody to get there. It was hard with schedules. For Dave to go out, put up the money that he did — he was the voice that helped really get this thing together. I just knew Dave would be the guy that could really get it done — between the financial aspect and then just him and what he’s able to do. The three winners each get $1.33 million, which is both a ton of money and kind of a random amount of money (adding to $4 million). How did you and Dave arrive at that number? To be honest, again, I’ve got to tip the cap to Dave — he led the charge there. I think he was able to gauge after the first one…the demand for brands and partnerships as well, and everything that went into it. But really, what we decided to do was put everything back into it. That was what Dave suggested. So, we haven’t made really any money from it — it’s all been pretty much put back into the tournament. That was [Portnoy’s] idea for the first one [and] for the second one as well. And obviously, it’s paid off and paid dividends. So I’m happy we did it. Brad Dalke wins 2025 Internet Invitational YouTube/Screenshot Forget winning, simply being featured in the Internet Invitational can now be a career-maker. Do you already have YouTube Golf creators in your DMs begging for a 2027 invite? Yeah, there’s been a few. There’s been like some guys and girls where it’s like, “Alright.” Like, they could be— they should be in for the next one, or we might have missed this name or that name, and a lot of people talking about that. As far as what it’s done for peoples’ careers, I always look at like Brad Dalke last year who had won the whole thing to see what it did to his career. That to me is the coolest thing, and you nailed it — it’s like win or lose, that can completely change your career. I mean, I’m seeing now with Evan Thompson the amount of people going to his page. So like, I think people know that if you go, even if you don’t win, you have a chance to really help your career. And the thing that we noticed from even the first one, people who were knocked out were hanging around. It was amazing. That was really cool, really special to me. On the last episode of the first year, I I looked around, I was like, “Man, all these people could have gone home and they’re all here.” And that was really special. It also seems like the most fun party possible. [Laughs] Yeah, that too. I never thought I’d be this into a non-live sporting event, but with the number of cameras, the care taken in post-production, and of course, the NDAs, it works — though it is quite the editing task. Sports are valued on traditional TV due to their live nature — do you think the Internet Invitational will ever go live? You know, it’s a good question. I thought about maybe doing the final live. That’s a conversation that we’ve had, but I think you’ve got to be able to protect all the moments that we’re able to get, and I think the Barstool production guys do such a good job editing it that I think live would take away a lot of the drama and the moments. So yeah, that’s something we’ve talked about. I think if anything, down the road, the conversation we’ve had is: “Do you do the finale live?” Maybe one day, but for now, I just think it’s so good as it is, it’s one of those things where, you know, if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it. How do you pick the field? Some of the players are obvious: they’re yours or Dave’s or Good Good, etc., but there are always a few randoms and a few “Why nots?” Like, why not Golf Sidekick ? We are so entrenched within the YouTube Golf space, between Bob Does Sports and then [Barstool Sports’] Fore Play Golf as well. We really know what’s going on around the YouTube Golf space. So we always are constantly looking out for new people and new names that have come up. For us, I think the biggest thing that we go for, really, it’s personality above all. Like you know, some people have put in their request to me of, you know, “I’m a scratch.” It’s like, that’s great, but we don’t really care because our thing is having all ranges of golf handicaps and whatnot. So really, it’s personality above all. Who has traction around the YouTube Golf space? Who do people want to see as well? So all of that goes into it. And then there’s always new names that are popping up. It’s funny. I’ll give you a name that probably could have been in it that really popped up after we had done the list. There’s a name like Chance Taylor who really popped up after the list was done. [He] will probably get an invite for next year. And of course, there’s always going to be the names of, “What about this guy, that girl?” And to me, that’s a good thing. Like, people talking about that — that’s great. We’re always open to looking at that and seeing who is next. So I think that kind of dialogue of, “How come not this person or that person?” — to me, that’s a really good, positive thing. Would the internet invitational be better or worse if you replaced the 8 highest handicapped golfers there and added the 8 best players in the world? pic.twitter.com/CV11TkVOmY — Wesley Bryan (@wesleybryangolf) November 4, 2026 Wesley Bryan, the tournament’s former PGA Tour winner, put out a controversial tweet asking if the Internet Invitational would be made better by dropping the worst eight golfers from this year’s field and adding the best eight PGA Tour pros. It was not especially well-received by YouTube Golf fans, whom I agree with: the special part of the tournament is its average-Joe golf-game quality. What is your response to Wesley’s tweet? Wesley’s a good friend, and look — Wesley definitely knows how to stir the pot. He definitely did a good job of doing that. But I agree with you. The Duke, who I worked with at the Four Seasons— seeing a guy sweat over a shot, having no idea where the ball is going to go, there’s a certain beauty to that. Seeing people scratching and crawling to win life-changing money. I look at Beef — you know, last year and rest in peace — asking him what he would do with the money, and he got choked up just talking about buying his parents a house, and he did exactly that. When you put the average Joe, who’s not a great golfer— that, to I think a lot of people, was riveting. I mean, it’s kind of what Bob Does Sports was built off of. Not on purpose — I’d love to hit shots, knowing where it’s going — but people love that of not knowing where it’s going, not having the best golfer. So I think a whole range of handicaps is great. And again, for us, it’s personality above all. But yeah, I think there’s a certain beauty to that. So I’m all for higher handicaps. I would rather watch that type of shot with a mix of good golfers. So I think it’s a perfect mix. Let’s talk about The Duke who is, by far, the worst golfer out there. Because he had strong teammates, Duke was carried through to the final 12 . But then the alternate shot format made it impossible for his teammates (Ryan Ruffels and Marissa Wenzler) to carry the burden. Because of the serious money on the line, it created a really unfortunate situation for two very good golfers who could have won — especially Ruffels — will The Duke be invited to play again next year? As it went on, you’re exactly right. That is something that’s cool with this tournament, is somebody with a very high handicap that isn’t that good can get carried to the finals and get carried, you know, a really long way. Look, I think you’ve got to listen to the audience for sure, and what they’re asking for, and at the same time, the conversation that I’ll have to have with the Barstool guys as well. I think it was perfect for the time that we had The Duke, but it’s definitely something that we’ve got to look into. Obviously, it’s been cool to watch him— I mean, I remember seeing him at the Four Seasons when we worked there together. We didn’t really talk at all, so we met on the golf course. But you’ve got to listen to the audience, it’s the conversation that we have to have because there are a lot of people that got left [behind], and there are certain times where people can be exposed the further they go. It’s something we’ve definitely got to look into for sure. I don’t have the answer yet , but we listen to everything, and it’s it’s something we gotta look into. Did Big John’s ball move in his match against Sam? Well, to be honest, I didn’t see much. Sam had posted a clip on Instagram where it does look like it moved, but that’s something where, if we’re going out to film a regular YouTube Golf video, you call somebody out for that, and the YouTube Golf Community would find that to be a very nervy thing to do. I don’t question anybody for anything they do when it comes to that amount of money on the line. Things definitely change, and again, it’s something you would never see going out to film a regular YouTube Golf video, but when you put that type of money on the line, you know, it does things. In some ways these controversies only exist because of the generosity of the purse. If not for the huge money, neither The Duke thing nor the penalties (that may or may not have happened) would matter. A hundred percent. There was a lot of talk around— and look, I’m not saying that it can’t happen, but there’s certain athletes that have even reached out to me — like big time athletes — about being in the Internet Invitational. I think the downside to that is you want it to be life-changing money for the people there. That brings out that drama, that brings out everything. Whereas, you know, there’s a lot of athletes where that money wouldn’t affect them as much. So I think that’s the problem you have if you put in real athletes. I think there’s a way to work them in — whether they be captains and not in it for the money — but that is the beauty of the tournament that might get taken away if you have big time athletes partaking in it. Not to say it can’t happen, but that is definitely a downside to it. There’s been some athletes that have called and said things to me where it’s like, I don’t know how you turn down that person, but it’s definitely a conversation we’ll have, and I think we’ll make the right play with it and see where it goes. But it’s just a testament to how how big this thing has gotten, and to see that they’re all watching. Salim the Dream at 2026 Internet Invitational YouTube/Screenshot I want to talk a bit about the drinking. I’m no teetotaler, definitely like to have a few on the golf course. But in the Internet Invitational, we see people getting absolutely sloshed deep in a team-based tournament, which could again cost someone else a huge prize. The most obvious example is with Salim the Dream, who appeared blackout drunk in the semifinals episode. Now, he played so well in that state it hasn’t cost anybody — yet. What are your thoughts on that topic? We want to trust everybody that we have to drink responsibly and not give it away. And I know there’s definitely nerves and everything that, you know, to a degree people like taking the edge off or whatnot. But we expect them to do that responsibly to where it doesn’t affect the play. Up until this point, I think it’s kind of worked for Salim because he’s playing good. But then there’s the downside of it. If you’re not playing good and you’re affecting your team, and you’re at a level where you’re so drunk — it does come to a thing where it’s not necessarily fair to your teammates, and absolutely can bother people for sure. So I think we’ve got to trust people to do the right thing and to make the right decisions on that front, and and see kind of how it plays out from there — but yeah, you’ve got to be very very mindful of that. You’re not just playing for yourself. And it’s worth me repeating again for the story that, as far as what we’ve seen, Salim has played exceptionally well as drunk as he was. (Salim also issued this statement following the release of episode five: “There’s a reason I challenged myself to 90 days sober after the Internet Invitational. Watching these episodes back is a good reminder of why I started. 87/90.”) You know what’s so funny is I struggle with my tempo, Tony. I’m watching him and I’m like, “How can a man be that intoxicated and swinging so smooth?” I thought the exact same thing. OK, I saved this one a bit: Are you able to quantify just how much money, followers, success the 2026 Internet Invitational will bring to Big John, who has been its breakout star after sinking arguably the biggest putt in YouTube Golf history ? I went to him after he hit the putt, and I said, “It doesn’t matter if you win this thing or lose this thing. What you just gained far outweighs any money that you can win. That is a career changer.” So he’s gonna make way more than even what the prize purse was, just based off what it now has done to his career. Brand deals are gonna come in— I mean, I remember seeing Brad Dalke right after he won, had a new sponsor, and that’s awesome. That’s the stuff we really, really love to see. And you know the thing with Big John is meeting him — of course he likes to have fun and likes to party and all of that stuff — he could not be a nicer guy. To see it happen to people that you truly want to root for, I really think that the people that win in YouTube Golf and have a lot of longevity are the people that are easy to root for and that are very likable. He is one of those guys, and his career will never be the same in a really good way. The other guy I expect this to help go from relative unknown to potential YouTube Golf superstar is Bobby Ray . The interesting thing about his Internet Invitational debut is that he went from tournament villain for basically scaring Short Game King to one of its more-likable guys. I thought he was kind of a dick after episode one, and then a few episodes later I’m rooting for him. Oh, totally! A lot of times it’s like who you’re matched up with, who you’re playing, what clip, who brings what out of you where things can totally change. It’s unbelievable what can happen week to week. Finally, I want to give a shoutout to (four-time PGA Tour winner) Kevin Kisner — how great has he been as the rules official for the tournament? People talk like, you know, “Should Kisner play in it?” My thing against it is you want as much Kisner as possible. So if you have him playing, you don’t get him bouncing around to all these different holes. So he’s so good in that role and just so likable and just fits in perfectly. He’s really fun and funny, but also extremely effective in what becomes a surprisingly important role for what is purposefully the opposite of a PGA Tour event. It was very smart to have him. The first year it was Dave and Big Cat [as rules officials], and they don’t know the golf rules too well, and it got to a point where when you have that amount of money on the line, you have to have somebody there that knows the actual rules. So you’re exactly right. I mean, he was so perfect to have there, and it was amazing how much he was needed throughout. The Internet Invitational finale episode rolls out on YouTube on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 1 p.m. ET. THR

articles.title: Around 10-15 Percent of SAG-AFTRA Membership Wants AI Blocked, CEO Tells Web Summit
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All November 12, 2026 8:52am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Duncan Crabtree-Ireland photographed in 2026 Courtesy of Getty Hollywood’s identity crisis was in focus at Lisbon’s Web Summit on Thursday. SAG-AFTRA ‘s national executive director and CEO Duncan Crabtree-Ireland was joined by Dan Neely, the co-founder and CEO of Vermillio, an AI licensing and protection platform aimed at helping humanity thrive in the age of generative AI. They spoke with Deadline ‘s Stewart Clarke about performers’ rights, coexisting with AI and the potentially landmark NO FAKES Act (Nurture Originals, Foster Art, and Keep Entertainment Safe Act), U.S. federal legislation currently in process (and in the U.K.) that is designed to protect a person’s voice and visual likeness against unauthorized digital replica uses. “I think that there’s been a sense that if we put the right basic rules in place, there is a way to coexist with AI,” said Crabtree-Ireland at the summit. “I think there’s been an understanding and an acceptance of the fact that no one can stop it, no one can block it. Some of our members would like us to block it. I hear from them every day, and they’re angry that we aren’t,” he said. When asked what percentage of SAG-AFTRA’s 160,000-strong membership would like to see AI completely obstructed, he replied: “If I were estimating, I’d say something like 10 percent, maybe 15 percent.” Crabtree-Ireland is buoyed by the collective agreement on three basic principles when it comes to adopting artificial intelligence in the entertainment space — consent, control and compensation. “When you’re taking someone’s image and doing that, those should be present,” he said. The fight for ethical use of AI is ongoing, he maintained, and said that much of SAG-AFTRA’s motivation is the shared certainty on the need for the human spark of creativity in our work. “We had a big strike in 2023. My favorite picket sign from that strike, a writer’s picket sign, not one of ours […] was ‘ChatGPT doesn’t have childhood trauma,'” said Crabtree-Ireland, “and I think that’s right. The human condition is uniquely human, and just mimicking it or copying it because you’ve been trained on it doesn’t mean that you can actually generate that spark of creativity.” He continued: “Some of our members really want to work with AI tools for augmentation, but none of them want to be replaced by AI because they love the act of creation. That’s why they do this. It’s an incredibly hard career. It’s so hard to be an artist in this world. But you do it because you love it. […] What you want to do is have the chance to do it, and yes, have tools that help you expand your creativity. And so that’s the sweet spot of this. And frankly, if we could settle on that, and then spend the rest of the AI resources towards curing some more diseases or some other things like that, I think we could get on board with that.” Neely, meanwhile, was bullish on his platform’s ability to course-correct. “We’ve developed a technology that allows us to detect when unauthorized uses happen,” he began to Clarke. “And then, once we understand that, and someone decides, ‘Hey, I’m actually okay giving consent now for something to take place. Here are the guardrails under which that can happen.’ So we have a guardrails product that says, ‘You can make these things,’ [or] ‘You can’t make those things.'” The Vermillio model itself ingests content from major intellectual property holders such as music labels, studios, book publishers, and talent. Unsurprisingly, a gray area has swiftly emerged — performers may suspect their likeness is being used but can’t say it is definitively their voice or look. “We have metrics to say what it is and what it is not,” explained Neely. “Maybe 30 percent Duncan’s voice, 30 percent of my voice and 40 percent original — we need to be able to determine at those levels what’s going on,” he said as an example. “So Duncan could block my right and I could block his.” The company are expecting “much more clarity” around that specific topic in the next 12 months. Crabtree-Ireland jumped in here to say SAG-AFTRA has a lower bar in this regard: “If it is going to be perceived as your voice, if it clearly sounds like you or if it looks like you — this is also an issue in the audiovisual world — then that is a replica.” He brought up the case of Scarlett Johansson, who threatened industry titan OpenAI with legal action for allegedly copying and imitating her voice after she refused to license it to the company. “I think OpenAI ultimately did the right thing and took that down. They did not admit that her voice was used, but it sure sounded a lot like her,” said Crabtree-Ireland, though he conceded it’s proved impossible to stay ahead of the technology advancements in AI. One major problem for the industry is that sense of built-in fandom. “Very few people are creating unique and interesting things and just saying, ‘Oh, this is going to survive on its own,'” said Neely. “What happens is, no, they attach themselves to something that already has fandom and fame. So I’m going to go use an actor’s likeness, their name, their image, their voice. I’m going to use an aspect of that because that’s going to drive people to go listen to it, watch it, do something with it. And so that’s what’s happening more often than not.” That, he added, is why the issue of likeness is so rife. Check out Web Summit’s panel with The Hollywood Reporter editor-in-chief Maer Roshan here . The conference runs Nov. 9-12. THR

articles.title: ‘Ebenezer’ Review: Johnny Depp Gets a Creepily Effective Comeback Vehicle in Ti West’s Horror-Tinged Take on Dickens’ Yuletide Classic
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Frank Scheck Plus Icon Frank Scheck View All November 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Johnny Depp (right) and Rupert Grint in 'Ebenezer.' Paramount Pictures Did the world need another cinematic adaptation of Charles Dickens’ classic A Christmas Carol ? Not really, considering the myriad versions that have appeared over the years, which play with regularity on television screens every holiday season. But Johnny Depp really needed a comeback vehicle, and he’s found an effective one in Ti West ’s horror-tinged adaptation that allows the actor to deliver the sort of quirky theatrical performance for which he became famous. While Ebenezer doesn’t break any new ground, other than possibly being the first version of the story not really suitable for young children, it fulfills its ostensible goal of restoring the actor to A-list status. Related Stories Movies Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer': First Reactions Movies AFM Hot Project: Daisy Ridley, Sosie Bacon, Simon Rex Join 'Get Rid of It' Considering that the director’s oeuvre consists of such films as The House of the Devil , Cabin Fever 2: Spring Fever , and the recent acclaimed X trilogy, it’s not surprising that this version of the Yuletide tale features a dark Gothic tone. Indeed, Ebenezer feels essentially like a horror film for most of its running time, featuring jump scares, grotesque visuals, and enough ghostly creatures to fuel a season of American Horror Story . It’s no wonder a terrified Scrooge pees himself at one point. Ebenezer The Bottom Line Gets the ghostly job done. Release date : Friday, November 13 Cast : Johnny Depp, Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber, Henry Lloyd-Hughes, Charlie Murphy, Tramell Tillman, Ian McKellen Director : Ti West Screenwriter : Nathaniel Halpern Rated PG-13, 1 hour 56 minutes Still, plenty of care has been taken for the movie, which features handsome visuals, excellent production design, and a stacked cast including Ian McKellen as Scrooge’s business partner Jacob Marley. Nathaniel Halpern’s screenplay expands upon the tale by providing more backstory than usual, with Marley still alive in the pre-credits prologue and demonstrating that he was just as irascible and nasty as Scrooge. Cut to seven years later, when Scrooge is at his most Scrooge-like, uttering enough humbugs to satisfy those Dickens fans. (Another nod to them is that the film is divided into “staves,” as was the author’s novella.) Soon enough, Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his former partner, who, besides carrying those infernal chains, looks decidedly worse for wear. Marley warns him that he’ll soon be visited by three ghosts who will … wait, why am I relating the story? You already know it. First, of course, is the Ghost of Christmas Past, played by a wispy Andrea Riseborough made up to look like a corpse that’s been left out in the sun. She brings Scrooge back to his early days, when his younger self (Arthur Conti, Carrie ) was in love with his fiancée Belle (Ellie Bamber), whom he subsequently lost due to his misplaced priorities. Then there’s the Ghost of Christmas Present, a surly figure played by Tramell Tillman ( Severance ), who physically decays as the visit wears on, eventually revealing horrific creatures trapped in his body. Finally, there’s the Ghost of Christmas Future (the appropriately named Robert Strange), an otherworldly apparition who introduces himself by having a crow fly out of his mouth. Interspersed with all the creepiness, which includes numerous rampaging ghosts behaving like zombies, are some moments of genuine emotion. Depp provides moving glimpses into Scrooge’s underlying humanity, from his missing his deceased partner to his anguish over having lost Belle to his pity for Tiny Tim (Freddie Lee-Grey), his employee Bob Cratchit’s ( Rupert Grint ) disabled son. Indeed, it’s when the film lets up on the frights and allows the story to breathe that it becomes most effective. The final redemption sequence, in which Depp gets to relax and show off his comic chops with the character’s newfound joyfulness as he visits nephew Fred ( Sam Claflin ) and his wife Clara ( Daisy Ridley ) with goose in tow, is a delight. Depp, outfitted with prosthetic make-up and facial hair, delivers a performance that no one would call subtle. In style, it most closely resembles a heavily made-up Albert Finney’s broad take on the character in the now largely forgotten 1970 musical Scrooge . But the actor’s charisma and star power eventually come through. articles.title: You Can’t See Everything: The Sneaky Problem With the Elizabeth Holmes Movie
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Steven Zeitchik Plus Icon Steven Zeitchik Senior Editor, Technology and Politics View All November 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Illustration by Christopher Hughes Logo text More than 100 years ago, a filmmaker directed the first documentary . Controversy has followed the form ever since. Nanook of the North , Robert Flaherty’s Inuit vérité, redefined way back in 1922 how we imagined cinema, but critics in subsequent decades charged him with staging scenes, sensationalizing events and substituting actors for real people. In the 1980s, Errol Morris disrupted the doc world with The Thin Blue Line , his reexamination of a Texas murder case from a decade earlier. So compellingly did Morris interrogate the incident that it led to an overturned conviction — but prompted a whole new inquest into why he reconstructed scenes. Two decades later, Michael Moore dropped the grenade of Fahrenheit 9/11 . The look at George W. Bush’s foreign policy sins brought Americans to the theaters by the millions but generated heat for what Moore exaggerated or left out. Related Stories Movies 'One in a Million' Filmmaker on the Ethical Dilemma He Faced and Learning to Let His Subject Find Her Own Way Movies Amanda Seyfried Feared 'You Can See Everything' Could "Destroy" Her Career, Says Her Opinion of Billy Evans "Only Got Worse" Yet something feels different with this decade’s documentary sensation, which doesn’t just play fast and loose with the truth, but plays fast and loose with the truth while making the truth the very subject of its inquiry. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s observational Elizabeth Holmes doc You Can See Everything , ostensibly about how much Holmes and her husband, Billy Evans, are lying, has already solicited the kind of box office dollars more familiar to midbudget thrillers. Like its forebears, YCSE leaves itself open to questions about manipulation, starting with the fact that two camera setups followed every supposedly unselfconscious reaction, and the fact that Holmes initiated the project, possibly with crisis PR specialist Risa Heller, who helped place a soft interview in The New York Times at around the same time. But this time skepticism goes beyond fears of subject-nudging and selective editing. The entire YCSE project is built by people who specialize in presenting falsehoods as truth, each layer composed by someone whose very brand is deception, like a grift-y cinematic lasagna. Holmes spent years duping presidents into believing the reality she created, and in that light, how many of her utterances can be taken as honest? Did she really, for instance, not understand “Who’s on First?” or what Fielder was getting at by challenging her on what Theranos’ machine couldn’t do in reality? Fielder has made a profitable living fudging fiction into truth — a season finale of his HBO show The Rehearsal tragically convinced a child he was the boy’s own father — and his involvement here can’t but cast a wait-a-minute cloak over the exercise. What we’re seeing, what we’re not seeing, how details have been shaded to make everyone in it, including him, seem like something they may not have been. Nathan Fielder moniters the cameras in the season one finale of The Rehearsal. Even the person regarded as the most authentic — Amanda Seyfried, the audience surrogate into whose hands we unthinkingly place our trust — is a skilled performance magician who did not, previous screen appearances to the contrary, introduce writers to William Randolph Hearst, get raised by Jean Valjean or hold a contest to determine her real father on a Greek island. Yet somehow we assume that she and all of her fellow master-conjurers are here telling us what actually happened. I mean, it’s a documentary; why would they do otherwise? Fielder and Oppenheim made truth the subject of their documentary — “you can see everything,” the title promises us — and then proceeded to fillet it at every turn. It is a testament to their power as filmmakers that we come away smugly confident at how we have caught on to what Holmes is trying to do to Fielder while often staying oblivious to what Fielder has just done to us. As veteran journalist and commentator Matt Pearce wrote on Substack recently, ” ‘I’m just trying to be accurate,’ Fielder says toward the end of his film, lying through his fucking teeth.” That’s not to say the movie isn’t great fun, full of enjoyable surprises and, in the end, a compelling meditation on reality and gullibility. It also doesn’t mean we’re not the mark. On one level, perhaps none of this matters. Why get hung up on how much is “real” when the whole thing is such a damn good time at the theater? Yet the movie’s blunt force comes precisely from that documentary categorization; fully invent the exact same film and YCSE loses a lot of its power. But even more important than what the documentary does for Fielder is what Fielder does for, or to, the documentary; such a good time risks turning the category, currently our most important broadcast investigative medium, into one more ennui-inducing vehicle for postmodern winkiness, a perhaps not-great development in an ecosystem where shared facts are already gasping for air. In such a context, other fast-and-loose criticisms raised against docs this season — Alex Gibney’s decision to create and deploy a speaking avatar of Elon Musk using his own words in Musk , or Ava DuVernay’s deployment of AI to bring archival photos to life in The 14th — seem like peccadilloes. And yet all come as part of the same set of questions. Documentary has entered a double reckoning, both technologically in this deepfake age, given how easily something can be made to look real, and ethically, given how much harder it can be in an era of echo-chamber truth to know what “real” is in the first place. Elon Musk in Alex Gibney’s documentary Musk . Alex Brandon/AP Images Into this morass, a further irony: a movie that’s largely scripted but may paint a truer picture. Ali G has lost something off his fastball since he and the Sacha Baron Cohen who disappeared into him gleefully confronted public leaders on HBO two decades ago with his convicted stupidity, revealing what lies behind the politesse of an ATF officer, a surgeon general and Donald Trump. And yet at his best, Baron Cohen in his new movie still pulls off all the spiritual aims of the season’s big documentary, only without hiding behind that word’s protective shield. Ali G: Who Iz I? picks up on the lab experiment Baron Cohen started in 2018’s Showtime series Who Is America? Perhaps it should come as no surprise that working with and learning from him on that show nearly a decade ago was one Nathan Fielder, who came to understand both the combustive power of unmasking foolishness onscreen and how much more explosive the chemical reaction would be if you just pretended everything was real. Every era gets the brand of documentary it deserves. In a time of rampant disinformation and unabated conspiracy theories, when nobody believes anything they (or their algorithm) haven’t curated and everyone resists attempts by others to try to change their mind, when every person speaks their own “truth” and decades of relativism has turned objective facts into a hilarious fiction, YCSE is, for better or worse, our most emblematic work. The film opens a new window, all right, not on Holmes but on us, staggering among the postmodern wreckage like a marooned sailor who still hasn’t come to terms with the fact that his ship is gone. You Can See Everything is a fascinating snapshot of our social state. I’m just not sure it’s a documentary. Sacha Baron Cohen in Ali G: Who Iz I? Courtesy of Amazon MGM Studios This story appeared in the Nov. 12 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: Searchlight Pictures Enters Merch Partnership With Universal Music’s Bravado (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All November 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sam Rockwell and John Malkovich in 'Wild Horse Nine.' Diego Araya Corvalán/Courtesy of Searchlight Pictures Bravado, the merchandising arm of Universal Music Group , is entering a partnership with Searchlight Pictures , the companies announced on Wednesday, marking the first time Bravado has worked with a film studio on merchandise. Bravado and Searchlight are starting the partnership with merch for Wild Horse Nine, including t-shirts as well as a bowling bag, signet rings, a scarf, passport holder and keychain among other offerings. They’re also selling vinyl from the film’s soundtrack. “We’re excited to partner with Bravado to explore new and innovative ways to bring Searchlight films to life beyond the screen,” Matthew Greenfield, President of Searchlight Pictures said in a statement. “Their creative vision and forward-thinking approach make them a great fit for our studio, and Wild Horse Nine is an exciting first opportunity to push creative boundaries together.” Bravado handles branding and merchandise for a wide swath of superstars including the Rolling Stones, the Beatles, Post Malone, Guns N’ Roses, and A$AP Rocky among many others. Bravado’s clientele is mostly music brands, though the company also works with Harley-Davidson and Travis Pastrana’s Channel 199. Searchlight represents the first time a film studio has partnered with Bravado on merch and reflects the merch company’s broader strategy in looking to court new business. The deal comes months after Bravado appointed Dan Goldberg as SVP of Strategy & New Ventures, where he was tasked with finding new verticals for the company beyond its typical music partnerships. “Searchlight has built an incredible catalog of films that people have real connections to and we’re thrilled to be working with them as our first partner in film and entertainment,” Goldberg said in a statement. “Great films create lasting fandom, and we see a real opportunity to build on that through products and experiences that extend those stories beyond the screen.” THR

articles.title: Damian Lewis to Star in Paramount+ Soccer Comedy ‘Day 1s,’ Matthew Vaughn Directing
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All November 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Damian Lewis Zak Hussein/Variety/Getty Images Logo text Paramount+ is teaming with a couple of soccer legends in its latest series pickup. The streamer has greenlit a comedy called Day 1s set in the world of the English Premier League. Damian Lewis ( Billions ) will star in the series, which also counts soccer greats Cristiano Ronaldo and Thierry Henry among its executive producers. Matthew Vaughn (the Kingsman franchise) directed the pilot episode, and Dan Mazer ( Borat ) will serve as showrunner. Day 1s is the first production for UR-MARV Studios, a joint venture Vaughn and Ronaldo recently launched. DoubleD Sports, led by Darren Dein, also produces in association with Archery Pictures. Related Stories TV Michelle Pfeiffer and Kurt Russell Tease Major "Twists" in Season 2 of 'The Madison' TV CBS Unveils Competitors for Drew Barrymore-Hosted 'Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic' Special (Exclusive) “We couldn’t be more pleased to be working with Casey [Bloys], Sarah [Aubrey], Amy [Gravitt] and the team at Paramount+ on a show that Darren conceived and pitched to me,” Vaughn said in a statement. “It’s the perfect project for Cristiano and I to start our company with — and to say he is a friend and a partner is a true honor. I’m sure the man who has broken every record in football will soon be doing the same in film and TV.” Day 1s will follow “a gifted young footballer who achieves his dream of playing in the Premier League when he signs for Brentford FC, bringing along his friends who stood by him long before the money, fame and success — his Day 1s,” the show’s logline reads. Brentford is a real club in the Premier League, based in West London and currently eighth in the 2026-27 season. “I’ve spent my entire life in football, and I know that some of the most powerful stories happen away from the pitch,” said Ronaldo. “Football is about dreams, ambition, loyalty, sacrifice and the people who believe in you from day one. That’s what makes Day 1s special. As a producer, I’m proud to help bring a different side of the game to life, through a story that I believe can connect with audiences far beyond football. To take this first journey in the industry alongside my partner and friend Matthew Vaughn and having a superb former player and a great person like Thierry Henry on board makes this all even more special.” Vaughn, Dein, Ronaldo, Henry, Mazer and Lewis are executive producing the series with Doug Ellin ( Entoruage ) and Kris Thykier. “I’m thrilled to be joining Day 1s as an executive producer and to be working with Paramount+, Matthew Vaughn, Damian Lewis and such an incredible cast and crew,” said Henry. “This is a project with real heart and I’m excited for audiences to see it. It’s also a welcome change to finally be on the same team as Cristiano after so many battles on the pitch.” Added Lewis, “ Day 1s is a show about friendship and football. I’m excited to be in the starting line-up. Can’t wait for kick-off.” Vaughn is repped by WME and Johnson Shapiro. Mazer is with CAA LBI Entertainment and Davis Law Group. Lewis is repped by Markham, Froggatt & Irwin and Range Media Partners. Henry is with DoubleD Sports. Thykier is repped by Del Shaw. THR

articles.title: YouTuber Dami Lee Signs With CAA (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dami Lee Courtesy of CAA Architect Dami Lee, who uses her expertise to bring niche design concepts to a wider audience through digital storytelling, has signed with CAA for representation . With around 2.5 million followers for her YouTube channel, Lee’s recent videos include Is Chongqing REALLY a Cyberpunk City? , which has over 3 million views, and another two million views for Why Lord of the Rings Architecture Isn’t Just Fantasy… It’s a Warning. CAA will also represent Nollistudio, a video production banner Lee co-founded with filmmaker Raffaele di Nicola, to bring creator content to YouTube and other platforms. The Hollywood talent agency will work with Lee and Nollistudio to expand their creator economy business and YouTube channel across all areas. Lee’s cinematic storytelling explores buildings or cities, whether from history and imagined environments, that audiences can potentially see with new eyes and fresh opinions. That includes video content that plays off architecture as seen through the lens of film, TV and popular culture. Lee has explored beyond design concepts through the fictional landscapes of Dune , as with The Hidden Secrets of Dune’s Darkest Planet, and Lord of the Rings . And Nollistudio also explores real-world architecture and cities that have shaped our world, as with popular YouTube videos about ancient water holes beneath the Iranian desert and new theories about Egyptian pyramids. “Their multidisciplinary team combines design, research and filmmaking to explore how the built environment shapes our lives,” CAA said in a statement about Nollistudio’s video output. THR

articles.title: Dark Comedy ‘Honeyjoon’ Returning to Theaters As Launch Film for John Fithian’s New Venture
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Honeyjoon' Inés Gowland The Tribeca award-winning indie dramedy Honeyjoon by director Lilian T. Mehrel will return to theaters in early 2027 as a launch film for the Fithian Group’s theatrical marketplace platform Attend. The announcement was made Wednesday at the American Film Market , where Mehrel took part in a panel on using technology and data, including the Attend marketplace, to transform indie film distribution. Honeyjoon , a dark comedy starring Jackpot! actor Ayden Mayeri and Amira Casar and about a Kurdish-Persian mother and her American daughter vacationing in the Azores after a major loss, had an earlier limited theatrical release by Utopia’s arthouse label Circle Collective in summer 2026. Mehrel will now expand her theatrical rollout using the digital and marketing platform offered by The Fithian Group that matches producers and filmmakers directly with cinemas without having to partner with a traditional distributor. Fithian Group founding partner Patrick Corcoran in a statement said “we are thrilled to collaborate with Lilian on the theatrical expansion of Honeyjoon with Attend. She is the kind of bold visionary filmmaker that we want to launch our platform. We can’t wait for more audiences to share this unforgettable theatrical experience.” That will follow Honeyjoon winning the $1 million AT&T Untold Stories Award after premiering at Tribeca in 2025. The film went on to play around 50 festivals, including the Tribeca Lisboa Festival in Portugal a year ago, and win over 25 audience and jury awards. Now John Fithian — who founded The Fithian Group after heading up the National Association of Theatre Owners along with two of his longtime lieutenants at NATO, Corcoran and Jackie Brenneman – has tapped Honeyjoon as a curated inaugural film to launch Attend. The goal of Attend is to match a movie like Honeyjoon with the right makeup of cinemas based on various data. A filmmaker will upload various data into the platform, which will use AI to determine where best the movie might perform. Mehrel said of her distribution deal with Attend in her own statement: “The audience response led the way. Every screening, audiences burst into laughter and tears and share that the film makes them feel alive… they made it clear that Honeyjoon needs to be shared in more theaters, for more people to discover and share this special experience. I’m so excited to do that with Attend.” THR

articles.title: MotoGP U.S. Rights Head to ESPN in Deal With Liberty Media
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All November 12, 2026 9:21am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Maximo Quiles of Spain and CFMOTO Gaviota Aspar Team leads the field during the Moto3 race during the MotoGP Of Malaysia - Race at Sepang Circuit on November 1, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Photo by Mirco Lazzari gp/Getty Images ESPN is back in business with Liberty Media . The sports media juggernaut has inked a deal to broadcast MotoGP, the motorcycle racing circuit owned by Liberty, beginning in 2027. It’s a two-year deal that will cover both the U.S. and Latin America, where ESPN already had MotoGP rights. MotoGP’s most recent U.S. rights were with Fox Sports, and they had previously been with Warner Bros. Discovery and NBC Sports. ESPN say that the races will air on all of ESPN’s platforms, as well as on Disney+. Liberty Media, which is led by Derek Chang, owns both MotoGP and Formula 1, which left ESPN this year to move its U.S. rights to Apple TV. Liberty bought MotoGP in 2024 at a $4.5 billion valuation with a goal of building it into a worldwide brand as it has done with F1. The U.S. market, for obvious reasons, is a top priority, so ESPN’s reach is seen as a boost to that effort. “This agreement with ESPN marks an important milestone in MotoGP’s growth strategy across the Americas,” said Carlos Ezpeleta, deputy CEO of MotoGP. “ESPN’s position as one of the world’s leading sports broadcasters, combined with its strong connection with audiences across the United States and Latin America, makes it the ideal platform for us to continue expanding MotoGP’s reach and bring the sport closer to millions of people. This is an exciting opportunity to introduce MotoGP to new audiences while continuing to serve our passionate existing fan base through one of the most influential sports media brands in the world.” “ESPN and MotoGP have a strong relationship that dates back nearly 25 years, when we began bringing the championship to fans across Latin America,” added Freddy Rolón, head of global sports & talent office for ESPN. “This is a great example of how relationships that begin in one region of our international business can grow across ESPN’s global portfolio, creating new opportunities to connect different audiences with world-class sporting events.” THR

articles.title: ‘Ebenezer’ Review: Johnny Depp Scowls His Way Through a Spookily Atmospheric but Redundant ‘Christmas Carol’ Retread
articles.full_text: × Nov 12, 2026 9:00am PT ‘Ebenezer’ Review: Johnny Depp Scowls His Way Through a Spookily Atmospheric but Redundant ‘Christmas Carol’ Retread Tinged with horror, as one might expect with Ti West at the helm, the umpteenth adaptation of the seasonal standard isn't a Scrooge-up, but who exactly is it for? By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest Remembering Sebastián Lelio, an Auteur Who Centered Women’s Stories With Style and Sensitivity 4 days ago ‘Jimmy’ Review: Cornball James Stewart Biopic Gets the Manner, but Not the Man 6 days ago ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ Review: Football Heroes Take to the Battlefield in Peter Berg’s Emptily Macho WWII Epic 2 weeks ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source ©Paramount/Courtesy Everett Collection “Before he was Scrooge he was Ebenezer ,” claims the poster for “Ebenezer,” which seems a bit of a desperate lie. The character of Ebenezer Scrooge did, presumably, have a first and last name at all stages of his life, both of them quite well-known to anyone even tangentially acquainted with Charles Dickens’ novella “A Christmas Carol” — of which Ti West ‘s handsomely produced, Gothically flavored new film is the latest in a countless string of adaptations. Other marketing materials at least acknowledge the familiarity — “The name you know, the story you don’t,” runs another tagline — while still positioning “Ebenezer” as some kind of origin story or alternative spin on an oft-told tale. Related Stories UFC 333 Livestream: Here's How to Watch Volkanovski vs. Evloev Online for Free The biggest surprise of the film, however, is that it’s really no such thing. A mostly straightforward take, albeit with slightly grislier ghost effects than most viewers will be used to, it tweaks and pads the narrative here and there — but not in ways drastic or daring enough to justify all this revisionist framing. That’s more of a relief than it is a disappointment — an edgelord “Christmas Carol” wasn’t on anybody’s holiday wishlist — but you can see why the powers that be at Paramount may have been inclined to exaggerate matters a little. As it is, the most unique selling point of “Ebenezer” is the retro Hammer horror styling that one might expect from West, the indie-rooted genre classicist behind “The House of the Devil” and the “X” trilogy. Yet this PG-13 release also stops some way short of being an outright horror film, faithfully upholding Dickens’ sentimentally redemptive arc and meaning-of-Christmas message. Too frightening for many children and too old hat for many adults, then, “Ebenezer’s” commercial prospects thus rest on its biggest gamble: the casting of Johnny Depp in the title role. Back from the international arthouse wilderness after eight years on the A-list blacklist, Depp returns to studio cinema to take on the kind of flamboyantly transformative, pantomime-style part that he used to do on the regular for the likes of Tim Burton and Gore Verbinski. Slathered in peaky old-age prosthetics, with a hunched, craggly demeanor and short, snarly vocal inflections, he makes for a perfectly solid, by-the-book Scrooge — with occasional moments of ripe inspiration in his line readings — without ever broaching the pained, soulful depths of, say, Alastair Sim’s gold-standard screen incarnation from 1951. It’s perhaps canny that Depp has chosen for his comeback vehicle a character who hardly demands to be loved: How much viewers are individually rooting for the star himself may determine how much they share in the film’s warm-and-fuzzy payoff. For the most part, however, “Ebenezer” is a pretty chilly affair, beginning with a needless prologue that details just how Scrooge’s cantankerous business partner Jacob Marley (Ian McKellen) became Marley’s ghost one frosty Christmas Eve; jumping ahead seven years to a mood of near-identical misery in Scrooge’s loan office, as he grudgingly grants his put-upon clerk Bob Cratchit (Rupert Grint) the next day off, lends proceedings an additional layer of déjà vu. From there we check off all the well-worn story points, as Scrooge spurns the seasonal requests of charity collectors and his earnest nephew Fred (Sam Claflin) alike, before taking to his bed so Marley can cue the phantom parade. Even if you’re shrugging through this with a been-there-done-that air, you may still be startled by the sheer freakiness of Andrea Riseborough’s appearance as the Ghost of Christmas Past: a wheezy, tulle-swaddled ghost bride with boiled-egg eyes and an eerie one-syllable-at-a-time manner of speech. She’s sufficiently unnerving, in fact, to distract us from some light embellishment of the relationship between the young Ebenezer (Arthur Conti) and former fiancée Belle (Ellie Bamber) — which, along with a supposedly upbeat but bleakly capitalistic change in Cratchit’s professional standing, represents the greatest liberty taken by Nathaniel Halpern’s generally rote script. Tramell Tillman brings some compellingly surly energy to his Ghost of Christmas Present, here an ailing, antagonistic type with spirit-skin cracking like scorched earth; Daisy Ridley draws the shortest star-casting straw as Fred’s modern-minded wife Clara. It all ticks along efficiently enough, never exactly dragging — not least because you generally know exactly what’s coming next — but never stirring the heart in the way the best “Christmas Carols” do. For viewers not invested in the Deppaissance, the rewards of “Ebenezer” are chiefly ones of atmosphere and craft — things that West, attentive to detail from the luridly scarlet, 1960s-style opening credits onwards, doesn’t skimp on. Production designer Eve Stewart is the film’s clear MVP, going heavy on the blackened timber and mildew in her dank, crooked re-creation of Dickensian London, well served by Checco Varese’s charred, coaly lensing; you can practically smell the sour rot here, everywhere from sidewalks to soft furnishings. Even when the film gives in to Yuletide cheer, it retains a frost-bitten edge, both visually and spiritually: This is one “Christmas Carol” where you sense, by the end, that the reformed Scrooge may just have held onto a cold, hard nugget of cruelty. A change of heart is for life, after all, not just for Christmas. ‘Ebenezer’ Review: Johnny Depp Scowls His Way Through a Spookily Atmospheric but Redundant ‘Christmas Carol’ Retread Reviewed at Charlotte Street Hotel screening room, London, Nov. 9, 2026. Crew: Director: Ti West. Screenplay: Nathaniel Halpern, based on the novella 'A Christmas Carol' by Charles Dickens. Camera: Checco Varese. Editors: West, David Kashevaroff. Music: Tyler Bates. articles.title: The Game Awards Adds Disney+ to Livestream Lineup
articles.full_text: × Nov 12, 2026 9:00am PT The Game Awards Adds Disney+ to Livestream Lineup By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest ‘The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’ Remake Sells 5.2 Million Copies in First Four Days on Nintendo Switch 2 1 day ago Indie Game Publisher Vendetta Unveils 2027 Release Slate, Including ‘Surfpunk,’ as It Sets New Advisory Board (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago AMC Global Media Takes $2.1 Million Hit Amid ALLBLK Streamer Sale, Content Licensing Revenue Up 42% in Q3 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Frank Micelotta/Picturegroup The Game Awards are expanding. This year, the video game industry’s biggest night will be livestreamed on Disney+ in addition to its customary platforms , including Twitch and YouTube. Airing Thursday, Dec. 10 beginning at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT out of the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, the 12th edition of the annual show will once again be hosted by the awards ceremony’s creator, Geoff Keighley. As is customary for the unorthodox awards event, the 2026 Game Awards will feature not only the unveiling of its prestigious honors across multiple categories, but also world premiere game announcements and musical performances. Related Stories UFC 333 Livestream: Here's How to Watch Volkanovski vs. Evloev Online for Free The Game Awards will stream on Disney+ in the U.S. and in select international markets. Per the streamer, “As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney’s most anticipated titles in gaming.” When The Game Awards first bowed in 2014 the ceremony drew 1.9 million livestreams. Since then, the show has exploded in popularity and continued to add more distribution platforms with last year’s event being livestreamed on Amazon’s Prime Video for the first time. The 2025 ceremony racked up 171 million global livestreams across Prime Video, YouTube, Twitch, Steam, TikTok Live, X, Kick, Facebook and Instagram Live as well as across platforms in China and JioHotstar in India. Variety has confirmed the 2026 ceremony will be livestreamed on Disney+, YouTube, Twitch, Steam, TikTok Live, X, Kick, Facebook and Instagram Live. Disney+ is joining in this year as it looks to promote the existing and upcoming roster of Disney’s licensed and developed video games as well as the streamer’s growing slate of gaming-related programming, including “Disney Twisted-Wonderland: The Animation” and the upcoming original anime series “Death Strand Isolations” on Hulu in the U.S. and Disney+ internationally. articles.title: More Than Half of Video Game Workers Laid Off Over the Past Two Years Are Still Unemployed, GDC Industry Report Finds
articles.full_text: × Nov 12, 2026 9:00am PT More Than Half of Video Game Workers Laid Off Over the Past Two Years Are Still Unemployed, GDC Industry Report Finds By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest More Than Half of Video Game Workers Laid Off Over the Past Two Years Are Still Unemployed, GDC Industry Report Finds 5 minutes ago The Game Awards Adds Disney+ to Livestream Lineup 6 minutes ago ‘The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’ Remake Sells 5.2 Million Copies in First Four Days on Nintendo Switch 2 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Adobe Stock One third of video game industry workers say they have been laid off over the past 24 months, and more than half those surveyed say they haven’t found a new job since. According to the 15th State of the Game Industry Report, released Thursday by the organizers of the GDC Festival of Gaming, 62% say they have applied for 20 or more jobs, while 25% have applied for 100 or more. Additionally, 21% of those surveyed overall are unemployed, up from 13% in last year’s report, 9% of reemployed respondents have left the game industry and 4% have started their own companies or studios. Related Stories UFC 333 Livestream: Here's How to Watch Volkanovski vs. Evloev Online for Free “One in three (34%) respondents have been laid off in the last 24 months, up from 28% in the previous report and the number rises to 39% for U.S.-based respondents,” the report says. “Of the one-in-three, 68% were laid off in the past 12 months. Nearly half (49%) said their companies have conducted some form of layoffs in the past 12 months: 68% at AAA studios, 35% at older indie studios and 14% at younger indie studios.” GDC says 54% of those laid off say they are still unemployed. This year’s State of Gaming Industry Report is being released earlier than usual, as the GDC Festival of Gaming organizers say “this edition and reports going forward have been adjusted to release near year’s end, befitting the report’s reflections on the current state of the industry and a snapshot of the year.” The report is calculated based on the responses of over 2,600 game industry professionals, which GDC says is a 12% increase from the prior year. Additional key findings in this year’s report include 40% of game industry professionals reporting they use generative AI tools as part of their job, up 4% year over year and 57% of those say they use it daily. Per the report, “Usage is highest among those working in business operations & services (71%), at mobile-only studios (70%), and those working on free-to-play games (58%). Company policy tends to vary significantly by company size, with 27% of AAA workers feeling encouraged or pressured to use generative AI, compared to only 9% of indie studio workers.” Elsewhere in the report, 10% of respondents say they are developing for the next PlayStation and 8% for Xbox’s “Project Helix.” PC (83%) remains the dominant development platform, and the figures for PlayStation 5 (47%) and Xbox Series X/S (40%) are consistent with the previous survey. articles.title: Industry Trio Launch Distinkt, AI-Powered Agency for Global Talent (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 12, 2026 9:20am PT Industry Trio Launch Distinkt, AI-Powered Agency for Global Talent (EXCLUSIVE) By Matt Donnelly Plus Icon Matt Donnelly Chief Correspondent @MattDonnelly Latest Skydance Succession: As David Ellison Sets His Team, Heads Are Rolling as Hollywood Finds Out Who’s Really in Charge 1 day ago Legendary Entertainment Hires Apollo Partner Aaron Sobel (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago A24 on Top: With Bigger Budgets, Better Box Office and Splashy IP, Is it Finally Time to Sell? 1 week ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Distinkt, a talent firm built for a large population of unrepresented creators and clients around the world, has launched out of Los Angeles and London. The agency will use AI workflows and human agents to connect actors, directors, producers, editors. photographers and digital creatives with opportunities in key markets. Distinkt is up and running with nearly 2,000 clients in 43 countries. Related Stories UFC 333 Livestream: Here's How to Watch Volkanovski vs. Evloev Online for Free The California-licensed company is founded by Robert Herman, Chris Gibbin and veteran communications executive Chris Day , who will serve as the agency’s chief spokesperson. Combined, they bring decades of experience across representation, film and commercial production and advertising. While not disclosed at launch, the new venture has been booking clients on varied projects including ad spots and scripted series and films since May. “We believe professional representation should be accessible to anyone with talent,” said CEO Herman. “We built Distinkt so that a significant part of the coordination and administration of agency work is managed by technology. That frees our agents to focus on judgment, evaluation and negotiation, and it means we can offer effective representation to far more of the world’s working creative talent.” Distinkt arrives at a moment when Hollywood’s legacy agencies are urgently trying to unlock the earnings of the creator economy, and talent face an unprecedented work slump as production continues to flee Los Angeles. The agency estimates there are more than two million actors unrepresented worldwide and more than 50 million creators who are earning some income. The global creator economy market size, currently $310 billion in 2026, is estimated to reach $1.3 trillion by 2033, according to a 2026 Grand View Research study. Distinkt will not ask clients to be represented exclusively, freeing up the user base to sign with other firms. Every Distinkt client receives four “AI teammates” on a proprietary platform to analyze work opportunities, as well as a panel of AI “specialists” in areas like legal compliance and contract analysis (trained and versed in guild standards in areas like the U.S., U.K., EU, EMEA, LATAM and Asia-Pacific markets). Human agents make all final decisions and broker deals. Distinkt is free of charge for talent clients, who can leverage the platform to browse opportunities and receive media and career analysis as agents hustle for work. Internal thinking at Distinkt is that the three-letter agencies like CAA and WME represent star talent at the height of their earning power. They’re going after untapped pools like the some 70% of SAG-AFTRA members they estimate do not have agents. “The traditional representation model has served the industry incredibly well and continues to serve many artists at the highest levels of their careers,” said Gibbin. “But the economics of that model inevitably mean that a huge amount of talent around the world remains unrepresented or underrepresented. Distinkt is designed to reach more of those people and give them a genuine advocate and a pathway into the creative economy.” Distinkt is currently privately held, but will likely seek investment in the coming months as clients surge. “We’re using technology to give agents superpowers, not to replace them,” said Herman. “Finding an opportunity is only the beginning. A great agent team has to understand what that opportunity is worth, know where there is room to push and fight for the best possible deal. We’ve built technology to help our agency do all of those things better.” ‘We Are the Shaggs,’ Documentary on the Legendary Cult Band, Coming to Theaters in 2027 Loading comments...

articles.title: Prime Video, RTP Take Portuguese Rights to ‘Gisberta,’ Leonel Vieira’s True-Crime Docuseries
articles.full_text: × Nov 12, 2026 9:26am PT Prime Video, RTP Take Portuguese Rights to ‘Gisberta,’ Leonel Vieira’s True-Crime Docuseries The four-part Portugal-Brazil co-production, directed by Vieira and Rodrigo Rebouças, marks Volf Entertainment’s first true-crime series By Emiliano de Pablos Plus Icon Emiliano de Pablos Latest South International Series Festival to Launch 2027 Investors Week, Linking Producers With Private Capital 6 days ago ‘Wednesday’ Director Paco Cabezas and Javier Ruiz Caldera, Helmer of ‘5 More Minutes,’ Talk Genre Filmmaking and Creative Risk 1 week ago ‘La Bola Negra’ Becomes Spain’s Third Biggest Spanish Hit Ever as Its Box Office Surges 8% Above Pre-Pandemic Average 1 week ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Gisberta' Courtesy of Volf Entertainment Prime Video and Portuguse public broadcaster RTP have acquired Portuguese rights to “ Gisberta – Life and Death of a Trans Woman,” a four-part true-crime docuseries from Leonel Vieira , the director-producer behind box office hit “O Pátio das Cantigas” and HBO Max thriller “O Grito.” The four 45-minute episodes are in post-production at Lisbon-based Volf Entertainment , which is producing with Brazil’s Ultravioleta . Prime Video has SVOD rights in Portugal; RTP holds free-to-air and AVOD rights. Related Stories UFC 333 Livestream: Here's How to Watch Volkanovski vs. Evloev Online for Free Brazilian filmmaker Rodrigo Rebouças (“Meninos ao Mar”) created the project and co-directs with Vieira, who also serves as showrunner. “Gisberta” revisits the 2006 murder of Gisberta Salce Júnior, a Brazilian transgender woman killed in Porto after being tortured by 14 minors from the Catholic-run Oficina de São José. The teenagers were acquitted of homicide, although some received lesser penalties or educational measures. The case sparked outrage in Portugal and Brazil. Drawing on archive footage, court records, Gisberta’s letters, interviews and dramatized reconstructions, the series traces her life from Brazil to Europe, the killing and its judicial aftermath. It also examines allegations of sexual abuse and mistreatment of children at the institution, which closed in 2010. Interviewees include relatives, friends, lawyers, journalists and people connected to the case. The project was presented at Conecta Fiction & Entertainment in Toledo in 2024, where it won two awards: Acorde music-licensing support and an invitation to Chile’s Sanfic Industria Series Lab and pitching sessions. “The Conecta awards gave the project a good boost: they were the springboard for us to pitch it to Amazon Prime,” Vieira told Variety . “With most of the financing secured between Amazon and the Portuguese cash rebate, we then approached the public broadcaster RTP, which also decided to come on board.” Vieira is also looking to French distributor About Premium Content (APC), involved in financing the project during development, for international sales. “APC is an excellent international distributor for this project, and we’re confident they will do a great job with it,” he said. Founded in 2022 and backed by an investment fund managed by Quadrantis Capital, Volf has built its slate around Vieira’s extensive film and television career. “Gisberta” marks the company’s first move into true crime. “Yes, it is Volf’s first true-crime series and, I believe, the first to be produced for a streaming platform in Portugal,” Vieira said. “We hope it does well, because we have another powerful story that we could also tell.” Volf’s credits also span the Spain-Portugal thriller “Favàritx,” released on Max and RTP. Gorilla Grodd amid Peter Safran and James Gunn ‘s exit from DC Studios . Gisondo is set to reprise his Jimmy Olsen role in an HBO series, a character he originated in 2025’s Superman film opposite David Corenswet and Rachel Brosnahan. With Skydance taking over Warner Bros. and DC Studios, the future for unreleased projects is uncertain. Former WBD CEO David Zaslav infamously shelved Batgirl as a tax write-off, and some fear the Superman spinoff series could have a similar fate. Related Stories News 'Constantine' Director Feels "More Hopeful" For Sequel Following James Gunn & Peter Safran's DC Studios Exit Executives Departing DC Co-Head James Gunn Reflects On "Trying" Four Years, Juggling Being Filmmaker & Exec While promoting his new film Focker-in-Law, Gisondo was asked about the situation, and the actor told ScreenRant , “Oh, that kind of stuff is definitely above my pay grade.” Watch on Deadline “I love James and Pete so much. I think they’ve done a great job. I am so grateful to them both,” he added. “I think there’s still a lot of questions as to what this means moving forward. I hope we still get the chance to work together in some capacity. I don’t really know. Definitely going to miss them.” Earlier this year, HBO Max gave an eight-episode, straight-to-series order to the workplace comedy titled The People v. Gorilla Grodd . Gisondo would reprise his Superman role as Jimmy Olsen, and Jimmy Tatro would play Gorilla Grodd, with the series set in a true-crime mockumentary style. Season 1 will center on DC bad guy Gorilla Grodd, who gains psychic powers and other abilities after an encounter with an alien spaceship. The cast of the spinoff series also includes Beck Bennett as Steve Lombard, Mikaela Hoover as Cat Grant, and Wendell Pierce as Perry White, along with new additions Mary Holland, Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Dan Perrault, Andrew Leeds, and Tim Baltz. articles.title: Denis Villeneuve Shares Update On James Bond Casting: “I Am Pushing The Gas”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando DC Universe Actor Frank Grillo Calls James Gunn & Peter Safran “Two Of The Most Loyal Guys” Following Their DC Studios Exit Denis Villeneuve Shares Update On James Bond Casting: “I Am Pushing The Gas” Skyler Gisondo On The Future Of ‘The People V. Gorilla Grodd’ After James Gunn’s DC Exit: “There’s A Lot Of Questions” View All November 11, 2026 8:40pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Denis Villeneuve Getty Images / MGM Many names have been tested for the new James Bond , and Denis Villeneuve has shared an update on the casting process. In a new interview posted by GQ, the Dune director was asked if the new 007 agent had been cast. “It’s—it’s in the process. In the process,” the filmmaker said, with the publication noting he said it with a smile. “ Villeneuve then added, “I am pushing the gas.” Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult were the latest names reported to have screen-tested for the iconic role, which was last played by Daniel Craig in 2021’s No Time to Die . Other actors who have reportedly tested include Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Casting Robert Pattinson & Nicholas Hoult Round Out James Bond Screen Tests News Timothée Chalamet Explains 'Dune: Part Three' Is "Its Own Thing" As He Praises Ending Pierce Brosnan, who played the role starting with 1995’s GoldenEye , recently shared his thoughts on the names circulating for the role. “All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum, Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong,” Brosnan told Vanity Fair . “They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men.” Brosnan said he was “eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history,” later adding, “Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.” Following GoldenEye , Brosnan would reprise his role in 1997’s Tomorrow Never Dies , 1999’s The World Is Not Enough , and 2002’s Die Another Day . The process for casting the next James Bond has been ongoing. In March of this year, Deadline reported that Nina Gold had closed a deal to become the casting director for the next James Bond film. Gold’s credits include HBO’s Game of Thrones , the Netflix series The Crown , and five films in the Star Wars franchise. Following the merger of Warner Bros. and Paramount, Skydance parted ways with Gunn and Safran, who were still in the initial stages of rebuilding the DC Universe. Amid the executive shakeup , Grillo posted a video with a message to the departing duo. “I feel like now that the dust has settled a bit, and every jerk off with an Instagram handle has an opinion — I just wanted to publicly thank two of the finest men that I’ve met in this business, in Peter Safran and James Gunn,” Grillo said on Instagram. “Two of the most loyal guys.
