articles.title: Jacob Elordi To Star In Adaptation Of ‘The Executioner’s Song’ From United Artists
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin Aaron And Adam Nee Board Live-Action ‘Catan’ Movie At Netflix Departing DC Co-Head James Gunn Reflects On “Trying” Four Years, Juggling Being Filmmaker & Exec WME Sets Expanded Leadership Group View All November 10, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jacob Elordi; 'The Executioner's Song' Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Scott Stuber’s United Artists has acquired the rights to the 1982 motion picture The Executioner’s Song and set Oscar nominee Jacob Elordi to star. Based on Norman Mailer’s landmark 1979 Pulitzer-winning true-life novel, Elordi will play convicted murderer Gary Gilmore and also will serve as a producer on the film adaptation. Related Stories Books 7 Jacob Elordi Movies & TV Shows And Where To Stream Them Casting Scarlett Johansson To Star In Ari Aster’s ‘Eddington’ Follow-Up ‘Scapegoat’ At A24 UA’s Stuber and Nick Nesbitt will produce alongside Elordi, his manager Matt Vioral and producer Sherry Marsh. Filmmaker Lawrence Schiller — who directed the original 1982 film and conducted the extensive interviews with Gilmore, his family and key figures that formed the foundation of Mailer’s book — will serve as an executive producer. Mailer’s masterpiece chronicles the true story of Gilmore, a cold-blooded murderer who, after being tried and convicted for killing two men in Utah, insisted on being executed for his crimes. Fighting attorneys for a legal system intent on keeping him alive long after it sentenced him to death, Gilmore became a national media sensation and the first person executed in the United States following a four-year de facto moratorium on capital punishment. Told with impressive authority and compassion, The Executioner’s Song journeys deep into the heart of American violence, media frenzy and loneliness. Watch on Deadline

articles.title: Sundance Institute Names Allison Graff-Weisner As Chief Development Officer
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Skydance Bosses Throw Shade On Warner Bros Film Slate; Q4 Profit Will Take $200M Hit ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is A Box Office Hero With $32M Live-Action Foreign-Language Opening Record, Best Ever For Gkids – Sunday AM Update ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is King Of The Global Weekend Box Office With $63M, Towers Over ‘Ramayana’s $55M+ WW Opening View All November 10, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Allison Graff-Weisner Courtesy The Sundance Institute has appointed Allison Graff-Weisner as its new Chief Development Officer (CDO). A 25 year vet in the nonprofit, education, and cultural spaces, Graff-Weisner will spearhead a capital raising campaign associated with the organization’s upcoming transition to Boulder, Colorado. Graff-Weisner will serve on the executive leadership team, where she’ll oversee expanding the Institute’s national and global donor base. She will report directly to CEO David Linde. “Allison is exactly the kind of transformative leader the Sundance Institute needs at this pivotal moment in our history,” said Linde. “Her proven track record of scaling organizations, combined with her deep experience in the cultural and educational sectors, makes her uniquely qualified to lead our development efforts. As we prepare for our transition to Boulder and look to expand our support for independent artists globally, Allison’s ability to build values-aligned partnerships will be instrumental to our sustainable growth and future success.” Related Stories Executives Sundance Institute Appoints Tracy Brady As Chief Marketing, Brand And Communications Officer News Sundance Institute Names 2026 Episodic Intensive Fellows Graff-Weisner joins the Sundance Institute from Otis College of Art and Design, where she has served as VP of Institutional Advancement. There, she has led advancement across all areas of giving, significantly growing scholarships for a highly diverse student body and establishing strategic industry and philanthropic partnerships. Prior to Otis College, she was the Deputy Director of External Affairs at the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, where she was involved in the museum’s launch across contributed revenue, membership, special events, and corporate engagement. Watch on Deadline “I am incredibly honored to join the Sundance Institute, an organization whose commitment to artistic risk-taking and independent voices has profoundly shaped global culture,” said Graff-Weisner. “Robert Redford’s founding principles of supporting artists outside traditional systems of power resonate deeply with me. I look forward to working with David, the Board of Trustees, and the incredibly talented Institute team to build an innovative fundraising model that ensures bold, original storytelling continues to thrive for generations to come.” Earlier in her career, Graff-Weisner spent over 18 years at City Year in various executive capacities, ultimately serving as the Chief Development and Engagement Officer. During her tenure, she spearheaded private sector fundraising efforts, managing a $20 million national budget, and co-designed a $225 million campaign in support of City Year’s 30th Anniversary. She also served as the Founding Executive Director of City Year Los Angeles, growing the site to an annual budget of $12 million and raising $50 million cumulatively. articles.title: Millie Bobby Brown To Star In, Produce Netflix Comedy ‘Non-Refundable’; Jack Innanen Also Set
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt ‘Being Heumann’ Composer Francesco Le Metre Tapped Into Judy Heumann’s Drive And A ’70s Punk Rock Spirit – Sound & Screen Film Alaskan Crime Procedural ‘Wild Life’ From Juliet Lashinsky-Revene In Development At NBC Untitled Signs Nnamdi Asomugha & His iAm21 Entertainment Banner View All November 10, 2026 8:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Millie Bobby Brown and Jack Innanen Michael Schwartz/Jack Innanen EXCLUSIVE: After wrapping up Stranger Things and capping off an Enola Holmes trilogy, and with a David Harbour co-starring spy comedy upcoming, Millie Bobby Brown has found her next project with Netflix : a comedy titled Non-Refundable that she’ll produce and headline opposite Jack Innanen , the breakout star of FX’s Adults . With Emmy-nominated SNL alum Paul Briganti aboard to direct, Non-Refundable is billed as a high-concept commercial comedy centered on Nate (Innanen) and Dani (Brown), an ex-couple who are still on the hook for their wedding venue despite breaking up. This leads them to travel to Mexico out of spite, where they try showing each other up with new dates. Related Stories News 'The Perfect Lie' Actor Matthijs Van De Sande Bakhuyzen To Lead AFM-Bound Arctic Thriller 'The Art Of Survival' News 'Swapped' Composer Siddhartha Khosla Used Music From Every Continent For Netflix's Animated Adventure - Sound & Screen Film Pic is based on a spec by David Bernstein. Bobby Brown and Jake Bongiovi will produce for PCMA ( Damsel , Enola Holmes ), alongside Andrew Swett and Aaron Ryder for Embrace Entertainment (Netflix’s Office Romance ) and Will Speck and Josh Gordon for Speck + Gordon Inc. Executive producers are Bobby Brown for PCMA, Eric Fineman and David Kern. Watch on Deadline Sources said Non-Refundable reflects Netflix’s interest in revitalizing a version of the rom-com you see less of these days — a film like Forgetting Sarah Marshall that had big laughs and emotional stakes in equal measure. Execs were on the lookout for fresh takes and knew they’d found the one in new writer Bernstein’s spec when the team started quoting its one-liners and referencing its set pieces around the office. At Netflix, Brown has become synonymous with megahit genre fare like Stranger Things , Damsel and the Enola Holmes films. But execs thought of her after seeing her performance in Just Picture It , an upcoming Netflix rom-com where she stars opposite The Fabelmans’ Gabriel LaBelle, which speaks to underappreciated comedic chops. Innanen wowed Netflix execs with his turn as Paul Baker in Adults , an FX hang-out sitcom compared to a Gen Z version of Friends or New Girl . Meanwhile, Briganti was the choice to direct given his work at SNL spanning six seasons, where he demonstrated an eye for surprising, off-the-wall humor, as well as a knack for getting the best out of talent. During his time there as segment director across Digital Shorts and more, select highlights included working on breakout Please Don’t Destroy videos, including “Three Sad Virgins” (feat. Taylor Swift), and directing Brad Pitt to an Emmy nomination via a Covid-era cold open segment where he played Dr. Anthony Fauci. Wrapping up her five seasons with Stranger Things on New Year’s Eve 2025, Bobby Brown is fresh off Enola Holmes 3 , which nabbed over 20M views in its first five days alone. Upcoming, she’s set to reunite with her Stranger Things dad David Harbour on a father-daughter espionage thriller for Netflix from Adolescence ‘s Jack Thorne & A24. She is repped by WME and Hansen, Jacobson. Seen over the summer in the second season of the critically acclaimed Adults — which seemed to have broadened awareness around the series — Innanen has also previously been seen starring opposite Dan Levy in Netflix’s crime comedy Big Mistakes from Levy and Rachel Sennott. The Canadian actor is repped by UTA, Range Media Partners and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. Briganti reteamed with Please Don’t Destroy post-SNL on the Peacock comedy Please Don’t Destroy: The Legend of Foggy Mountain . He previously intersected with Innanen as the director of multiple episodes of Adults and began his career making videos for CollegeHumor, where he went on to become site director. He garnered early attention for the Hugo Award-nominated satirical video “Fuck Me, Ray Bradbury,” starring Crazy Ex-Girlfriend’s Rachel Bloom, before going on to work on series including The Late Late Show with James Corden , Adam Ruins Everything , Crazy Ex-Girlfriend , Chad and At Home with Amy Sedaris , to name a few. He is repped by WME, Mosaic and Ginsburg Daniels. Speck and Gordon, the filmmakers behind Blades of Glory and Office Christmas Party , are repped by 3 Arts and CAA. articles.title: CAA Wants to Create an AI-Generated Celebrity Advertising Machine
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All November 9, 2026 1:10pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source CAA chief Bryan Lourd Taylor Hill/FilmMagic Celebrity ads are getting an AI makeover. Powerhouse ad agency Ogilvy announced on Monday that it’s partnering with CAA to launch ECHO, an AI platform that allows marketers to whip up AI-generated ads featuring celebrities. The collaboration opens the door for talent to take on more endorsement deals without having to spend much more time shooting commercials while safeguarding how their digital replicas are used. The platform utilizes what CAA calls its “vault,” a database that captures, stores and licenses the digital likeness, voice and intellectual property of clients who opt in. With ECHO, brands will be able to create a portfolio of media-ready assets off of a short shoot, potentially reducing costs by as much as 75 percent and vastly reducing turnaround time, the companies said. Talent must sign off on every ad, with automated compliance engines checking AI-generated materials against contracts and brand safety guidelines. The major talent agency did not disclose which A-listers opted in to the effort. “We built The CAA Vault to ensure that talent owns, controls, and can safely monetize their digital likeness on their own terms and only with their consent,” said CAA head of strategic development Alex Shannon. “By connecting The CAA Vault to Ogilvy’s ECHO platform, CAA is giving many of the world’s leading brands a secure, consent-first activation layer, delivering full visibility and protection for talent and high-craft, verified creative at the speed of culture for brands.” ECHO’s workflow can be integrated directly into standard post-production tools. A traditional asset shoot of eight to 10 assets can be expanded into roughly 30 to 50 for the creation of ads taking advantage of buzzy TikTok trends, CAA and Oglivy said. All consumer-facing products will carry a visible watermark that reads, “[Talent Name] Approved | Recreated with AI”. In a statement, Ogilvy CEO Laurent Ezekiel said the tool solves the “fundamental tension between speed, scale and trust” in the AI era. “We are giving our clients unprecedented competitive advantage – allowing them to lead culture in real time with total trust and uncompromised craft.” The tools represents the interest in monetizing the commercial use of celebrities’ digital likenesses and, perhaps, changing views among consumers regarding the deployment of AI. Brands have largely been hesitant to wade into those waters due to pushback against deepfakes and unauthorized AI use but acceptance appears to be growing. Last month, the likeness of 1930s movie star Greta Garbo was revived in an ad from Swedish ball-bearings market SKF. ECHO is among the first to build an infrastructure around celebrities who opt into the usage of their digital replicas in ads. “We are witnessing the ‘NIL moment’ between advertising and entertainment,” said Ogilvy chief innovation officer Carol Reed. “Instead of fearing AI or using it to produce cheap volume, building ECHO in partnership with CAA proves that technology can protect artists while setting storytellers free. Our global research confirms that consumers don’t want AI to sideline the artist; they want explicit proof that the talent is in control.” THR

articles.title: Skydance Details Cost Savings and Plans HBO Max-Paramount+ Bundle in First Post-Deal Earnings Report
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All November 9, 2026 1:17pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Skydance's Ynon Kreiz and David Ellison at a press event on Oct. 6. Nate Jensen courtesy of Skydance Skydance , in its first earnings report after completing its megadeal for Warner Bros. Discovery, outlined where it expects to drive synergies and cost savings and teased a bundle of HBO Max and Paramount + for early 2027, as well as an investor day in the first half of next year. The company reported Q3 earnings Monday afternoon, with revenue of $7 billion, net earnings of $73 million and adjusted EBITDA of $1 billion, all skewed a bit by the fact that the WBD deal did not close until after the quarter ended. As a result, none of WBD’s results are included in the report, which was authored by CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. Instead, it is the deal and what it means for Skydance’s future that will dominate the earnings conversation, with the looming bundle surely top of mind for investors and consumers, ahead of an inevitable merger of the services in the future. The move is similar to Disney’s approach with Hulu, where those two services remain distinct, but also have become increasingly intertwined. As for where the cost savings will be found? Skydance says it expects at least $2.2 billion from corporate overhead, real estate and facilities as they rationalize office space and eliminate duplicitous corporate roles; $1 billion from marketing by streamlining spend and utilizing their own platforms for more promotional work; $1.2 billion from technology as they unify tech stacks and products; $1.4 billion from procurement and vendor management. The company also says that it sees an opportunity for savings in content, though it reiterated that it still expects to spend $30 billion on content each year. “With the reach of our combined platforms across streaming, broadcast and cable, each title can work harder for us, and as one company we can make smarter choices about how we distribute and monetize our slate,” the executives wrote. THR

articles.title: Jessica Lange on Bringing ‘Long Day’s Journey Into Night’ Back to the Big Screen, Returning to ‘American Horror Story’ and Retirement Rumors
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All November 9, 2026 2:31pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jessica Lange ANGELA WEISS/AFP/Getty Images “You age out of a lot of parts, that’s just the nature of things,” Jessica Lange , the legendary stage and screen actress, said during a recent recording of The Hollywood Reporter ’s Awards Chatter podcast at the Virginia Film Festival , where she was being honored with the fest’s Visionary Award . The 77-year-old, who also brought to the fest her latest film, a big-screen adaptation of Long Day’s Journey Into Night , was discussing the possibility of retirement and continued, “I wouldn’t mind ending on Mary Tyrone [the protagonist of Long Day’s Journey , a morphine addict in 1912 Connecticut], let me tell you. I would embrace that, because there’s no greater part I’m ever going to play.” Related Stories TV 'American Horror Story' Finale: Paul Anthony Kelly on the Season 13 Ending: "I Was Flabbergasted" TV 'American Horror Story' Lead Joey Pollari on That Wild Jessica Lange Reveal and Up-in-the-Air Fates Headed Into Finale One of only 24 people ever and one of only 10 people still living who have won the “triple crown of acting,” as in, at least one Oscar, Emmy and Tony (she has won two, three and one, respectively), Lange has been a screen actress for 50 years. She made her film debut after being “discovered,” while working part-time as a model, and cast by producer Dino De Laurentiis in his large-scale remake of King Kong (1976). She received a huge publicity build-up, even appearing on the cover of TIME magazine. But the film proved to be such a giant flop that, she explains during this conversation, it shattered her self-confidence and almost destroyed her career. Jessica Lange in King Kong Photofest Slowly but surely, though, she rose from the ashes, first with a supporting turn in Bob Fosse’s All That Jazz (1979), then with unforgettable lead performances in films such as Bob Rafelson’s The Postman Always Rings Twice (1981), Graeme Clifford’s Frances and Sydney Pollack’s Tootsie (both 1982, and both of which brought her Oscar nominations, the latter resulting in her first win), Richard Pearce’s Country (1984), Karel Reisz’s Sweet Dreams (1985), Bruce Beresford’s Crimes of the Heart (1986), Costa-Gavras’s Music Box (1989), Martin Scorsese’s Cape Fear (1991) and Tony Richardson’s Blue Sky (1994, for which she won her second Oscar). Jessica Lange in Frances Photofest Then, as she became a mother and entered her forties, a mid-career malaise set in. For a number of years, she worked far less frequently, more often in supporting roles, and rarely in projects that excited her. That changed with the HBO limited series Grey Gardens (2009), for which she won an Emmy, and a result of her association with producer Ryan Murphy , which began soon after and encompassed four seasons of the anthology series American Horror Story (2011-2015), two of which brought her Emmys, and a single season of the limited series Feud: Bette and Joan (2017). Jessica Lange, with Drew Barrymore, in Grey Gardens Photofest But no part has enchanted her more than Tyrone in Long Day’s Journey Into Night , which she first played on the London stage in 2000 (becoming the first American actress to receive an Olivier Award nomination) and then reprised on Broadway in 2016 (winning a Tony). She spent much of the past decade trying to bring it to the big screen — a previous film version, starring Katharine Hepburn, was released in 1962 — and encountered almost as much drama as is featured in the play itself. Financing came together and fell apart numerous times, including even after the cast and crew were on set in Ireland. But ultimately, she got it across the finish line in collaboration with writer David Lindsay-Abaire and director Jonathan Kent, and she is immensely proud of the finished product. Now, as Long Day’s Journey Into Night plays at film festivals and in select theaters courtesy of a tiny distributor, Lange is hustling to make sure people know about it and see it. And having also recently returned to American Horror Story for its 13th season, which rolled out between Sept. 24 and Oct. 29, she finds herself back in contention for both an Oscar and an Emmy. For now, at least, Jessica Lange isn’t going anywhere. Jessica Lange, with Ed Harris, in the new film adaptation of Long Day’s Journey Into Night Courtesy Virginia Film Festival THR

articles.title: David Ellison Is Very Bullish On AI’s Creative Potential
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Erik Hayden Plus Icon Erik Hayden Executive Editor, Business Erik_Hayden Follow Sign Up View All November 9, 2026 3:59pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Skydance CEO David Ellison Gabe Ginsberg/Getty Images In his first earnings call as CEO at the helm of both Paramount and Warner Bros., David Ellison talked up his merged Hollywood empire as a tech-forward enterprise — and part of that tightrope walk included an embrace of AI while also dismissing “AI slop.” It’s a two-step that’s not necessarily an easy one. The technology is widely seen as a harbinger of doom for Hollywood’s traditional workflows (i.e. building sets, shooting with real background extras, going on-location, etc) while also being increasingly adapted and integrated into the business (see: Ben Affleck’s VFX firm, which has helped Netflix use AI on 300-plus titles so far, while supposedly preserving the things that make Hollywood, Hollywood). Ellison told analysts that he expects AI to help his company’s studios make content faster and cheaper, describing the technology as the biggest breakthrough in the industry since CGI effects went mainstream. Skydance plans to spend $30 billion annually across its content portfolio — that includes everything from prestige TV HBO projects to CBS procedurals and MTV reality shows as well as NFL sports rights and features at Warners and Paramount. “I don’t think it can be discounted how fast this technology is moving,” Ellison said after table-setting by saying that “in a world of AI slop we think there will always be a premium for truly hand-crafted storytelling.” Ellison has a unique lens into the issue as heir to his father Larry Ellison’s AI-powered Oracle tech fortune, which is a key facet of his effort to rebrand legacy Hollywood studios as a tech-centric venture. (To that point, the enterprise cloud apps of Oracle Fusion got a call out in the earnings call as well when talking about consolidating back office functions.) The CEO also views franchise IP — he described his empire as having 40 $1 billion franchises — as a moat protecting against the onslaught of AI content, delivering more premium experiences to his 203 million-plus subscribers at a soon-to-be merged Paramount+ and HBO Max. He then launched into an anecdote about a franchise that his Skydance Media has rebooted multiple times over the past two decades. “AI really has the potential to be the biggest creative unlock in modern history,” Ellison bullishly said. “The last time we saw anything close to this was really the advent of CGI and digital composites in the early ’90s. That technology gave birth to amazing stories like Jurassic Park and Terminator 2 . It’s hard to imagine that AI is not going to have a more significant impact than that. I personally believe that’s going to be an incredible unlock on creativity.” “If you go back in time, speaking of Terminator which everyone knows is one of my favorites, if you go back to ’83, when James Cameron made that movie it was made for $4 million,” Ellison noted. “If you wanted to make that picture today shot-for-shot, it’d be $60 million-$70 million.” The CEO added: “There’s not a lot of bets that get taken like that across our industry. And we think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budgets more digestible to take that amount of risk.” Cameron, who directed the original Arnold Schwarzenegger feature as well as its acclaimed sequel, has been one of the CEO’s biggest backers (and an early “Team Ellison” advocate as Skydance was fighting Netflix for its Warner Bros. prize). The Avatar helmer has himself been on the vanguard of the technology, with his Lightstorm banner just buying an AI-driven 3D post-production firm in September. Skydance is also looking to bake in an AI productivity narrative as it looks to find some $6 billion in cost-synergies from merging Paramount and Warner Bros. In addition to finding redundancies in corporate overhead, real estate and facilities as well as consolidating back office and corporate functions, those efficiencies include scaling AI-workflows across the combined company. That includes merging Paramount+ and HBO Max within a year, which Ellison described as an “ambitious target” that is “possible because of the latest tools in artificial intelligence.” THR

articles.title: Dave Chappelle’s Charlie Kirk Joke at MSG Draws Rebuke From Erika Kirk
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All November 9, 2026 4:08pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dave Chappelle Netflix Turning Point USA CEO Erika Kirk has condemned those who laugh at political violence after Dave Chappelle made a joke referencing the killing of her husband, Charlie Kirk , during a show in New York on Saturday. Chappelle was performing for a sold-out crowd at Madison Square Garden when he delivered the bit. In it, he talked about the pressure on famous people to say and do the right things before bringing up the murder of Kirk, who was fatally shot during a speaking event at Utah Valley University in September 2025. Erika Kirk, who succeeded her husband as head of TPUSA, posted about the incident on X on Sunday. Related Stories News Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan Apologize for Laughing at "Insensitive Joke" About Charlie Kirk on 'I've Had It' Podcast News Dave Chappelle Announces Fall 2026 Arena Tour To see leftist podcasters, comedians, and commentators laugh about political assassination as though it’s entertainment and the destruction of a human life is a punchline, is beyond disgusting. My husband, Charlie Kirk, was killed in an act of political violence, something our… — Erika Kirk (@MrsErikaKirk) November 8, 2026 “My husband, Charlie Kirk, was killed in an act of political violence, something our two children and I will live with every day for the rest of our lives,” she wrote. “A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together. “You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard. Political violence must never be something this country tolerates, excuses, or celebrates,” she concluded. Chappelle framed the remark around free speech, pointing to the chill on public commentary that spread across media and entertainment after the shooting. “I feel fucked up saying this,” Chappelle said. “It’s scary being a public speaker. And I mean, look, ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered — and I shouldn’t say this publicly — but, I feel better. I know I shouldn’t say that, but it’s just a feeling.” In the weeks after Kirk’s death, several journalists and TV personalities were suspended or fired over comments about the killing. They included then-MSNBC political analyst Matthew Dowd, who was let go after suggesting on air that the conservative activist and Second Amendment advocate had helped create the political climate that led to his assassination. The backlash culminated in ABC pulling Jimmy Kimmel Live! off the air for nearly a week over a monologue in which the host addressed the reaction to Kirk’s killing. Chappelle, who has not responded publicly to Erika Kirk’s statement, has long courted controversy with his comedy, particularly around identity politics. His material about transgender people has been a flashpoint since 2021, when his Netflix special The Closer set off internal protests at the streamer, including an employee walkout. In an interview with NPR’s Newsmakers earlier this year, the comedian said some Republicans had “weaponized” transgender jokes like his and campaigned on them. The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Chappelle’s representative for comment on the backlash and Erika Kirk’s statement but did not hear back Monday. Separately, on Saturday, Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan of the I’ve Had It podcast apologized for laughing at a joke about Kirk’s death on a prior episode. On Thursday’s episode, the hosts read posts from X about the midterms, including one that said, “We’re digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again.” At least two of the podcast’s sponsors, Cash App and Chewy , then said on X that they were dropping their sponsorship. View this post on Instagram In an Instagram post, the hosts of the progressive podcast said laughing at the joke was wrong and announced a donation to Everytown for Gun Safety. “It was an insensitive joke, and we should not have laughed. We regret it, and we apologize,” they wrote. “Whatever our political differences, there is nothing funny about gun violence. We’ve long supported common-sense gun safety reform. To that end, we’ve made a donation to Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention organization in America.” On Monday, Utah District Court Judge Tony Graf scheduled Tyler Robinson, the 23-year-old man accused of assassinating Kirk, to stand trial in the summer of 2028. A statement about the delay of the trial from the Kirk family called the decision “deeply disappointing.” THR

articles.title: Ariana Grande on First Time Meeting Ben Stiller: “Directing Me in an Orgy Scene in ‘Zoolander 2’”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All November 9, 2026 4:59pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro, Ariana Grande and Jimmy Fallon on 'The Tonight Show.' Todd Owyoung/NBC Ariana Grande won’t be forgetting the first time she met Ben Stiller anytime soon. During a recent episode of The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , Grande, Stiller and Robert De Niro made a joint appearance to chat about their new film Focker-in-Law , which releases on Nov. 25. At one point, host Jimmy Fallon asked the Grammy-winning singer about the first time she met Stiller, to which she replied, “I met Ben in a very different way,” drawing laughter from the audience. Related Stories TV Alex Warren to Host Kids' Choice Awards, Airing on CBS for the First Time; Taylor Swift Leads Nominees General News Pete Davidson Slams Body Shaming of Ex-Fiancée Ariana Grande “He was directing me in an orgy scene in Zoolander 2 with a hippo and Susan Sarandon,” she revealed. In the 2016 action-comedy, directed by Stiller, Derek (Stiller) and Hansel (Owen Wilson) are lured into the fashion world again, in Rome, where they find themselves the target of a sinister conspiracy. Grande makes a cameo as part of Hansel’s eccentric romantic circle, which he calls his “orgy” group. “So right off the bat, we had a comfortability,” Grande added, as Stiller quipped that they had an instant connection due to the unusual encounter. “It sounds like two truths and a lie, but it’s my reality,” the Wicked star said. The pair have now reunited in Focker-in-Law , which sees Greg (Stiller) and Pam Focker’s (Teri Polo) son Henry (Skyler Gisondo) get wrapped up in family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman, Olivia Jones (Grande), who appears to be his complete mismatch. The “Petal” singer also told Fallon that their first scene together in Focker-in-Law was another interesting experience. “We were thrust into rehearsing the Heimlich scene, where I give you [Stiller] the Heimlich,” Grande said. “So I thought maybe we’ll sit in [director] John [Hamburg’s] office with a script and talk a little, get to know each other a little more and work on the scenes and talk about Greg and Olivia.” “But no. We met the stunts team, and they were amazing. And they were like, ‘All right, Ben, bend over. Ariana, you’ll get behind and just put your arms around him.’ And I was like, ‘Oh, perfect. Yeah,'” she added with a laugh. “My mom was like, ‘How was your first day, honey?’ I was like, ‘Well, I gave Ben Stiller the Heimlich for a few hours.’ It was crazy.” Grande’s appearance on The Tonight Show marked her return to the public eye after stepping back from the spotlight once her Eternal Sunshine Tour wrapped in September. The Hollywood Reporter learned in August that the singer would be “taking a step back from visibility” for a “much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny.” Grande has faced a wave of online commentary surrounding her health and body over the last year. THR

It only took 25 years but David Schwimmer has finally reunited with Ross’ iconic red sweater from Friends . Once he’s finally reunited with the garment, another guy approaches to say, “Hey, that’s my dream sweater.” Schwimmer once again takes off running. articles.title: ‘Summer School, 2001,’ the First Czech-Vietnamese Feature, Is Coming to America via Cinemas, Amazon (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All November 9, 2026 6:31pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Summer School, 2001' Courtesy of KVIFF In 2025, Summer School, 2001 , the debut feature of writer-director Dužan Duong and dubbed the “first Czech-Vietnamese feature film,” made a splash at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival and beyond. Now, it is coming to America, courtesy of Reel Citrus, an L.A.-based distributor of Asian and diaspora films. The company will open Summer School, 2001 in a limited U.S. theatrical release on Dec. 11 at Cinemark cinemas, hitting screens before Dune 3 and Avengers: Doomsday opens a week later. The film will then stream on Amazon from Dec. 18 before rolling out globally. Related Stories Movies Claes Bang, Valerie Pachner Drama 'I Is Another' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM Business The Hollywood Reporter Launches Turkish Edition “At a time when immigration and belonging are front-page news in both the U.S. and Europe, the release brings two diasporas into the same theater,” said Reel Citrus. Summer School, 2001 follows 17-year-old Kien, who returns to his family’s market stall in Cheb, a small town on the Czech border, after spending 10 years in Vietnam. It becomes a chaotic summer, during which the family must try to become whole again. After its Karlovy Vary world premiere, the movie drew more than 20,000 moviegoers during its run in Czech cinemas. At the Czech Lion Awards, the Czech national film honors, Summer School, 2001 won the best screenplay award for Duong, Jan Smutný and Lukáš Kokeš, along with the best supporting actor honor for Dũng Nguyễn, the first Vietnamese actor to win a Czech Lion. The Czech Film Critics’ Awards named it the best screenplay and the Discovery of the Year. ‘Summer School, 2001’ Courtesy of KVIFF At Viet Film Fest, the largest U.S. festival for the Vietnamese diaspora, the film won the Bronze Drum (Trống Đồng) Award for the best feature film, the best actor honor for Tô Tiến Tài and the Audience Choice Award for best feature. Reel Citrus says it chose the theaters to target the communities that the film, which is in Vietnamese and Czech with English subtitles, speaks to. Most of the cinemas are in areas with large Vietnamese American populations, including Southern California, where it plays in Huntington Beach next to Little Saigon, the Bay Area, Houston, Dallas, Seattle, Las Vegas and the Washington, D.C. area. The rest of the theaters are in Chicago, Cleveland, Pittsburgh and Central Texas, “home to strong Czech, Polish and other Central and Eastern European communities,” the company explains. Vietnamese American families and Czech and Polish moviegoers came out in droves for a screening of Summer School, 2001 at the Avalon Theatre in Washington, D.C. last March. Co-presented with the Embassy of the Czech Republic, it served as an early test for Reel Citrus, which says it releases films “in person, one community at a time.” Reel Citrus acquired North American rights across all media, along with worldwide streaming rights, to Summer School, 2001 from AZN kru. “ Summer School, 2001 was an eye-opening film for us,” said Brittany Tran, founder & managing director of Reel Citrus. “Many of us grew up knowing the Vietnamese American story, but we knew far less about the Vietnamese families who built their lives in the Czech Republic and across Europe. Our diaspora is global, and when Vietnamese communities in the U.S. see the communities in Europe, we realize how much we share.” Dužan Duong, courtesy of Karlovy Vary International Film Festival She added: “We know we’re opening the week before Dune and Avengers , so we’re competing with the gods. But audiences who rarely see their own stories on the big screen are exactly who this release is for.” And Duong, who talked to THR about his creative vision for Summer School, 2001 and his other creative work, shared: “Vietnamese families have been part of Czech life for decades, but our stories rarely reach the screen. I made this film for my community in Cheb and for every family that has had to find its way back to each other. Seeing it open in American theaters, in front of Vietnamese and Czech audiences together, means more than I can say.” Check out a trailer for Summer School, 2001 here. THR

articles.title: Steve Buscemi Reveals Which Show He Refuses to Appear on: “I Don’t Care How Much You Paid Me”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All November 9, 2026 6:39pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Steve Buscemi Theo Wargo/Getty Images If you were hoping to see Steve Buscemi take on the hot wings challenge, don’t bet on it. During a recent appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , host Josh Horowitz asked the veteran actor, who’s promoting his new films Wild Horse Nine and Klara and the Sun , about things he dislikes. “I’m confused why people like spicy food, why they like their mouths hot,” Buscemi replied. So First We Feast’s Hot Ones , hosted by Sean Evans , likely won’t ever be a stop on the actor’s press tours. Related Stories Movies 'Klara and the Sun' Review: Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams Should Have Insisted on a Factory Reset for Taika Waititi's Cloying, Clumsy AI Fable Movies John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell Buddy Up for London Film Festival Premiere of 'Wild Horse Nine' “Sam Rockwell told me that he and Parker Posey did Hot Ones — that’s something I would never do. I don’t care how much you paid me, how much they said, ‘But it would really support the film,’ no. It not only makes me confused, it makes me angry,” he added with a laugh. “You’ll never get me, Hot Ones !” In recent years, Hot Ones , which launched in 2015, has become a routine stop for celebrities as they’re making the rounds to promote their latest projects. The YouTube talk show, created by Evans and Christopher Schonberger, sees the host interviewing guests as they eat a platter of ten wings, each coated in a progressively hotter hot sauce. Dozens of celebrities have taken on the challenge, including Jennifer Lawrence, Paul Rudd, Billie Eilish, Post Malone, Conan O’Brien, Charlize Theron, Pedro Pascal and Shaquille O’Neal, among others. But seeing many stars end in tears or yell in pain (“I feel like I’m gonna die,” Lawrence said during her episode) likely wasn’t a selling point for Buscemi. Earlier this year, Evans revealed some of his favorite Hot Ones episodes during a chat with Matt Belloni. “I always say if you’re new to the show, check out the Conan O’Brien episode or the Gordon Ramsay episode. Jennifer Lawrence is another one or Maya Rudolph. Paul Rudd is a classic. Charlize Theron,” he said at the time. “I always say to start with those. If you like those episodes, you’ll probably like the show. If you don’t like those episodes, stop there. There’s nothing for you.” THR

articles.title: Olivia Cooke Says ‘House of the Dragon’ Fandom Led Her to Step Away From Social Media: ‘There’s a Lot of Ugliness,’ ‘Misogyny’ and ‘Racism’
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 4:29pm PT Olivia Cooke Says ‘House of the Dragon’ Fandom Led Her to Step Away From Social Media: ‘There’s a Lot of Ugliness,’ ‘Misogyny’ and ‘Racism’ By Payton Turkeltaub Plus Icon Payton Turkeltaub Latest Julia Garner Says Madonna Biopic Status Changes ‘Every Hour,’ But She’d ‘Love for the Movie to Get Made’ 2 hours ago Olivia Cooke Says ‘House of the Dragon’ Fandom Led Her to Step Away From Social Media: ‘There’s a Lot of Ugliness,’ ‘Misogyny’ and ‘Racism’ 4 hours ago Nicolas Cage Calls ‘Spider-Noir’ Season 1 ‘Perfect’ and Says He Felt Relieved When It Was Canceled: ‘You Never Wanna Get Stuck Repeating a Character’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Olivia Cooke , who plays the controversial Queen Alicent Hightower in HBO’s “Game of Thrones” prequel “ House of the Dragon ,” recently told GQ that she stepped away from social media ahead of the show’s third season because of the fandom’s “ugliness.” “I think some of those interpretations just catch fire, and they become something that bears no resemblance to what was shown on the screen at the time,” said Cooke on the subject of the fanbases’ theories and opinions (which include observations about Cooke herself as well as her relationship with the show’s directors). The uber-passionate fanbase was, in part, why she went offline and deactivated her Instagram ahead of Season 3 dropping in June, she revealed. “There’s a lot of ugliness to that fandom as well. It’s steeped in misogyny. There’s a lot of racism. I try to let it take up minimal mental real estate.” Related Stories Netflix Sets Release Date for Rob Lowe Documentary 'The Outsider’ Netflix Stock Deflates to Two-Year Low. What Will It Take to Revive Revenue Growth? While viewers of the prequel series are well-acquainted with the taboo at this point, Season 3 saw Cooke’s Hightower in a number of contentious storylines, including sharing a kiss with her son that results in an incestuous daydream scene later on. Cooke’s “House of the Dragon” co-star Milly Alcock was also tasked with navigating a toxic subset of the show’s fandom when a group of viewers decided to pit the younger actors against their adult counterparts. Co-creator Ryan Condal described the comparison as “horrible”: “It’s horrible for all these young performers that did a great thing, and kind of did an impossible thing… Everybody should have just been celebrating the success and reception of that show. And people should find something else to do with their time, frankly.” On her social media break, Cooke noted that it got to a place where she felt it was “not nourishing.” “I think the celebri-fied nature of being an actor has now snowballed into this monster. And I just think we need to get off this train and realize that we make these TV shows and films, yes, for escapism, but also because it’s artful and it’s creative and it’s not for followers or for a brand deal or to get free shit. Even though that is nice sometimes.” As for her relationship with director Clare Kilner, Cooke told the magazine that Kilner proves “you don’t have to stomp around the set and exert testosterone. You can just handle each department with kindness and care.” “House of the Dragon” first aired on HBO in 2022. The prequel series earned three Golden Globe nominations and one win for best television series, drama. It’s been nominated for 14 Emmys and won 2: outstanding fantasy/sci-fi costumes in 2023 and outstanding period or fantasy/sci-fi makeup (non-prosthetic) in 2025. articles.title: Tina Knowles’ WACO Theater Center Sets Grand Reopening Celebration for South L.A.’s Historic Vision Theatre
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 4:41pm PT Tina Knowles’ WACO Theater Center Sets Grand Reopening Celebration for South L.A.’s Historic Vision Theatre By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest Tina Knowles’ WACO Theater Center Sets Grand Reopening Celebration for South L.A.’s Historic Vision Theatre 4 hours ago James Bond Shocker: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult Late Contenders for 007 After Auditioning for Denis Villeneuve 3 days ago Bradley Cooper and Danny McBride’s ‘G.I. Joe’ Movie Set for 2028; Paramount Shifts New ‘Paranormal Activity’ to Halloween 2027 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source WACO Theater Center The Vision Theatre Performing Arts Center in South L.A. is reopening following 15 years of extensive renovations and a $40 million investment. To celebrate the historic theater’s return, WACO Theater Center, led by founder & artistic director Tina Knowles and executive director Shay Wafer, is hosting a grand reopening celebration in Leimert Park. “The reopening represents more than the return of a historic theater,” a release announcing the news notes. “It is a celebration of Black creativity, cultural preservation, artistic excellence and the enduring legacy of Leimert Park, a neighborhood that continues to serve as the heartbeat of Black arts and culture in Los Angeles for generations.” Related Stories Keira Knightley and 'Black Doves' Creator Joe Barton on Why Helen Should Have Been the One to Kill [SPOILER], That Oner and Hopes for Season 3 CAA's Roeg Sutherland Says It's Too Soon to Predict Fallout From Netflix Firings, Thinks Recent Mergers Represent 'Opportunity' for Industry The three-day homecoming celebration, presented by Wells Fargo, will take place Nov. 13 through Nov. 15 and feature live performances, music, entertainment and community festivities. Key events include a family-friendly, “Proud Family”-themed block party and screening of the Disney+ holiday special “A Proud Family Wizmas”; a conversation with the cast of Netflix’s “A Different World”; and an intimate evening with Club 20/20 and “House Guest with Scott Evans” sponsored by Cécred and curated by Knowles. The celebration concludes on Sunday with a live concert launching the WACO at the Vision Music Series, with a powerhouse live band led by Steve Mackey’s Taco Tuesdays, The Sessions L.A. and The Crockpock. “Leimert Park has always been a place where Black culture, creativity and community come together. To be part of bringing this beautiful theater back to life is incredibly meaningful,” Knowles said in a statement announcing the news. WACO Theater Center will serve as co-operator and co-manager of the Vision Theatre Performing Arts Center in partnership with the City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs. “The Vision Theatre represents so much history, but more importantly, it represents possibility. We want young people to walk through these doors and see a future for themselves in the arts,” Knowles continued. “We want artists to have a place where their stories are celebrated, and we want this community to know that this theater belongs to them. This is about honoring the legacy of those who came before us while creating something extraordinary for generations to come.” Originally built in 1931, the Vision Theatre stands as one of South Los Angeles’ most iconic architectural and cultural landmarks. For nearly a century, the theater’s Art Deco façade has defined the Leimert Park Village skyline. In 1990, award-winning actress Marla Gibbs purchased the historic venue, renaming it the Vision Theatre, with a dream of creating a thriving home for Black arts, culture and community. An initial renovation of the property was completed in 2011, and the current project, led by the City of Los Angeles, began in 2015. The office of Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass helped launch the partnership between WACO Theater Center and the Department of Cultural Affairs, laying the foundation for the theater’s long-term activation. Now complete, the Vision Theatre will serve as a destination for live theater, music, dance, multidisciplinary performances, arts education and community-centered cultural programming. “The renovation of the Vision Theatre unites historic preservation with state-of-the-art venue upgrades to create a world-class cultural venue that all Angelenos can be proud of,” said Daniel Tarica, general manager of the City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs. (The upgraded theater now boasts a 729-seat auditorium, a newly constructed mezzanine and balcony, expanded stage and backstage facilities and cutting-edge audio, visual and broadcast technology.) “This landmark in the heart of the creative hub of Leimert Park will be a main stage that uplifts local talent, serves as a resource for the community and will be a cultural destination for all.” Since its founding in 2016, WACO Theater Center has championed the transformative power of the arts, with a particular eye toward celebrating the rich experiences and cultural heritage of the African diaspora. Now housed at the Vision Theatre, WACO will significantly expand its reach by presenting theatrical productions, live music, dance, visual arts, multidisciplinary performances and educational programming. “The reopening of the Vision Theatre is an investment in the future of South Los Angeles and the artists who make this community extraordinary,” said Wafer, WACO Theater Center’s executive director. “Our vision is to create a thriving cultural institution that is active year-round, where artists can develop and present new work, young people can access meaningful arts education and audiences can experience world-class programming right here in Leimert Park. This is about building a sustainable home for creativity, opportunity and community connection.” All activities are free and open to the public with an RSVP. Ticketing, registration and additional program details will be available on WACO Theater Center’s website . Event sponsors include Wells Fargo, Cécred and Walt Disney Entertainment, with KBLA Talk 1580 as the media partner. The celebration is presented in collaboration with the City of Los Angeles DCA, WACO Theater Center’s municipal co-management partner for the Vision Theatre Performing Arts Center, with additional support and participation from PRG, Dance Theatre of Harlem, Pan Afrikan Peoples Arkestra, Blackhouse Radio, and the Leimert Park Village Merchant Cohort. articles.title: French Judo Legend Teddy Riner Announces 2027 Presidential Bid, Drawing Praise From Emmanuel Macron
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 5:28pm PT French Judo Legend Teddy Riner Announces 2027 Presidential Bid, Drawing Praise From Emmanuel Macron By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest How the American French Film Festival Is Bringing French Cinema to 3,000 Los Angeles High School Students With Packed Screenings of ‘In Waves’ 3 hours ago French Judo Legend Teddy Riner Announces 2027 Presidential Bid, Drawing Praise From Emmanuel Macron 3 hours ago Prime Video, Scanbox Entertainment Team on New ‘Hamilton’ Films and TV Series Based on Bestselling Swedish Spy Franchise (EXCLUSIVE) 8 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Credit: Banijay French judo superstar Teddy Riner , a five-time Olympic gold medalist and multiple world champion, has announced that he is running for president of France in 2027 in a fiery speech posted on social media. The athlete, who has never held political office but is one of France’s most recognizable and popular sporting figures, portrayed himself as a political outsider determined to stand for ordinary French citizens which he feels have been let down. Related Stories Netflix Stock Deflates to Two-Year Low. What Will It Take to Revive Revenue Growth? Netflix Names Mattel Executive Roberto Stanichi as VP of Consumer Products and Experiences Riner’s announcement comes at a particularly turbulent moment in France, just five months before a presidential election that has exposed deep divisions across the political spectrum. The far-right party Rassemblement National is dominating the polls by a wide margin, with Marine Le Pen drawing between 33% and 37% of first-round voting intentions in recent surveys, roughly twice the support of her closest rivals. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who leads the radical-left party La France Insoumise, has been gaining ground and is polling at around 17% to 19%, while the political center remains fragmented, with no candidate emerging to succeed Emmanuel Macron . The country has also been rocked by weeks of mass protests over the soaring cost of living and conditions in schools which escalated into violent riots. “My name is Teddy Riner, and today I’m telling you straight to your face: I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential election,” he said while facing the camera and sitting at a desk in a presidential-style setting while bookshelves and a tricolor French flag in the background. La résignation n'est pas une option. Face aux difficultés de notre pays, l'heure est venue de prendre ses responsabilités.⁰⁰Je suis candidat à l'élection présidentielle de 2027. ⁰⁰ #TeddyRiner2027 #Présidentielle2027 #LaFrancequonveut pic.twitter.com/nM7rTfyTrH — Teddy Riner (@teddyriner) November 9, 2026 “I know what people are going to say about me: ‘He’s crazy,’ ‘He’s not part of the establishment,’ ‘He doesn’t know the rules,’ ‘He’s never been involved in politics.’ But ask yourselves this question: What is really crazy today?” Riner went on to paint a bleak picture of France, citing growing public debt, economic hardship and a breakdown of law and order. “Is it crazy to refuse to watch France collapse under the weight of its debt, a little more every day? To see a country so rich pretend that it is poor?” he asked. Riner criticized what he described as an unfair system that places an excessive burden on working people. “Is it crazy to reject the hypocrisy of a system where those who get up early, work hard and follow the rules have no choice but to pay for everyone else?” Macron reacted warmly to Riner’s announcement in an interview with the French broadcaster France 5 welcoming his decision to enter politics and praising his sense of duty. “Teddy Riner is a tremendous athlete who makes our country proud,” Macron said. “I supported him in competitions and as an athlete, and he is a committed man.” Macron, who cannot seek a third consecutive presidential term in 2027, applauded the prospect of citizens from outside the political establishment taking part in the national debate. “Political life, the life of the nation, does not belong to professionals,” Macron said, alluding to his own path, as he came into politics a decade ago after working in investment banking at Rothschild. “The life of the nation belongs to women and men who want to give their time, who are ready to commit themselves and fight difficult battles to make our country better. I am very happy that someone like Teddy Riner, who is a great champion, has decided to take part in this presidential debate and bring his convictions, his ideas and his talent,“ Macron continued. articles.title: How the American French Film Festival Is Bringing French Cinema to 3,000 Los Angeles High School Students With Packed Screenings of ‘In Waves’
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 6:11pm PT How the American French Film Festival Is Bringing French Cinema to 3,000 Los Angeles High School Students With Packed Screenings of ‘In Waves’ By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest How the American French Film Festival Is Bringing French Cinema to 3,000 Los Angeles High School Students With Packed Screenings of ‘In Waves’ 2 hours ago French Judo Legend Teddy Riner Announces 2027 Presidential Bid, Drawing Praise From Emmanuel Macron 3 hours ago Prime Video, Scanbox Entertainment Team on New ‘Hamilton’ Films and TV Series Based on Bestselling Swedish Spy Franchise (EXCLUSIVE) 8 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Philip Guerette The American French Film Festival , which celebrated its 30th anniversary this year, has been on a journey to cultivate a new generation of French movie lovers for two decades with its educational program for Los Angeles high school students. This milestone edition brought around 3,000 students to the DGA theater for five packed screenings of “In Waves,” Phuong Mai Nguyen’s heart-wrenching animated feature which was bought Netflix at Cannes. Related Stories 'KPop Demon Hunters,' 'Squid Game' Stars Fete Netflix's Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases 'Tantara,' 'All of Us Are Dead' Season 2 'Stranger Things' Prequel Spinoff 'Other Worlds' Ordered to Series at Netflix Adapted from AJ Dungo’s graphic novel at set in Southern California, “In Waves” is a love story between a shy teenage boy and the girl who teaches him how to surf and how to live, before she succumbs to cancer. The screenings, which drew applause and tears throughout, also gave students the opportunity to engage in the post-screening Q&A with the film’s producer, Priscilla Bertin , and screenwriter Fanny Burdino. Philip Guerette Spearheaded by Anouchka Van Riel , the festival deputy director, the program brings together more than 60 schools over five days, with roughly half coming from the public school system and half from private institutions. It also reaches beyond French-language classes to students studying performing arts and other creative disciplines. In an interview with Variety , Van Riel discussed the importance of the programme to allow younger audiences to discover international cinema at a time when arthouse moviegoers are aging and foreign-language films face growing challenges in U.S. theaters. She also talked about the program’s rapid growth, why subtitles are no longer the barrier they once were, and the powerful response to “In Waves” which Netflix is positioning in the Awards race. How many students and schools participate in the program? We have more than 60 schools participating over five days, so that’s more than 12 schools a day. We organize five screenings of the same film, each with around 600 students. That’s approximately 3,000 students every year. I’ve built a database of around 300 schools, and we start reaching out in May. Within a week of sending the first email, half the seats — around 1,500 — are already booked. Then I spend the summer filling the remaining places. There’s enormous demand. We also make a point of having a mix of public and private schools, roughly 50/50. That’s very important to us. For public schools, transportation can be a challenge. Some have to apply for grants just to pay for the buses. There’s an entire economy around organizing these trips, and a lot depends on the teachers. Philip Guerette How does the festival work with teachers to prepare students for the screenings? We work with the American Association of Teachers of French, which prepares two educational guides, one in French and one in English. The French-language guide is around 100 pages long. It’s incredibly detailed and allows teachers to explore the film from multiple perspectives, including its themes and cinematic language. The guides are designed to help students study the film before or after the screening. And we don’t just work with French-language classes. Around half of the participating classes are English-speaking. Many Los Angeles high schools have performing arts programs, and those students come because they’re interested in cinema and want to meet the filmmakers. The majority of these kids have never attended a film screening followed by a Q&A. That’s something we want to change. That’s surprising in Los Angeles, where the film industry is everywhere. It’s extraordinary. I’m a member of the Producers Guild, and I receive invitations to screenings and conversations with filmmakers almost every day. There are incredible events happening constantly, but these kids don’t have access to them. Of course, if their parents work in the industry, that’s different. But otherwise, most students aren’t exposed to that world. I grew up in a small town in Alsace, and I remember my French teacher taking us to the movies all the time when I was in middle school. Some of those screenings even had Q&As. There’s a tradition of that in France that doesn’t really exist here in the same way. We used to organize masterclasses for university students, including at USC, but we realized it was difficult to attract them. They’re already surrounded by so many opportunities on campus. With high school students, we can work directly through the teachers. That’s how we’ve developed this program. Is the goal ultimately to cultivate a younger audience for French cinema? Absolutely. It’s about renewing the audience. A couple of years ago, we screened “The Marching Band,” and when the film was eventually released theatrically in the U.S., I was invited to moderate a Q&A. I loved the film, so I was very happy to do it. But the theater was only half full, and I don’t think there was a single person under 65. That’s the problem. Foreign-language films have traditionally been considered niche in the U.S. Streaming platforms have helped change that perception somewhat, but we still need to familiarize younger audiences with these films. That’s why this program is so important. Are subtitles still an obstacle for younger American audiences? Not nearly as much as people think. We’ve conducted surveys with students after the screenings, and more than 80% say subtitles aren’t a barrier to watching foreign-language films. It’s not a completely scientific study, but it gives us a good indication of how attitudes are changing. Between streaming platforms, social media and series like “Squid Game,” young people have become accustomed to watching subtitled content. Sometimes there’s still a little hesitation before the screening. But once they’re sitting in the theater, they realize it’s easy. I really don’t think subtitles are the problem for this generation anymore. Distribution is a major part of the problem. That’s why streaming platforms have become so important for the circulation of foreign-language films. But there’s also the question of exposure. If young people aren’t given opportunities to discover these films, they’re not necessarily going to seek them out themselves. In Waves Courtesy of Netflix This year’s selection was “In Waves.” What made it particularly suitable for the program? There’s a wonderful connection between this film and the festival. The producer, Priscilla Bertin, had already come to the festival two years ago with “Wild Diamond,” and at the time she was in post-production on “In Waves.” We became familiar with the project very early, and it made complete sense for us to bring it back this year. What’s interesting is that the film is based on an American graphic novel that was discovered by a French producer in a secondhand bookstore in France and developed into a movie. We explain that background to the students before the screenings, including why it’s considered a French film and the response has been extraordinary. The screenings were packed, and the students seemed particularly moved by the film. What was the atmosphere like? It was very striking. At the first screening, I went straight into introducing the filmmakers for the Q&A, and I realized something wasn’t right because the students were still processing what they’d just watched. Usually, when a film ends, the students immediately line up to ask questions. But with “In Waves,” it took time. Every day, there was this moment of silence. The film had affected them so deeply that they needed a little time before they could speak. There’s something cathartic about sitting in a dark theater with other people, crying together and sharing the same emotions. You feel safe because everyone is experiencing that grief together. I think young people have fewer opportunities to experience cinema that way now. That’s what made these screenings so special. articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 6:37pm PT LISTEN: ‘Roland Martin Unfiltered’ Rides Midterm Elections Momentum After Historic Vote Variety's 'Strictly Business' podcast features conversations with industry leaders about the business of media and entertainment By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest LISTEN: ‘Roland Martin Unfiltered’ Rides Midterm Elections Momentum After Historic Vote 2 hours ago WME Streamlines Motion Picture Lit and Talent Departments, Promotes Will Ward to Lead Fashion 11 hours ago Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music 5 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source On today’s episode of Variety ‘s “Strictly Business” podcast, digital news entrepreneur Roland Martin discusses the growth of his “ Roland Martin Unfiltered ” program and how it gained momentum during the buildup to this last week’s historic midterm elections. Martin’s daily political news and commentary roundtable program went on a barnstorming tour over the three weeks leading up to Election Day on Nov. 3. The show targeted key areas in the South and Southeast where the protection of voting rights, affordability, the relentless GOP attack on DEI and other issues had already fired up voters. Related Stories Netflix Orders YA Drama 'Prep' Based on Curtis Sittenfeld Novel From Nicole Taylor 'Love Is Blind' Star Rob Feeley Breaks His Silence on Michaella, the Beekeeper and Why He Nearly Skipped the Reunion “Twelve cities in fifteen days. It was Little Rock, Arkansas. Fairfax, Virginia. Lansing, Michigan. We came home for a day. Then it was like Indianapolis, Atlanta and then we were in Jackson, Mississippi, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Miami Gardens, West Palm Beach, Tallahassee, Florida. Back to Atlanta and Lithonia, Georgia again. Baton Rouge. then. Arlington, Texas. Dallas, Texas. Houston, Texas. Fort Bend County. And then came home two days before the election,” Martin says. “It was absolutely crazy. the first week I had our 35-foot bus on the road. And then that second week I had that and the Sprinter [van] on the road. And we were flying into a city, doing the show, go to the hotel, put all of our suitcases in the Sprinter and then would just pack overnight clothes. They would drive to the next city overnight. We would then fly to the next city. Uber to the hotel, check in. Go set up. Do the show. Repeat, rinse, repeat. I was a show host, a producer, a travel agent, a logistical coordinator. It was crazy.” Martin, an alumnus of CNN, TV One and Tom Joyner’s radio program, says the tour reflected the freedom and flexibility offered by working in digital media. And it all has the potential to reach viewers in a different way than a traditional news program. “What’s so different from linear is that you’re really touching viewers. You’re really communicating with them. I’m not spending three, four, five, six minutes on a segment. Sometimes I’m doing twenty, thirty minutes doing deep dives,” Martin says. “I’m not trying to do a mainstream show. I am not trying to replicate MS NOW, CNN, ABC, NBC, CBS, Fox News, or any of those people. We break all the rules. We’re not trying to be slick. I’ll grab my DJI action camera and I’m shooting stuff and it’s totally unconventional. But we’re serving the audience and communicating them in a different way.” MS NOW Has 2026 Midterm Elections Coverage: Here’s How to Watch Election Night Results Live Online Free Cleveland Cavaliers on DAZN: Here’s How to Watch 2026-2027 Regular Season Games Live Online Here’s How to Watch WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Live Online Nike Releases New Jordan Spiz’ike Low ‘Jam Central’ Sneakers: Here’s Where To Shop a Pair Online Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian M’billi on DAZN: Here’s How to Watch the WBC Title Boxing Match Live Online ‘Vote for America 2026:’ Here’s How to Watch Newsmax’s Midterm Election Special Online for Free Loading comments...

articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 6:53pm PT Julia Garner Says Madonna Biopic Status Changes ‘Every Hour,’ But She’d ‘Love for the Movie to Get Made’ By Payton Turkeltaub Plus Icon Payton Turkeltaub Latest Julia Garner Says Madonna Biopic Status Changes ‘Every Hour,’ But She’d ‘Love for the Movie to Get Made’ 2 hours ago Olivia Cooke Says ‘House of the Dragon’ Fandom Led Her to Step Away From Social Media: ‘There’s a Lot of Ugliness,’ ‘Misogyny’ and ‘Racism’ 4 hours ago Nicolas Cage Calls ‘Spider-Noir’ Season 1 ‘Perfect’ and Says He Felt Relieved When It Was Canceled: ‘You Never Wanna Get Stuck Repeating a Character’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source FilmMagic Julia Garner has given an ambiguous update on the long-delayed Madonna biopic, which has made little progress since its 2020 announcement. During a recent interview with CBS , the actress was asked about the film’s status, to which she responded: “I don’t know. Every hour it changes, in a way.” “It’s not up to me. I would love for the movie to get made, obviously. But I also feel whatever happens, I made a great friend,” she continued. “I love Madonna. I think she’s incredible.” Related Stories Keira Knightley and 'Black Doves' Creator Joe Barton on Why Helen Should Have Been the One to Kill [SPOILER], That Oner and Hopes for Season 3 'Blue Eye Samurai' Sets Season 2 Release Date at Netflix The last update Garner gave on the biopic was in July 2025, when she guested on the “SmartLess” podcast and told hosts Will Arnett, Sean Hayes and Jason Bateman that she was still set to star as the seven-time Grammy winner in the film. “That’s supposed to still happen,” Garner said, adding that she’s “such a fan of Madonna” and that she “grew up listening” to her music. She also assured fans that “anything that’s great…takes a long time,” referring to the delayed film. Back in 2023, Variety reported that the film had been scrapped ahead of Madonna’s world tour and would remain on pause indefinitely at Universal Pictures. Variety also exclusively reported that Garner landed the part in 2022 after a grueling process that included a full-on singing-and-dancing boot camp. Florence Pugh, Alexa Demie, Odessa Young and Bebe Rexha were also reported to have been in consideration for the role. The pop icon herself was set to direct, while two different scripts were reportedly penned by Diablo Cody (their writing sessions were widely disseminated on social media) and Cressida Wilson. Garner stars in Netflix’s “ The Altrusists ,” which tells the story of Sam Bankman-Fried (Anthony Boyle) and Caroline Ellison (Garner), “two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye — before they were accused of stealing $8 billion.” The eight-episode limited series hits the streamer on Nov. 19. articles.title: ‘Ramayana’ Makes History as First Indian Film to Top U.K., Ireland Box Office as ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Debuts in Third
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 7:25pm PT ‘Ramayana’ Makes History as First Indian Film to Top U.K., Ireland Box Office as ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Debuts in Third By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Ramayana’ Makes History as First Indian Film to Top U.K., Ireland Box Office as ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Debuts in Third 1 hour ago Bong Joon Ho on Restoring ‘The Host’ and Why It Still Resonates 20 Years On: ‘We Are Repeating Our Mistakes’ 5 hours ago China Box Office: ‘Traces of Justice’ Reclaims Top Spot as Local Debuts ‘Embers’ and ‘The Coffin Swap’ Arrive 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Everett Collection Sony’s animated mythological adventure “ Ramayana : Rise of a Legend” made history by becoming the first Indian feature ever to debut atop the U.K. and Ireland box office, collecting £2.1 million ($2.8 million) to lead a crowded slate of new releases and push Anime Ltd.’s “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” into third place. The previous box office ceiling for Indian cinema in the territory was second place, held jointly by S.S. Rajamouli’s “RRR” in 2022, Shah Rukh Khan starrers “Pathaan” and “Jawan” in 2023 and Ranveer Singh’s “Dhurandhar: The Revenge” earlier this year. Related Stories 'Stranger Things' Prequel Spinoff 'Other Worlds' Ordered to Series at Netflix Netflix Hires Apple Alum Steve Wilson to Lead Podcast Content Acquisition Disney’s “ Wild Horse Nine ” secured second position in its opening frame, taking $1.9 million. Anime Ltd.’s “Godzilla Minus Zero” claimed third place, generating $1.8 million. Black Bear’s period comedy “ Wicker ,” which led the chart in the previous session, moved to fourth place in its sophomore frame, collecting $1.5 million to push its running total to $5.7 million. Universal’s concert presentation “George Michael: The Faith Tour” debuted in fifth position, generating $1.3 million. A24’s “Primetime,” directed by Lance Oppenheim and starring Robert Pattinson, followed in sixth position in its second weekend, adding $1.1 million to elevate its total to $4.6 million. Lionsgate U.K.’s comedy horror “Ghosts: The Possession of Button House” took seventh spot in its third frame, collecting $997,064 to raise its cumulative gross to $10.3 million. Warner Bros.’ DC horror thriller “Clayface” landed in eighth place in its third session, generating $911,261 to take its running cume to $8.1 million. Entertainment Film Distributors’ biographical drama “I Play Rocky,” starring Anthony Ippolito, opened in ninth place with $810,781. Trafalgar Releasing’s event presentation of “Stray Kids World Tour ‘Run It’ Live Viewing” rounded out the top 10 in its debut weekend with $793,559. Just outside the top 10, Altitude’s Cannes winner “La Bola Negra” debuted in No. with 721,301. Meanwhile, Mubi’s “Fatherland,” directed by Paweł Pawlikowski and starring Sandra Hüller, maintained its foothold in its third weekend, ranking at No. 24 with $74,401 to lift its cumulative total to $997,741.
