articles.title: ‘an open field’ Is a Deeply Personal Story of Loss, Grief and Compassion (Exclusive Netflix Trailer)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All November 6, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'an open field' Courtesy of Netflix In March 2019, a Boeing 737 MAX crashed in Ethiopia just six minutes after taking off from the airport in the country’s capital, Addis Ababa. It had 157 people on board, and all of them died. Among them was Max Thabiso Edkins . His older brother Teboho Edkins decided to make a film about the experience of grief and mourning that his family and the local community went through. The result is the very personal 38-minute short film an open field , directed by Edkins and produced by his father, Don Edkins, and Carine Chichkowsky. The film is now going global, hitting Netflix on Dec. 1, about a year after its world premiere at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ) 2025, where it won the best short documentary award. Related Stories Business Netflix Taps Mattel's Roberto Stanichi to Lead Consumer Products and Experiences Business Dark Slope to Open New Virtual Production Stage in Vancouver (Exclusive) The title of the movie becomes clear when you watch it. In an open field, the filmmaker finds out that dozens of nearby villagers immediately converged on the crash site to help. Some even stood vigil for a month to protect and preserve the area. Years later, they continue to mourn alongside family members who visit the site, including Edkins and his father, also making the film a story about collective grief and compassion. “Boeing’s widely criticized response to the crash stands in sharp contrast to the community’s enduring compassion,” highlights a synopsis. “Both a personal essay on loss and an exploration of the potential healing power of collective mourning, Edkins’s film is a quiet testament to humanity – moments of warmth, resolve, grief, fear, patience, and simple acts of kindness.” Indeed, the film feels like a cinematic attempt to connect with a late brother and son’s spirit. In that sense, an open field is a family film. And it may be set in a far-away place for many viewers, but it transcends borders, given that the plane’s passengers came from more than 30 countries and that anyone who has lost a loved one has faced the burden of that loss. ‘an open field’ Courtesy of Netflix an open field is a South Africa-France-Germany production by Day Zero Film and Video Productions in South Africa, Day Zero Films UG in Germany and Survivance in France. The cinematographer is Jide Akinleminu, the editor is Anne Fabini. The film, shot in color and black-and-white, features dialogue in both English and Amharic. “This is a delicate and personal work and about something fundamental to being human,” says director Teboho Edkins. “I hope that the film can find its way to as many people as possible, and that something in it might resonate with them. Having Netflix bring the film to its global audiences is very meaningful to me, and I’m grateful for their support as it makes its way out into the world.” THR can now exclusively premiere a trailer for an open field ahead of its Netflix debut. THR

articles.title: Romanian First-Ever Country of Focus at AFM, ‘Fjord’ Director Cristian Mungiu to Attend
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All November 6, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fjord, Sebastian Stan, 2026. Neon/Courtesy Everett Collection In a surprise move, the American Film Market , traditional home to mainstream cinema in all its schlocky glory, is going upscale arthouse. At next week’s AFM — Nov. 10-15 at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles — there will be a focus on Romanian cinema. AFM has named Romania its first-ever country of focus. National film industry group Creative Romanian Filmmakers (CRFM) will bring over a delegation of filmmakers, producers and production companies to present their latest movies and to meet with industry execs to discuss shooting in Romanian and international co-production opportunities. Related Stories Movies 'an open field' Is a Deeply Personal Story of Loss, Grief and Compassion (Exclusive Netflix Trailer) Movies 'Elsinore' to Close Camerimage Festival “Romania has been part of the AFM community for many years, and we’re proud to recognize its contributions to global cinema as our first-ever Country of Focus,” said Jackie Brenneman, President & CEO of the Independent Film & Television Alliance (IFTA), which produces the AFM. “Together with Creative Romanian Filmmakers, we look forward to showcasing the country’s exceptional talent and opportunities for international collaboration.” “Since 2016, Creative Romanian Filmmakers has brought Romanian producers to the world’s most important film markets and festivals, and the American Film Market has always been a key stop on that journey,” added CRFM managing director Mihai Lupu. “Being named Country of Focus this year is a milestone for our entire industry – an invitation to buyers, sales agents and producers to discover Romanian stories, talent and locations, and to build lasting partnerships with us.” The delegation will include Cristian Mungiu , attending with his Palme d’Or winning drama Fjord , starring Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve . Fjord is Romania’s official entry for the Oscar in the best international feature category and is seen as a shoo-in for the Academy long-list, being announced Dec. 15. “This year, a Romanian film was awarded at every major festival,” noted Mungiu. “I believe Romanian films have real potential in international markets – not only at festivals, but with a wider audience. In this sense, Fjord ’s awards-season campaign and its North American theatrical release look promising.” Mungiu also put in a pitch for his country as a shooting location, noting that “not only is the Romanian cash rebate working again, we have also started a conversation with the Romanian authorities about providing upfront cash-flow financing for the rebate, and we hope to see concrete results as early as 2027.” At AFM, Mungiu will take part in a panel, “Beyond the New Wave: Romania as Your Next Production Partner,” on Saturday, Nov. 14, from 4:00–5:00 PM on the Constellation Stage at the Fairmont Century Plaza. Mungiu will be joined by Valentin Savu, General Manager, Romanian Office for Film and Investments in Culture, Alma Bacula, Head of Production & Partner, Icon Films, and leading producers Iuliana Tarnovetchi, Gabriel Popescu and Ionuț Ionescu to discuss opportunities for filming in Romania, and partnering with local producers to accessing the country’s filming incentives. AFM will showcase four Romanian films with screenings at the AMC Century City 15: Comatogen by Igor Cobileanski, Gone Guy by Andrei Dascalescu, Grounded by Ligia Ciornei and The Circle by Valeriu Andriuta. Romanian companies participating in the event at AFM include Augmented Films, Bullsrecords, Idea Film, Nomad Films Global, Profesional Film Partners, Quantum Media Creative, Frame Film, Mavish Ask, Negrea Visuals, Sýmbolon and Tarnovski Marketing Consultancy. At the Fairmont Century Plaza, Romanian companies will have dedicated exhibition space in suites 1005 and 1037 for meetings. THR

articles.title: How John Summit Is Turning Arenas Into the “World’s Biggest Nightclub” for CTRL ESCAPE Tour
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content John Summit during his CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour. Gautthiierr “I’m always about doing things first and really breaking the mold and breaking barriers, especially in the DJ world,” John Summit says. That mentality spawned the 32-year-old DJ’s idea to embark on his first-ever arena tour. For any DJ, organizing a global arena tour is a tall order, as their home away from home is typically nightclubs and music festivals. While Summit has become a fixture in those spaces in recent years, he also saw an opportunity for something bigger. Following one-off shows at New York’s Madison Square Garden and Los Angeles’ Kia Forum, Summit admits he didn’t even want to flirt with the idea of a full arena run initially because there are a limited number of DJs capable of pulling off a tour on a similar scale to massive mainstream pop acts. Related Stories Music Singer Jackson Wang Signs With WME (Exclusive) Music With 'The Girl of Your Dreams,' Ashe Finds Her Sweet Spot: "I'm A Really Solid Version of Myself" Sure, a handful of DJs such as The Chainsmokers and Kaskade have launched their own versions of arena and stadium tours. Still, Summit considers his multi-country CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour a particularly unique and ambitious opportunity, as he’s the sole headliner on each date, and it’s strictly a DJ set rather than mixed in with pop performances. John Summit during his CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour. Julian Bajsel “There’s been DJs who’ve played arenas, but to this scale and this level, this is a very ambitious tour and it’s not something I technically have to do because obviously the clubs and festivals and everything has been working so well,” Summit tells The Hollywood Reporter . “But because I did those one-off shows and they worked out super well, I knew that I had the confidence to actually take the show on the road.” Luckily for Summit, the tour’s visual concept came easily as his sophomore album CTRL ESCAPE already had a theme centered around breaking out of the corporate 9-to-5 “matrix.” The notion was personal for Summit, as he left his job as a CPA in 2019 to follow his passion for music — and it clearly worked out. “The fans can relate as well too because you’re going to that show; they probably all worked their 9-to-5 during the day to then be able to afford the ticket at night,” Summit says. “So it’s going to be that show is their way of breaking out of that.” It was important for Summit to build a world that his fans could truly escape into, so he leaned on his creative director, Alex Alvga, who also worked on his sophomore album and other shows, to channel the corporate-to-rave transformation that originated in his “LIGHTS GO OUT” music video. John Summit during his CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour. Jamal Eid “We used the music video to drive the whole rollout of the album, and from there we just built the whole narrative,” Alvga tells THR . “Then for the arenas, we just wanted to keep building on that.” The attention was in the detail, from Summit’s mixing table looking like an old computer monitor to the speakers having a ’90s computer casing around them, to backup dancers wearing corporate attire dancing in cubicle-like structures. “We have a lot of stuff that plays into that same aesthetic that we’ve been playing up until now, because of course the best thing as a fan is just when everything feels cohesive,” Alvga says. But the team didn’t slack on lighting, automation, lasers, pyro and practical effects either, a necessity for what is essentially a massive dance party. Summit delivers several immersive moments throughout the show, from dropping 1,200 employee performance review papers over the crowd to a fired/hired bit with audience members who aren’t dancing enough. All these elements are key components for the narrative Summit aims to tell during his four-act performance. “I can’t really think of any DJs who really do an actual story throughout a set,” the DJ says. Alvga says it “starts with a control, then we go into the escape section and then we go into the Experts Only section,” which is act three and will feature Summit in the crowd at the much more intimate B stage. “By that moment in the show, the narrative already explains the workers have escaped. Now it’s time to party and have fun,” the creative director says of the fourth and final act, titled “release.” With the visuals, design and story set, the last — and arguably the most important — piece of the puzzle is the music. John Summit during his CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour. Julian Bajsel When it comes to his other shows, Summit often finalizes the set hours before taking the stage and “it’s not even an official set list because I get on stage and I switch it up,” he says. However, with a tour of this scale, there’s much more at play behind the scenes. “Honestly, the biggest challenge for me is getting the music done ahead of time and then not going full improv with it,” Summit says. Thankfully for his team, this DJ found his perfect mix. “I know how I’m going to start, I know I’m going to finish [and] I know the big moments in the middle,” he says, while also weaving in moments “to get a little spicy with it and creative.” As Summit sets out on this new chapter, he’s excited to learn and grow with each show. As for his fans, he hopes that by the end of the night, “the phones are down, you’re dancing, you’re in the moment.” John Summit during his CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour. Gautthiierr Fans will also need to be locked in so they don’t miss potential surprises, special guests and an outfit change or two. “I’m starting in my [accountant] suit and I guarantee you I won’t be finishing it in the suit,” Summit quips. However, despite having a group of backup dancers, don’t expect Summit to debut a whole dance routine. “I’ll do my typical fist bump, don’t worry,” he says with a laugh. “But no breakdancing or anything. I’m not going to go full Tate McRae or anything.” That’s the fans’ responsibility — lest they get fired by the boss on the first day now. He says, “It’s kind of cool to turn an arena into the world’s biggest nightclub for a night.” THR

articles.title: Meet the British Foodie Demystifying the Michelin Guide’s Secrets
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All November 6, 2026 8:28am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jesse Burgess in 'Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars.' Apple TV Jesse Burgess is a chef whisperer. If you’re interested in food and have a penchant for scrolling, you may already know this from one of his many vertical clips. The 35-year-old English foodie, host and co-founder of media platform TopJaw, forged a reputation for charming London’s culinary luminaries into opening up not just about their work but the restaurants, bars and Sunday roasts that they adore. And, just as informative, the spots that they think are overrated. Interviewing chef after chef after chef for going on 10 years, Burgess has honed another rather novel skill. He can talk about fine dining without a ring of pretension. “This guy properly reads the fucking room,” says Gordon Ramsay , several times a TopJaw guest. “Jesse understands what he does and doesn’t know. He talks from a viewer’s perspective and lets you in on the secret, what’s going on … where a critic would have the tendency to slide toward being an asshole.” Related Stories TV Apple TV Renews 'Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars' for Season 3 TV Toni Collette to Lead Apple TV Dramedy 'Lenni' An asshole was the last thing Apple TV needed when casting its ambitious culinary series, Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars . The word Michelin already evokes thoughts of white tablecloths, comical price tags, foams, fermentations and microgreens applied via tweezers. (And, you know, the whole tire manufacturing part of the business.) To preemptively deflate perceived elitism, many associated with the project say there was ultimately only one choice to be its face. Gordon Ramsay and Jesse Burgess Photo by Dave Benett/Getty Images for Studio Ramsay “I’d heard about the show, because they had already filmed quite a bit of it without a host, flying to chefs all around the world,” says Burgess, over lunch this past summer in East Hollywood. “I didn’t think I had a hope in hell of getting the job.” The series was being produced by Studio Ramsay Global, so it was Ramsay who suggested Burgess fly out to do a screen test during the first season’s Sweden shoot. “We had a long list of A-listers lining up to present the show, and Apple wanted some of their own talent, but Jesse, from my side, was the running favorite from day one,” says Ramsay. “What makes him special is his vulnerability in these situations” It’s a unique situation in which Burgess found himself. Ostensibly another cooking competition, Knife Edge , which concludes its second season on Nov. 6, follows chefs from around the world as they strive to earn, maintain or up their count of stars in the storied Michelin guide. They punch walls. They weep. They hemorrhage money. They make very appetizing meals. But in lieu of having Burgess exhaustively interview them, he’s almost the translator of their work — narrating the trials of operating a restaurant and describing meals as he eats them with the relatable manner of a thoughtful guy at the pub who just really wants to tell you about his burger. Most episodes include one of Michelin’s many international galas where the stars are announced and presented. Maintaining a distance from the hopeful chefs like he’s Jane Goodall, Burgess takes it all in from the backs of different ballrooms as careers are made and hearts are broken. His empathy and everyman quality make him suitable for this job, but he doesn’t claim to have ever had ambitions for a traditional career in entertainment. Burgess just likes travel and eat and talk about both. Chatting over our respective plates of Somali chicken and grilled fish at East Hollywood Pan-African bistro Foods From Afar (his selection), Burgess traces his curiosity back to his mother’s career as cabin crew on Britannia Airways and then private jets. View this post on Instagram “To me, her life was just so exciting,” he says, recalling how he’d wait for her return and edible souvenirs. “I had Beluga caviar because she’d flown to Russia, Danish pastries from Copenhagen, Stollen from Cologne. She hates me telling these stories because she reckons she wasn’t allowed to take the food out of the country. She thinks that someone’s going to come and arrest her or something.” In 2015, Burgess made eating his business. He partnered with his friend Will Warr and founded TopJaw. The digital media brand originally just focused on YouTube and on London, because they couldn’t afford to go very far, with Burgess in front of camera and Warr largely behind the scenes. Growth was slow and incremental. It took four years before they hit 10,000 subscribers. But when they began posting travel videos, things accelerated quickly. One in particular, 48 Hours in Paris , went viral. It’s since logged 2.6 million views. Unfortunately, this mitzvah was the eve of lockdown. Restaurant content wasn’t a viable plan in 2020, and the guys thought of hanging it up. But when restrictions loosened, a shift back to the U.K. and, pivotally, a focus on Instagram grew the business so that it could be Burgess’ full-time pursuit by 2023. Today, they have almost 1.9 million followers across platforms. They produce travel videos in cities around the world now, but, in world culinary capital of London, TopJaw has arguably become the most valuable resource for recommendations. He’s not just interviewing chefs anymore, either. Every few clips there’s another luminary: Matt Damon, Florence Pugh (twice), Kate Winslet, Theo James. The singer Jessie Ware, who hosts food podcast Table Manners with her mother Lennie, recently mocked Burgess’ rising profile by referring to him as “Mr Michelin” in her visit to TopJaw. (The calls for talent participation, by the way, are almost exclusively incoming.) Knife Edge has already been renewed for a third season , and Burgess will be there to chronicle the professionals he admires succeed and fail — and to eat their food. But when I ask him the obvious question, if this is another paver in the path from content creator to traditional TV host, the suggestion seems to leave him a little indifferent. “There’s so much that I want to do in that world, and I don’t think I’m necessarily attracted to doing more TV,” he says. “There’s a lot of green grass on both sides. Plus, making videos on the internet is awesome.” So is getting to travel and eat for a living. Jesse Burgess in Apple TV’s Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars . Apple TV THR

articles.title: Katherine Ryan Feeling ‘Grief and Relief’ Over Russell Brand Conviction After Reportedly Calling Out His Behavior on Comedy Central
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 7:16am PT Katherine Ryan Feeling ‘Grief and Relief’ Over Russell Brand Conviction After Reportedly Calling Out His Behavior on Comedy Central By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Katherine Ryan Feeling ‘Grief and Relief’ Over Russell Brand Conviction After Reportedly Calling Out His Behavior on Comedy Central 59 minutes ago ‘Avatar: Fire and Ash’ Sets Collectors Edition Featuring Miley Cyrus Q&A and Deleted Scenes 1 hour ago Joaquin Phoenix Stars in AI Eyewear Campaign Directed by Jonathan Glazer 2 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Years after Katherine Ryan reportedly confronted Russell Brand about alleged predatory behavior while working alongside him on Comedy Central’s “Roast Battle” in 2018, the comedian has spoken out following his conviction on rape and sexual assault charges. “It really made me feel just quite dysregulated again, caught off-guard, emotional, in awe of the survivors who also had nothing to gain,” Ryan said on the latest episode of her podcast “Telling Everybody Everything.” “They came forward despite Russell Brand having fame, power, money and a legion of fans ready to attack them.” Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ The Canadian comedian said she and other women had been privately processing the verdict, which she described as bringing both a sense of justice and renewed grief for those affected. “I will never be someone who like, dances on graves. There has been some justice done today,” she said. “There’s a level of relief, but there’s grief alongside relief.” She continued: “Everything’s nuanced, and it was proved in court that a terrible thing happened, and that means that a terrible thing happened.” Ryan previously made headlines in 2022 when she told Louis Theroux in his BBC documentary series that she had confronted an unnamed male comedian about his alleged predatory behavior. During the interview, Ryan said she had worked alongside a man on a television program and called him a “predator,” describing the potential legal repercussions as a “litigious minefield.” Her comments fueled speculation that she was referring to Brand. Ryan has never publicly confirmed the identity of the comedian she was discussing. Brand, 51, was found guilty Thursday of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault following a four-week trial at London’s Southwark Crown Court. He was acquitted of two additional rape charges and one count of indecent assault. The comedian, who denied all allegations of non-consensual sexual activity, is scheduled to be sentenced on Monday. ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Werwulf,’ ‘Cliff Booth,’ ‘The Odyssey’ and More Costume Designers Show Exclusive Sketches From the Year’s Biggest Movies
articles.full_text: × Cliff Booth: Gloria Kim; Odyssey: I Ellen Mirojnick; Sense and Sensibility: Courtesy of Focus Features Ruffled gowns, sequins and a werewolf hunter dressed in layers of wool are among this year’s costume designs audiences will see on screen. Contemporary designs are seen in Olivia Wilde in “The Invite,” while a nod to the Regency era is made in “Sense and Sensibility.” And there are numbers. Marci Rodgers delivered over 3,000 looks for the “Michael” biopic starring Jaafar Jackson, while Ellen Mirojnick created over 5,300 designs for Christopher Nolan’s epic, “The Odyssey.” Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ Below, Mirojnick, Rodgers and more costume designers share exclusive looks at their concepts for costumes which reflect character arcs and show how clothing can tell a lot about a person before they have even spoken a single line. The Odyssey Gowns were crafted to reflect Anne Hathaway’s sweeping character arc Costume designer Ellen Mirojnick says that though Anne Hathaway’s Penelope had inner strength at the start of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” “it was important that she never appear queen-like.” As the film opens, Penelope’s “dresses were more vulnerable, simpler, not at all decorative. Her work at the loom was softer — it was artistic in a way.” By the time she sets forth to challenge her suitors, though, her gown is a “magnificent blue.” “That was quite intentional,” Mirojnick says. “It was to be the period at the end of the sentence. She needed to look armor-like.” Michael Re-creating the King of Pop’s Motown moment One key scene in Antoine Fuqua’s biopic about Michael Jackson was his performance of “Billie Jean” at the “Motown 25” concert in 1983. There, Jackson debuted not only his moonwalk but his signature outfit: a black sequined jacket, a fedora, a single glove, white socks, cropped pants and black loafers. Costume designer Marci Rodgers says she approached recreating the look “from the feet up.” She used the same shoe Jackson wore: a Florsheim Como Imperial loafer. The pants “were a version of the tuxedo pants that we see when he’s singing ‘Off the Wall’ — it’s the same style.” It turns out that the jacket Jackson wore during the performance belonged to his mother, Katherine. “To me, it was like his cape,” Rodgers says. “He was wearing a piece of clothing that was from his mother’s closet, and that, by far, transformed everything.” Jaafar Jackson, who plays Michael, had a similar jacket and lent it to Rodgers to study. “It was in my possession, so I was able to get as close as possible to re-creating the sequins of Michael’s mother’s jacket.” Wicker A fierce woman with a woven husband In “Wicker,” a spinster fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) in a medieval community, mocked by villagers for her independence, asks the local basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to make her a husband (Alexander Skarsgård) out of wicker. Writer-directors Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson wanted the fisherwoman’s husband to be created practically, rather than with special effects. So prosthetic makeup designer Joe Dunckley and lead makeup FX artist Sarah Rubano spent 18 months developing Skarsgård’s costume. It started with a full-body scan of the actor’s frame so they could sculpt pieces specific to him. The intricate weave was created using a relatively new powder-bed printing process. Dunckley explains, “It’s a volume of thermoplastic elastomer. You shoot a laser into it, and where that focal point of the laser is, it fuses the powder and you can build intricate weave and complex geometry.” In the end, 95% of the costume was made using 50 3D-printed appliances painted to look like wicker and stitched to a spandex suit. The key, Dunckley says, was not to lose Skarsgård under the makeup. Sense and Sensibility Updating Jane Austen At the start of Georgia Oakley’s adaptation of Jane Austen’s classic novel, the Dashwood women (Daisy Edgar-Jones, Esmé Creed-Miles and Caitríona Balfe) are mourning the loss of their father and husband, which meant that there were rules that costume designer Grace Snell had to follow: no shiny buttons, the fabric had to be dull and black was one of the few acceptable colors, along with gray and lavender. “I wanted Mrs. Dashwood to be the deepest shade of grief,” Snell says. So the designer fashioned a black taffeta dress. “What’s great about this black is it’s almost got this stripe of dark green in it, so it looks quite reflective. It felt like it could have been from any time.” Mrs. Dashwood stays in mourning for most of the film, but as the story progresses, Snell began introducing beige into her palette. Willoughby (Frank Dillane), who toys with young Marianne, “has a real interest in fashion,” Snell says “and wants to be seen.” For the London hop scene between Willoughby and Marianne, Snell put the young man in a rust-red moleskin coat. Opposite Marianne’s pink dress, “they look wonderful, but it looks explosive.” She completed Willoughby’s outfit with silk pantaloons. “They were only just coming into fashion, so he’s one of the first to bring them over from France,” Snell says, adding, “He’s a little bit of a rock star; he’s unattainable.” Werwulf A wealthy man is chosen to hunt the beast killing poor townsfolk This companion piece to Robert Eggers’ 2024 “Nosferatu” tells the tale of a 14th-century town beset by a werewolf. Willem Dafoe plays the landowner-hunter hired by the king to lead the charge against the beast. What sets Dafoe’s character apart from the film’s victims is the amount of wool he wears. “His is the character that really denotes wealth,” says costume designer Linda Muir. Because wool was a scarce commodity at the time, Muir put him in double-layered wool coats and linen shirts. His boots, too, are higher than those of anyone else in the film to emphasize his station. The props department made him a family signet ring, and to complete the look, Muir gave him a bycocket, which is commonly associated with Robin Hood. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth Booth’s beer-bottle shirt is his version of the Dude’s robe David Fincher’s follow-up to “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” starring Brad Pitt, is no longer about a cocky stunt double, Cliff Booth — now the stunt man is tending bar. Fincher’s instructions to costume designer Trish Summerville were to keep things authentic and grounded. “Cliff’s character is very lived in,” Summerville says. So she retained elements of Cliff’s character from the first film, like his love for Hawaiian shirts. “Back then, people didn’t have disposable fashion; you kept your clothes for quite a while. Cliff still has his favorite jeans — Levi’s — moccasins and work shirts.” In one scene, Cliff wears a Hawaiian shirt featuring beer bottles. Searching for the perfect shirt, Summerville found various rayon numbers from the ’50s through the ’70s printed with images of bottles of booze. But she needed multiples of the garment for Pitt and his own stunt double. “So I had an artist put them all together, and we printed the graphics on [new] shirts.” She adds, “It made me laugh. Cliff’s a chill rascal, so I thought the shirt was just great for him.” The Invite In Olivia Wilde’s latest, costumes and interiors work together as camouflage Atsushi Nishijima When Angela (Olivia Wilde) and her husband, Joe (Seth Rogen) — a couple on edge — invite their loud upstairs neighbors (Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton) to an intimate dinner party, things take an unexpected turn. In early meetings with Wilde, costume designer Arianne Phillips came to understand how the doorways and windows of Angela’s apartment created “beautiful framing” — so much so that Phillips thought of the costumes like portraits or photographs. “Olivia really loved the idea that Angela’s creative identity is so absorbed into the apartment that she basically blends into the walls,” Phillips says. “There’s a funny scene with her and Joe in the bedroom when she’s asking him about the paint color, and all the colors are so close, you can’t tell them apart. That was reflected in her blouse too.” Loading comments...

articles.title: Carson Daly, Laura Jarrett Ready to Launch ‘New Era’ at NBC’s ‘Saturday Today’
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 7:40am PT Carson Daly, Laura Jarrett Ready to Launch ‘New Era’ at NBC’s ‘Saturday Today’ By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Carson Daly, Laura Jarrett Ready to Launch ‘New Era’ at NBC’s ‘Saturday Today’ 35 minutes ago Jim Cramer Leads CNBC Into Creator-Media Era 2 hours ago Did Midterm Elections Cause Changes in News World Order? 18 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of NBC News Carson Daly was looking for a new challenge in a long career in the media business. On Saturday morning, he’ll get it. Daly will team up with Laura Jarrett , Joe Fryer, and meteorologist Angie Lassman on NBC’s “Saturday Today” telecast, the latest attempt by one of the big broadcast networks to create bespoke versions of their morning franchises that appeal to weekend audiences with a little more time on their hands in the A.M. “If people are waking up with us, we want to respect that and we want to give them something that’s worth tuning into,” says Jarrett, who joined “Today” in 2023, a year after moving to NBC News from CNN. Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ NBC, ABC and CBS have worked to create weekend-news programs with a little more distinction from their weekday flagships. The Saturday telecast of CBS’ “Saturday Morning” puts a spotlight on topics such as food and music. ABC recently recalibrated the anchor teams on its weekend broadcasts of “Good Morning America,” adding Rachel Scott and Rhiannon Ally. NBC has been encouraged in this vision by the Sunday telecast of “Today,” led by Willie Geist . The anchor offers a slower-paced hour of “Today” that tackles headlines as warranted, but also offers up a deeper interview with a person of interest as well as other features. Geist typically writes much of the show by himself. NBC News has experimented with turning Geist’s longer-form interviews into ticketed events , a move that generates live-media revenue. Adding Daly, however, brings a person with a different set of skills to the fore of the Saturday show. Jarrett’s previous co-host, Peter Alexander, had a long tenure as a Washington and White House correspondent . Daly has cultivated a broader set of experiences, famously hosting MTV’s “TRL” earlier in his career, then going to host the wee-hours NBC program “Last Call” and host and executive produce “The Voice.” Over that time, he’s learned to lead in-depth conversations and hold forth with musicians, newsmakers and entertainers. “I’ve always enjoyed longer-form interviews,” Daly says, and he studied Bob Costas and Greg Kinnear, who hosted late-night shows at NBC before his tenure started. “I have a natural curiosity,’” he says, and often comes into a segment with “one thousand questions” he might want to ask a guest — if only “Today” had more time for extended interviews Daly has been a staple on “Today” since 2013, when he joined as a correspondent of sorts, curating interesting developments taking place on social media from the show’s “Orange Room.” These days, he’s more of a regular presence in the weekday telecast’s second hour, and is often found talking alongside Savannah Guthrie, Craig Melvin, Al Roker and other “Today” anchors. Several months ago, he considered how he might push himself, and asked “Today” producers if they would consider letting him co-anchor on days when others were off — even on holidays. “I’ve never been afraid to take on a challenge,” Daly says. “I’m glad I stuck my neck out.” Jarrett has been enjoying her time on “Today” as well as her position as NBC News’ senior legal correspondent. Saturday viewers can still expect to get the headlines, she says. “We will still do the news. We will still do special reports” if warranted, she says. Jarrett has “a style on TV that I happen to not only respect but also enjoy watching, and so I think I’m going to learn a lot,” says Daly. Daly takes up his new duties just as the holiday season approaches, a cycle that often brings a broader audience to “Today.” On Saturday, says Jarrett, viewers might get a peek at the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree arriving in New York — in addition to the official launch of “a new era” for the Saturday program. ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: Meghan Markle’s Father Arrested Over Allegations He Possessed Child Sex Abuse Images
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 7:52am PT Meghan Markle’s Father Arrested Over Allegations He Possessed Child Sex Abuse Images By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Bear Grylls Speaks Out on Russell Brand Verdict After Helping Baptize Him: ‘Justice Has Now Been Served’ and the Victims Are ‘Heroes’ 5 hours ago ‘The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo’ Series Adds Jonathan Pryce, James D’Arcy, Lena Olin, Camille Cottin and More 1 day ago Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault in London Trial; Taken Into Custody 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source GC Images Meghan Markle ‘s estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr., has been arrested over allegations he possessed child sex abuse images. The 82-year-old was arrested in Florida on Friday in connection with allegations that emerged last month , as CBS News first reported. “A Florida man was arrested today on a federal criminal complaint alleging he kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades,” the U.S. Department of Justice said in a statement. “Thomas Wayne Markle, 82, of Lakeland, Florida, is charged with one count of possession of child pornography.” Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ A DOJ press release said that the FBI searched the storage units, which Markle Sr. had kept since 2008, and “seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected CSAM.” The affidavit describes several images, two of which “depict an adult man – whom a witness identified as Markle – with a nude prepubescent girl. The third image depicts a nude prepubescent girl in a room that appears to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines,” the release continued. Markle Sr. is expected to appear in court in Tampa, Florida on Friday. Last month, a report in The Sun claimed that child sex abuse images had allegedly been found in his former home in the Philippines by his son, Thomas Markle Jr. Markle Sr. vehemently denied the allegations to the Daily Mail, calling them “a bunch of lies” and adding: “I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.” In a statement at the time, the Duchess of Sussex said she was “deeply distressed” at the news. She claimed that in 2018, a letter about her father was sent to the Metropolitan Police and its Royalty and Specialist Protection unit and was “subsequently shared” with her. “It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” Meghan said. “I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.” The Metropolitan Police said at the time that they were “undertaking enquiries internally in an effort to confirm” that a letter had been passed from their officers to Meghan. It is understood that the Met has not and is not currently investigating Thomas Markle Sr. Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018, when he failed to walk her down the aisle at her wedding. She was escorted by King Charles instead. Thomas Markle has never met her and Prince Harry ’s two children. Last year, she sent a letter to him while he was in the hospital getting his left lower leg amputated due to a blood clot. “Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” Meghan concluded. The FBI also issued a statement last month saying that they were “aware of the allegations and will provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities. We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of U.S. law.” Representatives for Meghan Markle and the FBI did not immediately respond to Variety ’s request for comment on Markle Sr.’s arrest. Variety has also attempted to contact Markle Sr. for comment. ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: Melania Trump Series Sets Amazon Release Date
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 7:54am PT Melania Trump Series Sets Amazon Release Date By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest Melania Trump Series Sets Amazon Release Date 39 minutes ago Oobah Butler Sets HBO Series ‘Scams for a Better Tomorrow’; Professional Hoax Artist Takes On Wellness Industry, Royal Families and More 23 hours ago Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Amazon Prime Video will release its two-part Melania Trump docuseries on Nov. 20. The previously announced series, which will include “content never before shared with the public,” is split between two episodes: “Family & Trust,” which follows Trump as she prepares to become the First Lady, and “Pride & Honor,” which takes place moments after the inauguration. The docuseries follows the theatrical release of “Melania” on Jan. 30 and the film’s streaming release on March 9. Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ While a press release from Amazon touts “the historic success of ‘Melania, The Film,'” the movie lost tens of millions of dollars. It is true that the film outperformed expectations for a documentary at the box office, garnering $16.6 million worldwide, but considering Amazon paid a whopping $40 million for the rights to “Melania” — plus a $35 million marketing spend — the studio failed to recoup its investment theatrically. “Melania” is directed by Brett Ratner and executive produced by Trump herself alongside Marc Beckman. Ratner produces with Fernando Sulichin, as well as Muse Films, New Element Media and RatPac Entertainment. Variety ‘s chief film critic Owen Gleiberman hated “Melania, The Film,” calling it a “cheeseball infomercial of staggering inertia.” “It’s a ‘portrait’ of the First Lady of the United States, but it’s so orchestrated and airbrushed and stage-managed that it barely rises to the level of a shameless infomercial,” he wrote in his review . “Is it cheesy? At moments, but mostly it’s inert. It feels like it’s been stitched together out of the most innocuous outtakes from a reality show. There’s no drama to it. It should have been called ‘Day of the Living Tradwife.'” Watch a trailer for “Melania, The Series” below. ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Fjord’ Director Cristian Mungiu to Attend AFM as Romania Named First-Ever Country of Focus
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 8:00am PT ‘Fjord’ Director Cristian Mungiu to Attend AFM as Romania Named First-Ever Country of Focus By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest ‘Fjord’ Director Cristian Mungiu to Attend AFM as Romania Named First-Ever Country of Focus 37 minutes ago Taylor Swift’s Canceled Vienna Concerts Due to Thwarted Terrorist Plot to Be Subject of Documentary 1 day ago Pamela Anderson Set for Torino Film Festival Lifetime Achievement Award (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 2026 Getty Images Palme d’Or–winning filmmaker Cristian Mungiu — whose latest film, “Fjord,” is Romania ’s official submission for best international feature film at the Oscars — will be leading a delegation from his country at the upcoming American Film Market, where Romania has been set as the first-ever country of focus. The AFM is launching this new initiative in partnership with the Creative Romanian Filmmakers (CRFM) umbrella group at this year’s market, running Nov. 10–15 at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles. Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ The Romanian delegation will have a dedicated exhibition space at the Fairmont for meetings with international buyers and industry partners. Attending companies include Augmented Films, Bullsrecords, Idea Film, Nomad Films Global, Profesional Film Partners, Quantum Media Creative, Frame Film, Mavish Ask, Negrea Visuals, Sýmbolon and Tarnovski Marketing Consultancy. The initiative is being complemented by market screenings of Romanian films at the AMC Century City 15 cinema, including Moldovan filmmaker Igor Cobileanski’s psychological drama “Comatogen”; Andrei Dascalescu’s cycling journey documentary “Gone Guy”; Ligia Ciornei’s drama “Grounded,” which is set at the outbreak of war in Ukraine; and Valeriu Andriuta’s thriller “The Circle.” Mungiu will be among speakers at a panel titled “Beyond the New Wave: Romania as Your Next Production Partner,” to be held Nov. 14 at the Fairmont. He will be joined onstage by Valentin Savu, general manager of the Romanian Office for Film and Investments in Culture; Alma Bacula, head of production and partner at Bucharest-based Icon Films; and prominent Romanian producers Iuliana Tarnovetchi, Gabriel Popescu and Ionuț Ionescu. The panel will explore opportunities for filming in Romania, partnering with local producers and accessing the country’s production incentives. “This year, a Romanian film was awarded at every major festival,” Mungiu said in a statement. “I believe Romanian films have real potential in international markets — not only at festivals, but with a wider audience,” he added, noting that the awards-season campaign for “”Fjord” and its American theatrical release through Neon “look promising.” “And not only is the Romanian cash rebate working again,” Mungiu continued. “We have also started a conversation with the Romanian authorities about providing upfront cash-flow financing for the rebate, and we hope to see concrete results as early as 2027.” Commented Jackie Brenneman, head of the Independent Film & Television Alliance (IFTA), which produces AFM: “Romania has been part of the AFM community for many years, and we’re proud to recognize its contributions to global cinema as our first-ever Country of Focus.” “Since 2016, Creative Romanian Filmmakers has brought Romanian producers to the world’s most important film markets and festivals, and the American Film Market has always been a key stop on that journey,” said Mihai Lupu, managing director of Creative Romanian Filmmakers. “Being named Country of Focus this year is a milestone for our entire industry — an invitation to buyers, sales agents and producers to discover Romanian stories, talent and locations, and to build lasting partnerships with us.” ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: Fox’s Paul Cheesbrough Will Expand Duties After Roku Deal; Anjali Sud, Charlie Collier to Exit
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 8:00am PT Fox’s Paul Cheesbrough Will Expand Duties After Roku Deal; Anjali Sud, Charlie Collier to Exit By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Carson Daly, Laura Jarrett Ready to Launch ‘New Era’ at NBC’s ‘Saturday Today’ 35 minutes ago Jim Cramer Leads CNBC Into Creator-Media Era 2 hours ago Did Midterm Elections Cause Changes in News World Order? 18 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Fox Corp. Paul Cheesbrough , a one-time software engineer who has worked to transform upstart digital ventures at Fox Corp. into mainstream operations, is taking on an important new role at the company following its $22 billion purchase of Roku . Cheesbrough was named co-chair and CEO of Fox Digital Platforms on Friday, a division that will house Roku operations, Tubi and Red Seat Ventures, among other operations. and turbocharge the company’s new-media ambitions. Roku operates one of the primary portals consumers use to access their favorite programming via streaming and broadband. Anthony Wood, the founder of Roku and previously its chairmand CEO, will become a member of the Fox board and serve as co-chair alongside Cheesbrough. Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ “Together we have premium live sports and news, a growing streaming portfolio, and a leading connected TV platform,” Cheesbrough and Wood said in a memo Friday. “More importantly, we have talented teams who know how to build, innovate, and deliver for viewers, partners, and advertisers. We have a lot to celebrate — and a lot to build.” Under a new structure outlined Friday, the new unit of Fox Corp. will be built around Roku, to be led by CEO Mustafa Ozgen; direct-to-consumer properties like Tubi, Fox One and Frndly TV, led by CEO Pete Distad; and Red Seat Ventures and financial-technology company Credible, which will be led respectively by CEO Chris Balfe and CEO Robert Humann. Several senior executives are leaving the combined company. Charlie Collier, the president of Roku Media, who worked to develop the company’s original content and advertising operations, will exit, as . Chris Handman, Roku’s general counsel, and Robyn Peterson, executive vice president at AdRise, a technology platform for connected TV. Others are taking on new roles. Mike Bidgoli is being promoted to president of Tubi, reporting to Distad. , following a decision by Anjali Sud, CEO of Tubi, to take “a new role outside the company,” according to the memo. She will assist through a transition period. Andy Karofsky, co-founder and CEO of Frndly TV, a live streaming service, will also report to Distad. Lisa Holme, head of content for The Roku Channel, will report to Distad as well. Melody Hildebrandt will continue as chief technology officer. Jeff Dow, executive vice president of platform and media technology, will retire at the end of the fiscal year. Ad sales will report to Jeff Collins, president of ad sales for Fox. Cheesbrough, who got his start as a software engineer working for IBM, has shown a proclivity for digital media, having developed digital products for the BBC and Telegraph Media Group before joining News Corp., a sibling of Fox that is also run by its controlling holders, the Murdoch family. He previously served as the company’s chief technology officer and president of digital, and has presided over a methodical turn by the company, best known, perhaps for Fox News Channel and the Fox broadcast network, into direct-to-consumer operations and content pacts with independent hosts. “We won’t have every answer on Day 1,” the executives said. “We’ll share decisions as they’re made, be clear about what’s still open, and keep moving. Our priorities remain the same: build great products, serve our viewers and partners, and support each other.” ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: Comcast Co-Founder Julian Brodsky Dies at 93
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 8:09am PT Comcast Co-Founder Julian Brodsky Dies at 93 By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Comcast Co-Founder Julian Brodsky Dies at 93 9 minutes ago Fox Closes $22 Billion Roku Takeover, Says Streaming Platform Will Remain ‘Open Ecosystem’ 2 hours ago Lionsgate Quarterly Revenue Pops 41% on Strength of ‘Michael,’ TV Series Sales as Studio Narrows Net Loss 18 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Comcast Julian Brodsky , a cable TV pioneer and financial guru who was a co-founding partner of Comcast more than 60 years ago, has died. He was 93. Comcast announced his death Friday. According to the cable and media company, Brodsky died peacefully surrounded by his family while in hospice care on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Brodsky teamed with Comcast founder Ralph J. Roberts and co-founding partner Daniel Aaron to build the company from its earliest days, beginning with the acquisition of a small cable television system in Tupelo, Mississippi, in 1963. Working from a “modest office” near Philadelphia, the three laid the foundation for what would grow into one of the world’s leading media and technology companies, according to Comcast. Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ “Julian was an extraordinary leader, a brilliant financial mind and one of the architects of cable television,” Brian L. Roberts, chairman of Comcast, said in a statement. “He was a trusted partner and close friend to my father, Ralph, and someone I was fortunate to learn from and work alongside for so many years. He was one of the most creative financiers of his generation, but just as important, he established a culture of financial integrity, uncompromising standards, and respect for colleagues that remains at the heart of our company today.” Roberts added, “Julian was a mentor and a friend, and his contributions to our company and our community cannot be overstated. We will miss him deeply, and our thoughts are with his family and everyone who knew and loved him.” Brodsky was born in Philadelphia on July 16, 1933. He attended Overbrook High School and graduated from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. He served two years in the U.S. Army before beginning his career as a certified public accountant. While working as an auditor, he developed an early fascination with the emerging cable television industry, an interest that would shape the course of his career and help define his legacy. As Comcast’s longtime CFO, Brodsky was instrumental in financing the company’s expansion and efforts to raise capital. The company credits him with helping guide major acquisitions that transformed Comcast from a small regional cable operator into an industry leader. Brodsky was among the industry’s “earliest financial innovators,” according to Comcast, helping establish cable television’s credibility as an investment and demonstrating its long-term potential to banks, institutional investors and Wall Street at a time when the business was still in its infancy. Brodsky played a central role in Comcast’s initial public offering in 1972 and helped establish the company’s reputation for financial integrity and disciplined management, the company said. Along with Ralph Roberts, he formed Comcast Interactive Capital in 1999, now called Comcast Ventures, to invest in early-stage technology companies and obtain a window into opportunities that could potentially benefit Comcast’s business. In 2004, Brodsky became Comcast’s non-executive vice chairman and retired from the company and its board of directors in 2011. Brodksy’s contributions to the cable television industry were recognized with numerous honors, including his induction into the Cable Television Hall of Fame in 2003 and the National Cable & Telecommunications Association’s Distinguished Vanguard Award. Beyond Comcast, Brodsky was a dedicated philanthropist and a champion of the Philadelphia community. Together with his beloved wife of 70 years, Lois, he supported numerous cultural and educational institutions, including the Philadelphia Museum of Art, where he served for nearly three decades as a trustee. In October 2026, the couple announced a $20 million gift to establish the Lois G. and Julian A. Brodsky Learning and Engagement Center, reflecting their longstanding commitment to making art and education accessible to future generations. In addition to Lois, Brodsky is survived by their three daughters, Debra Brodsky, Ellen Brodsky (married to Ted Rybeck) and Laura Brodsky (Michael Beard), and his brother, Marc Brodsky (Vivian Brodsky). He was predeceased by his parents, David and Esther Brodsky. He is also survived by four grandchildren. A private memorial service will be held, and a celebration of Brodsky’s life will be announced at a later date. ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Sparks Frenzy in Europe as  Screenings Sell Out and Anticipation Soars: ‘People Are Just Desperate to See It’
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 8:37am PT ‘You Can See Everything’ Sparks Frenzy in Europe as Screenings Sell Out and Anticipation Soars: ‘People Are Just Desperate to See It’ By Elsa Keslassy , Alex Ritman Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy Everett Collection “ You Can See Everything ,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ’s smash-hit documentary about disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, has yet to open in major international territories. But the crescendoing anticipation for a nearly three-hour film that came out of nowhere suggests that it could also rock numerous other box offices in the coming weeks. In the U.K., where A24 is self-releasing the film, tickets began selling out a month before its opening on Nov. 20, prompting chains such as Picturehouse and Cineworld to add extra screenings. It’s a similar story in France, where distributor Metropolitan Filmexport has seen advance screenings sell out far ahead of its opening there on Dec. 30. Related Stories Pamela Abdy Delivers Fiery Speech After Warner Bros. Exit: ‘It Is Getting Harder, Not Easier, to Be a Woman in the Business’ “I’ve released hundreds of films and I’ve not known anything like it in terms of buzz — people are just desperate to see it,” says a distribution exec in the U.K. “I think it’s going to explode on Nov. 20. It’s going to be one of, if not the biggest documentary of all time, just based on pre-bookings.” Excluding concert films, 2004’s “Fahrenheit 9/11” is still the most successful documentary in the U.K. (it’s currently the most successful globally), with a box office of £6.55 million ($8.8 million), which, adjusted for inflation, is around $16.6 million today. It’s a figure many expect “You Can See Everything” to surpass. A24 adopted a staggered release strategy in the U.S., more than tripling the amount of screens in its second weekend. But Variety hears that, to cope with the pent-up demand, it’ll likely bolt out of the British cinematic gates wide, going straight into around 500 cinemas. In France, Victor Hadida, president of Metropolitan Filmexport, tells Variety that the company organized a nationwide series of sneak previews on Dec. 1 across roughly 100 theaters. Tickets sold out within hours. “It’s crazy because we put tickets on sale on Saturday at 9 a.m., and some theaters were already sold out by noon,” says Hadida, whose slate also includes “The Debut.” “The demand is enormous and it hasn’t stopped. You can see it on social media, and you can see people going to theaters asking about the film.” Unlike the U.K., Metropolitan Filmexport — which bought “You Can See Everything” from A24 at Toronto, shortly after it’s surprise Telluride premiere— will be following a similar progressive rollout to the U.S., opening in approximately 150 to 200 theaters before expanding based on demand. Hadida says the nearly three-hour running time was a key factor in scheduling the release during the Christmas holidays, when moviegoers have more time to spare. Metropolitan is betting that the Dec. 1 previews will help build word of mouth — something that has been absolutely crucial in the film’s success so far — ahead of the official opening. But by the time it comes out in France on Dec. 30, much of the rest of the world will already have had a chance to see it. After acquiring large swathes of Europe, Asia, the Middle East and South America for the film before the opening U.S. weekend, Sony has now revealed its release strategy for all of its 29 territories, with opening dates running from Nov. 19 through Dec. 9. Thanks to cultural and language crossovers, not to mention a strong eye for documentary films, especially theatrically, there are high expectations for Scandinavia. Sony has the entire region, and opens across Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden in the space of 48 hours from Nov. 19. There are similar hopes for another major market, Germany (Dec. 3). Highlighting anticipation there, a recent CNN article told the story of a German fan who crossed the border to get to a preview screening in Poland (where it opens Nov. 6). But with other territories such as India, Mexico, South Korea and Brazil on the rollout list and a film that continues to defy the norms or standard expectations, nothing should be ruled out. As one exec notes: “You can’t sell any market short when something becomes cultural like this.” In terms of actual promotional launch plans for “You Can See Everything,” talks are underway to fly Fielder and Oppenheim over to some of the more major premieres. However, as one publicity insider notes, since the film continues to enjoy a wildly unpredictable journey on home soil, plans are likely “very TBC.” With the U.K. likely the biggest overseas market, London would seem a highly probable destination for the pair (Oppenheim was in town in October for the London Film Festival screening of “Primetime”). They’re both due to attend two BAFTA screenings in the capital next week, so assumingly will be stay in town for the premiere, although exact details of that are yet to be revealed. Hadida adds that Metropolitan is hoping to bring them to Paris in December as well. But given the mystery around the film — not to mention some major spoilers to protect — there’s a limit to what anyone would want the filmmakers to actually talk about. Variety hears that the standard premiere media line would likely be scrapped, while any Q&As would likely be held just for awards voters (Fielder and Oppenheim will be taking part in Q&As at the BAFTA screenings in London) “It’s so different to a lot of other PR plans and strategy, because you just don’t want to say anything,” says the publicity insider. “That’s why it’s all so minimal — you just want the film to speak for itself.” Hadida in France also acknowledges that preserving the mystery — which has been a major element of A24’s marketing strategy — is key. “Part of their approach is also not to reveal too much about the film, because what’s important about this experience is that you discover what the film is about at the same time as the filmmakers,” he says. However, among the more eye-opening reveals in “You Can See Everything,” one that saw the film land an unexpected R-rating for “graphic nudity,” won’t be available to everyone. Due to censorship laws in Middle East, Variety hears that the scene in question — not critical but the source of much chatter — will have to be cut for it to be released. ‘One Minute to Midnight’ Review: A Stellar Cast Deliver Interesting but Overly Preachy Disquisitions on the Changing Nature of Male-Female Relations Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ Sets Broadway Closing; West End Production Announced For 2027
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ Sets Broadway Closing; West End Production Announced For 2027 Kimmarie Johnson Dies: ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ & ‘Dude, Where’s My Car?’ Actor Was 50 Jimmy Kimmel Has Some Post-Blue Tsunami Advice For Donald Trump: “Just Quit” View All November 6, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Buena Vista Social Club' Matthew Murphy Buena Vista Social Club , the Tony-winning musical inspired by the legendary Cuban artists that give the show its title, will close on Broadway January 17, 2027, after a 96-week, 767-performance run. Producers announced the closing date today. Although the production has not recouped its reported $17 million investment, they say it is “on schedule” to do so. Related Stories News Derek Klena To Play Broadway’s ‘Great Gatsby’ During Savannah Bananas Off Season News Tony Awards Extends CBS Broadcast Agreement Through 2032 The musical, which began previews on February 21, 2025, at the Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre, opened March 19 of that year to good reviews and consistently strong box office, features a book by Marco Ramirez, direction by Saheem Ali, choreography by Patricia Delgado and Justin Peck, creative consultation by David Yazbek, music supervision by Dean Sharenow and orchestrations, arrangements and music direction by Marco Paguia. “From our very first trip to Cuba to meet the musicians who created this masterpiece, I knew we had something truly special, something to cherish,” said lead producer Orin Wolf in a statement. “I am in awe of what Marco R., Saheem, Patricia, Justin, David, Marco P. and Dean have created artistically, bringing this extraordinary music to life on stage and presenting the first Broadway score performed exclusively in Spanish. Watch on Deadline “I am deeply grateful for the time we’ve had on Broadway – and the speed with which the team has created three more productions,” he continued. “We are thrilled the Broadway production is on schedule to recoup as we look ahead to an exciting tour, special engagements in Mexico and Puerto Rico, the film and so much more.” A West End production in London is scheduled to begin in 2027. As of now, there are four productions of the musical up and running: On Broadway; on a North American tour (currently at the Music Hall at Fair Park in Dallas, Texas; at the Antonio Paoli Festival Hall at the Centro de Bellas Artes in Puerto Rico, and at the Teatro de los Insurgentes in Mexico City. All feature the first Broadway score performed solely in Spanish. Producers say the musical has attracted the highest number of Hispanic ticket buyers in the history of The Shubert Organization. The Broadway production scored five Tony Awards including Best Performance by an Actress in a Featured Role in a Musical (Natalie Venetia Belcon); Best Choreography; Best Orchestrations; Best Sound Design of a Musical; and a Special Tony Award for the 10-piece center-stage band. The cast album won the Grammy Award. (Belcon is returning to the production November 30, as is Ashley De La Rosa on November 16). While the production has remained one of the stronger Broadway shows, the weekly tallies have dimmed considerably since its peak performances last year, when the musical often grossed well above the $1 million mark. The most recent available figure, for the week ending November 1, was $678,878, with attendance at 89% of the Schoenfeld’s capacity. The current BVSC cast oincludes Gina Torres, Rick Negron, Mel Semé, Jainardo Batista Sterling, Isa Antonetti, Da’Von T. Moody, Wesley Wray, Jesús Pupo, Renesito Avich, Tanairi Sade Vazquez, Chris Myers, José “Candelita” Iglesias, Bernie Williams (Guitar), Angélica Beliard, Joshua Gonzalez, Jacob Guzman, Ian Lassiter, Héctor Juan Maisonet, Ilda Mason, Marielys Molina, Eric Parra, Sophia Ramos, Clinton Roane and Anthony Santos. Inspired by true events, the musical tells the inspiring story of the legendary Afro-Cuban Havana band who reunited to record the 1997 Grammy Award-winning album Buena Vista Social Club. BVSC is produced on Broadway by Orin Wolf, John Styles, Barbara Broccoli, Atlantic Theater Company, Luis Miranda, LaChanze and John Leguizamo, with Executive Producer Allan Williams. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & Maybe Mergers Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel ‘Other Worlds’ A Go At Netflix From ‘First Shadow’ Team Of Kate Trefry & Duffer Brothers
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Disney TV Reorg Chatter Heats Up As Next Wave Of Layoffs Draws Near – The Dish Shari Rosenblum Leaving As Head Of PR For 20th Television After 25 Years Across Disney & Fox Paul Bettany To Star In Netflix Series ‘Pagans’ View All November 6, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix The long-rumored live-action Stranger Things spinoff series has been officially revealed by Netflix . Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure , co-created by Kate Trefry and the Duffer Brothers and directed by Joe Wright , is a prequel set in the 1950s, before Stranger Things and before the stage play Stranger Things: The First Shadow. It will premiere in 2028. A teaser, which you can watch below, provides more information about the offshoot’s setting — both in terms of time, April 19, 1955, and location, Marion, Nevada. It features a deserted bike by a restricted area at night, with town lights in the distance and an ominous disturbance in the sky that resembles a wormhole creation. Related Stories News ‘Stranger Things’ Creators Matt And Ross Duffer Share Updates On Their “Quite Different” Spin-Off Idea, Moving On From The ’80s And Working With Paramount News Netflix Sets ‘Stranger Things: Tales From ’85’ Voice Cast & First Look Photos Of Animated Spinoff The spinoff has been several years in the making, with Matt and Ross Duffer acknowledging that they’d had the idea since Season 4 of the mothership series came out in the summer of 2022. “We are moving forward with it. Netflix, they finally know what it is,” Matt Duffer told Deadline last November . Watch on Deadline And while the creative auspices of Other Worlds are all stressing that it will feature “a wholly new story,” “new characters, themes and mythology,” its connection to the Tony-winning The First Shadow is undeniable. Longtime Stranger Things writer Trefry wrote the stage play from a story by her, the Duffer Brothers and Jack Thorne.
