articles.title: International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario & Christopher Walken Set For True Crime-Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ — AFM International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com ‘Honeymooners’; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM View All November 6, 2026 6:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lokia Lokia EXCLUSIVE : Ahead of the American Film Market, international buyers from 12 territories have teamed up to form a new distribution network called Lokia . The 12 distribution partners comprise Wild Bunch Germany GmbH / Wild Bunch Austria (Germany and Austria); Praesens-Film (Switzerland); PRIS Audiovisuals SA (Portugal); Feelgood Entertainment (Greece); Kazoo Films (UK/Ireland); Noori Pictures (South Korea/ Thailand/Vietnam); Filmhouse (Israel); Blitz Group (Former Yugoslavia); Donart Film (Czech Republic); Mars Production (Turkey); and Horizon Distribution (Global Airlines and Shipping). Related Stories News Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com 'Honeymooners'; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM News International Insider: Russell Brand Guilty; AFM Fires Up; Trudie Styler Interview Incorporated in Luxemboug, the Lokia partners will look to develop and produce content together, pool market intelligence, capitalise on licensing and merchandising opportunities and will soon look to acquire content together. The number of companies in the network could grow in coming months. Watch on Deadline The move is a direct response to consolidation in the market and the challenge posed by the declining international pre-sales model. The companies will continue to acquire content individually for their separate markets and exist as standalone financial entities but the aim is to have larger stakes in IP and to be able to monetise and acquire more aggressively. Multiple projects are in development on the Lokia slate but aren’t ready to be revealed yet. The group isn’t expected to be acquiring as one entity at the AFM but that’s the plan a little further down the road. The Lokia network is the brainchild of Michael Favelle of Australia-based sales agency Odin’s Eye Entertainment and Odin’s Eye Animation, and was co-founded and built with Heiko Nemmert, formerly of German outfit Baby Giant. In addition to the challenge of the pre-sales market, the founders say the network was formed to “provide a solution to the puzzle of IP-derived consumer products for independent animated features.” Favelle explained: “Essentially, without worldwide theatrical guarantees before financing and additional finance to also cover IP extension, licensing campaigns are not realistic. But if there is a system where we co-ordinate both theatrical and licensing partners, offer them investment opportunities in the IP for hedging across territories and rights categories, amongst other synergies we can build a scalable repeatable pipeline, not only for animation but equally for live action.” “I knew we had something that might work when the first distributor I pitched the concept to asked if they could invest,” he continued. Founding partner Yong Ho Lee of South Korean buyer Noori Pictures noted: “It’s no secret that the Korean market has not bounced back after the pandemic. The Lokia partnership gives us greater opportunity to expand our business outside of our traditional home territory. The reality is that we are competing against global giants, and while it’s somewhat of a cliché, together we can be stronger.” Co-founder Nemmert supervised the build of Lokia’s operating system (Lokia OS) and runs the company’s operations and production side. Lokia OS is live and onboarding of distribution and licensing partners is under way. According to the founders, the platform puts the network in one working environment: partners submit projects, distributors return revenue forecasts, and financing and licensing partners see the aggregated picture before capital is committed. “Assets, market intelligence and transparent reporting all run through the same system,” they commented. Nemmert expanded: “Partners are responding to three things: they see projects early, their forecasts and input carry real weight in how a film is financed and produced, and they get a view across the whole network instead of working in isolation. Our system makes that coordination routine. And for our production partners, market validation and transparent feedback add clear value.” Former Marvel executive Russell Brown, Lokia’s Chief Capital and Monetisation Officer, is leading discussions with independent licensing agencies for each territory and is in talks with potential global category partners in toys, video games and publishing. The announcement of licensing partners is anticipated later in Q4, 2026. “The licensing and merchandising industry has never had the opportunity to participate in quality independent IP productions in such an orchestrated fashion, which is why we are seeing such a positive response from the major agents we are signing,” said Brown. Andrew Baker, CEO of Kazoo Films added: “Lokia is an innovative new company, giving distributors early access to projects, enabling us to assess and advise on the development of films, giving them the best commercial advantage. We are thrilled to be the partner for the UK & Ireland and look forward to working closely with Lokia and the other distributors to collectively bring market intelligence to early stage animated movies.” Lokia, which will be exhibiting at the American Film Market at Fairmont Suite 411, has also formed a strategic partnership with Fintage House to oversee reporting and manage collection accounts. Fintage House Co-Chairman Robbert Aarts will join Lokia’s board. It’s not the first grouping of international companies we’ve seen in recent years in response to shifts in the film distribution landscape. The Vuelta distribution group was formed in 2023, in 2024 a group of foreign distributors teamed up to help finance films produced by MadRiver, and producers alliance The Creatives has emerged since then. Lokia’s three principals comprise: Michael Favelle, Chief Creative Officer and President of Distribution who founded Sydney-based production, sales and distribution company Odin’s Eye Entertainment in 2006; Heiko Nemmert, Chief Operating Officer and President of Production, who was previously managing director of Berlin-based Baby Giant; and Russell Brown, Chief Capital and Monetisation Officer, who served as Executive Vice President of Worldwide Licensing, Promotions and Ad Sales at Marvel Enterprises and, from 2012, as President of Consumer Products, Promotions and Ad Sales at Valiant Entertainment. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Dobrev Rom-Com; ‘Obsession’ Producer Pic; New Int’l Distributor Network ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ Sets Broadway Closing & West End Date Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Katherine Ryan Feeling “Grief & Relief” Over Russell Brand Conviction After Calling Him A “Sexual Predator” On Comedy Central’s ‘Roast Battle’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Katherine Ryan Feeling “Grief & Relief” Over Russell Brand Conviction After Calling Him A “Sexual Predator” On Comedy Central’s ‘Roast Battle’ Bear Grylls Speaks Out After Getting Heat For Baptizing Russell Brand: “It Is Right That Justice Has Been Served” Russell Brand Trial: Katy Perry Omitted By Prosecutors View All November 6, 2026 6:36am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Russell Brand with Katherine Ryan and Jimmy Carr on 'Roast Battle' Comedy Central Katherine Ryan has said she is feeling “grief and relief” after Russell Brand was convicted of rape and sexual assault in London on Thursday. Ryan was one of the first prominent industry figures to call out Brand’s behavior, with Deadline revealing in 2023 that she repeatedly accused him of being a “sexual predator” during the recording of Comedy Central series Roast Battle in 2018. Related Stories News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault News Russell Brand Trial Reveals Worst & Best Of TV Industry That Protected, Then Exposed A Predator Speaking on her Telling Everybody Everything podcast, Ryan responded to Brand being found guilty of multiple sexual offenses at Southwark Crown Court. Watch on Deadline “It really made me feel just quite dysregulated again, caught off-guard, emotional, in awe of the survivors who also had nothing to gain,” she said. “They came forward despite Russell Brand having fame, power, money, and a legion of fans ready to attack them.” Ryan continued: “I will never be someone who like, dances on graves. There has been some justice done today. There’s a level of relief, but there’s grief alongside relief. Everything’s nuanced, and it was proved in court that a terrible thing happened, and that means that a terrible thing happened. “I just think again and again about people who have been hurt, and who have to carry that, who’ve carried that around long enough, and will continue to carry that in some way, regardless of what justice is done.” Deadline reported how Brand was dropped from Roast Battle after Ryan torched him on camera over allegations that he had sexually assaulted women. Her jokes did not make the final edit. One person familiar with the matter said Brand was “absolutely furious” at being targeted by Ryan. Ryan had previously spoken about her experience on Roast Battle , but did not name Brand or the show she was working on. In an appearance on BBC series Louis Theroux Interviews.. ., Ryan revealed that she confronted her unnamed co-star: “I – in front of loads of people, in the format of the show – said to this person’s face that they are a predator.” She revisited the subject during her Sky stand-up special last year . Ryan explained: “I was invited on a panel show, and I was so excited to do it, but then I found out that if I went on, I would be sat next to a man whom I firmly believe, but can’t prove to be a c***. And that’s the lawyer’s choice of words, not mine.” She continued: “Initially, I turned the job down, and then I thought: well, he’ll be there in his unnecessarily tight jeans, won’t he? He’ll be there, finger-banging Tucker Carlson or sucking off a Tibetan monk for views, whatever he does now… I thought I will go on the show, and I made a moral decision.” Her decision was that she would confront Brand and make jokes about his alleged reputation, “but in a fun way.” She recalled two gags she made about Brand, neither of which made the final edit when Roast Battle screened in the UK in 2018. Ryan said Brand was “fine with it for a while, until eventually he had a hissy fit and threatened to quit the show.” She continued: “The channel got upset. They didn’t want him to leave, and they issued him a new contract, which he waltzed into my dressing room and threw under my nose the next day. He said: ‘Look, you’re not allowed to be mean to me anymore, because I don’t consent.’” Ryan added that she had to “be nice” following Comedy Central’s intervention on the show, produced by Fulwell Entertainment. He was eventually replaced by Jonathan Ross. Brand will be sentenced Monday. He faces a significant jail term. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Fox Corp. Closes $22 Billion Acquisition Of Roku
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Fox Corp. Closes $22 Billion Acquisition Of Roku Online Media Pioneer Salon To Shutter: “Our Publishing Model Is No Longer Sustainable” Netflix Woos Mattel Veteran Roberto Stanichi To Lead Consumer Products and Experiences View All November 6, 2026 6:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images/Deadline Fox Corp. has closed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku , creating a massive new player in streaming. Shares in Roku, which was founded more than two decades ago, will stop trading on the Nasdaq as of Friday. Related Stories News How Fox’s $22 Billion Deal For Roku Raises The Floor For Its Content, Advertising Revenue & Creator Division Executives Both Sides Of Fox’s $22B Roku Acquisition Call It A Streaming Win-Win, But Wall Street Has Questions Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch earlier this week indicated that regulators outside the U.S. had blessed the merger, and there were reports that the U.S. Department of Justice also was nearing sign-off. But the closing came less than five months after the deal was proposed last June – well ahead of the initially projected window of the first half of 2027. Roku founder and CEO Anthony Wood will be involved with the combined operation, joining Fox’s board of directors and becoming Co-Chair of Fox Digital Platforms. The newly formed division includes properties like Roku, Tubi, Fox One, and Red Seat Ventures. Paul Cheesbrough is now Co-Chair and CEO of the digital division. Watch on Deadline While Wood is staying on, plenty of questions remain about how Fox intends to structure executive teams in advertising, product and many other areas. Tubi, the free, ad-supported service Fox acquired in 2020, has thrived as a San Francisco-based group granted a degree of autonomy by its parent company. One exec who could factor into the combination is Charlie Collier. The former CEO of Fox Entertainment has been president of Roku Media since 2022. Ahead of the deal, Roku said its platform reaches more than 100 million households, most of them in the U.S. but also in several other countries. The official announcement of the deal’s close said it marks the beginning of “a new transformational era” for Fox. The transaction creates “an innovative, scaled media and technology company with superior reach, engagement and monetization capabilities,” the company added. Fox expects to realize merger-related cost savings of $400 million within two years, and also sees the deal helping its free cash flow per share by 2028. “The closing of this acquisition advances the long-term strategy of Fox,” Murdoch said. “Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform. Our shared entrepreneurial passion and clear conviction toward building the future together with our new Roku colleagues gives us great confidence in the opportunities ahead of us.” Under terms of the merger agreement, Roku stockholders are entitled to receive $95.30 in cash and 0.9799 shares of Fox Class A common stock for each share of Roku Class A and Roku Class B common stock they owned immediately prior to closing. As a result of the transaction, Fox stockholders own about 74% of the outstanding shares of Fox common stock and former Roku stockholders own about 26%. Wood added in a statement, “We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn’t change today. What does change is our reach and resources. Fox has a deep respect for Roku’s culture and wholly shares our commitment to staying open to every content partner. Our teams will keep building and innovating as they always have, now with the support and capabilities of Fox behind us. I’m proud of what Roku’s employees have built, and I’m excited about what comes next.” ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & Maybe Mergers Read More About: 3 Comments

articles.title: ‘Dune’ Star Chang Chen Introduces Six Rising Taiwanese Actors In Golden Horse & TCCF Showcase
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Weta FX CEO Daniel Seah Unpacks TAICCA Partnership: “Taiwan Has Creative Talent, Technology & Government Support” Taiwan Creative Content Fest Opens With Focus On IP, Co-Production & Pledges Of Government Support Weta FX Partners With TAICCA To Position Taiwan As AI Hub; Expands Partnership With Moonshine Studio View All November 6, 2026 6:53am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Rosen, Ho Man-Xi, Lin Yi-Ting, Chang Chen, Sue Wang, Bai Xiao-ying, Ma Shih-yuan, Jimmy Liu Deadline Taiwanese star Chang Chen introduced six rising actors in a showcase co-organized by the Golden Horse Awards and Taiwan Creative Content Fest ( TCCF ) at the seventh edition of TCCF today. The event, which marks the first collaboration between TCCF and Taiwan’s Golden Horse Awards, aims to raise the profile of Taiwanese actors at a time when they’re becoming a key factor in structuring international co-productions. The six talents included actresses Bai Xiao-ying ( Girl ), Ho Man-xi ( Sunshine Women’s Choir ), Ma Shih-yuan ( Left-Handed Girl ), and Lin Yi-ting ( A Dance With Rainbows ), along with actors Rosen ( Marching Boys ) and Jimmy Liu ( Blind Love ). Related Stories News Weta FX CEO Daniel Seah Unpacks TAICCA Partnership: "Taiwan Has Creative Talent, Technology & Government Support" News Taiwan Creative Content Fest Opens With Focus On IP, Co-Production & Pledges Of Government Support Bai and Ho are both nominated for Best New Performer at this year’s Golden Horse Awards, while the remaining four talents were all nominated last year, with Ma winning in the category. Watch on Deadline “We’re seeing more co-productions involving Taiwan and it’s encouraging to see this kind of exchange,” said Chang, whose recent credits include Dune and Cannes Directors Fortnight title Lucky Lu . “It’s important for us to learn more about each other, particularly in international co-productions, to avoid misunderstandings that could delay the production process.” Sue Wang, Chair of TCCF organizer the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), said: “Taiwanese actors are one of the elements that could be used to apply for TAICCA funding, so we need to raise the profile of our acting talent and create more opportunities for them to be seen.” During the showcase, each of the actors talked about their acting, language and other professional skills and the kind of projects they hope to work on in the future. Bai speaks fluent Japanese, while Rosen and Ma both speak English. Liu was winning Taekwondo competitions before landing a role in Disney+ series American Born Chinese alongside Michelle Yeoh. Chang, who is currently serving as Chair of the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee, gave the six young actors a few career tips. “It’s not about whether a project is international or not, it’s about being adaptive to different production teams.” He also passed on some advice that he was given by a director early in his career: “Read autobiographies of as many people as you can. As an actor, you need to experience different lives throughout your career, but at your young age, your experience of life is limited. So read autobiographies to understand the thoughts and emotions of other people.” Golden Horse Film Festival opens tonight and runs until November 22, with the Golden Horse Awards being held on the final night of the festival. Sabu’s Arrested Memory and Shu Qi’s Girl are heading the nominations. TCCF also opened today and runs until November 9. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Dobrev Rom-Com; ‘Obsession’ Producer Pic; New Int’l Distributor Network ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ Sets Broadway Closing & West End Date Read More About: Comments

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Story Of Woman Who Shadowed Top L.A. Detective Jigsaw John Optioned For TV By UK Indie British Comedy Producer Who “Laughed” During Russell Brand Assault Dropped From BBC & Apple Shows Russell Brand Trial Reveals Worst & Best Of TV Industry That Protected, Then Exposed A Predator View All November 6, 2026 7:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand and his wife Laura Brand arrive in court Dan Kitwood/Getty UPDATED: Friday, 7.22 a.m PT: Russell Brand ’s lawyer has referred himself to the UK’s professional regulator for barristers after being accused of launching a tirade at a Sunday Times journalist Thursday outside the courthouse. Ian Winter KC said: “Having seen the ways matters have been characterised in today’s press, I consider my professional duty requires me to self-report those allegations to the Bar Standards Board so the matter can be subject to proper scrutiny. Numerous publications reported that Ian Winter KC launched a tirade at Sunday Times journalist Rosamund Urwin outside Southwark Crown Court. Watch on Deadline Winter was reported to have said to Urwin, “I hope you’re pleased with yourself.” She was heard replying, “I’m pleased justice has been done,” and Winter was then reported to have snapped back, “Well it wasn’t. You f**ked it.” Urwin was one of the lead journalists who broke allegations about Brand as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4 joint investigation in 2023. During his closing arguments last week, Winter said the documentary had “poisoned the well of justice deliberately” and “fundamentally corrupted” Brand’s accusers. The prosecution, on the other hand, argued that the doc was the catalyst for six women to come forward to the police but that none of the women knew each other and the doc was no “magic force” that caused them to “recast their memories.” Brand was earlier found guilty on one count of rape and three of sexual assault. Brand was found not guilty on two other counts of rape and one of attempted indecent assault, which was reduced from indecent assault during the trial. articles.title: Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario & Christopher Walken Set For True Crime-Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ — AFM
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario & Christopher Walken Set For True Crime-Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ — AFM International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com ‘Honeymooners’; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM View All November 6, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario and Christopher Walken Eric Ray Davidson/Storm Santos/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Taylor Kitsch ( Lone Survivor ), Alexandra Daddario ( The White Lotus ) and screen legend Christopher Walken ( The Deer Hunter ) are set to star true crime thriller The Long Island Bank Robber . Based on a true story, Kitsch will star as Stephen Trantel, “a successful Wall Street commodities trader. After being fired from his job, Stephen’s desperate attempts to keep his family afloat lead him down the unimaginable path of becoming one of Long Island’s most prolific bank robbers.” Daddario will star as Jeanne Trantel, Stephen’s “discerning wife who grows increasingly suspicious of her husband and yearns to pave her own path outside of the home.” Oscar winner Walken will play Stephen’s father, a retired police officer ‘with a strong ethical code.” Related Stories News International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM News Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com 'Honeymooners'; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM Matthew Gentile ( American Murderer ) will direct from a screenplay he co-wrote with Bianca Vera, based on the non-fiction book ‘ Til Heist Do Us Part by Jeanne Callahan and Michael Harvey. Production is to begin this month in New Jersey. Watch on Deadline Vaneast Pictures has acquired worldwide sales rights and will launch the project for buyers ahead of next week’s AFM . The film is being produced by Vince Jolivette and Richie Hill of Filmopoly ( The Threesome ), Chris Bellant of Vision Entertainment ( Neighborhood Watch ) and Danielle Gasher of Vaneast Pictures ( Hellhound ). Taylor Kitsch, Andres Budnik, Liam Scholey, Raymond Kimsey, Matt Allen, Dan Reardon, Kyle Fox, Alan B. Bursteen and Dawn Bursteen serve as executive producers. Patricia DiCerto ( Blue Jasmine ) has joined as casting director. Gentile’s feature directorial debut, American Murderer , was a true-crime thriller starring Tom Pelphrey, Ryan Phillippe, Idina Menzel, and Jacki Weaver. The movie won awards at multiple American festivals after launching at Taormina in Italy. “ The Long Island Bank Robber is a true story I learned about in my youth, growing up in New York City as a true-crime obsessive. A propulsive heist film on the surface, the story also tackles complex themes of grief, survival, and marriage. With Taylor, Alexandra, and Christopher as our three leads — I could not have dreamed of a better cast to bring this film to life,” said director and co-writer Matthew Gentile. “This package is a rare find, with that perfect combination of a gripping true-crime script, a talented director, and a star-studded ensemble. We can’t wait to get this one in front of buyers,” said Danielle Gasher, Vaneast Pictures. “We’re thrilled to bring Matthew Gentile’s vision for this film to life with this incredible cast and crew, and to be partnering with Vaneast for the global sales. This is such a compelling and layered story that we can’t wait to share with the world,” stated producer Richie Hill. Kitsch is represented by Untitled Entertainment and CAA. Daddario is represented by CAA, Untitled Entertainment, and Jackoway Austen. Walken is represented by CAA. articles.title: Genre Label Vasaria Pictures Forms Pact With Vertical Horror Streamer TerrorBox
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Genre Label Vasaria Pictures Forms Pact With Vertical Horror Streamer TerrorBox Comcast’s Sky Receives Security Threat After RTE Evacuates Staff International Insider: Russell Brand Guilty; AFM Fires Up; Trudie Styler Interview View All November 6, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Dead Signal' TerrorBox EXCLUSIVE: Vasaria Pictures , the genre label set up by Saw writers Patrick Melton and Marcus Dunston and producers Sean Gowrie and Nick Phillips, has teamed with horror-focused vertical streamer TerrorBox . The pair will work together to develop short-form content, often from emerging horror filmmaking talent, and seek to expand that into feature films. As part of the agreement, TerrorBox will release Vasaria’s short film Jezebel as a vertical series on the platform. Inspired by the classic Hammer horror films, Jezebel was directed by Phillips and written by and starring TikTok creator Claire Dellamar. Related Stories Casting 'Christmas At Maple Hollow Inn' Microdrama Hopes To Channel The Spirit Of Festive TV Movies Through Meta's Series Feature News Eric Roberts, Merrick Hanna & Neela Jolene Starring In Vertical Drama 'It's My Party And I'll Die If I Want To' The Jezebel short has amassed more than four million views on the popular horror YouTube channel Alter, and Vasaria is concurrently developing the property as a feature film in the vein of route taken by horror hits Obsession and Backrooms . Watch on Deadline Vasaria and TerrorBox will also collaborate on a vertical adaptation of Fate , a screenplay by Melton and Dunstan, who wrote four instalments of the Saw franchise ( Saw IV , Saw V , Saw VI and Saw 3D ). Vasaria will explore select TerrorBox titles for potential feature film development. Box Entertainment Group , which Ryan Justice set up in 2025 launched TerrorBox earlier this year as a microdrama service dedicated to horror. This was part of Box’s business model to create genre-specific platforms such as AxnBox, which is dedicated to action, adventure and Westerns. Justice, whose filmmaking credits include Followers and The Wild Man , said: “We’re building a platform where horror filmmakers have a dedicated home to create and keep creating. Partnering with the team at Vasaria brings an incredible depth of experience and storytelling talent to TerrorBox. “Vertical storytelling offers an entirely new canvas for horror, challenging filmmakers to rethink how they build suspense, create tension and scare audiences. We’re only beginning to explore what’s possible with this format, and that’s what makes it so exciting.” “We have been exploring the vertical space for some time, and after meeting Ryan, we knew we had found the right partner,” added the Vasaria team in a statement. “This collaboration gives us the opportunity to discover and work with exciting emerging voices in horror while also bringing our own stories to life in an entirely new format. We see tremendous creative potential in vertical storytelling and are thrilled to be building something with Ryan and the TerrorBox team.” TerrorBox has been expanding its lineup recently through independent acquisitions for titles such as Dead Signal , written and directed by Rick Shepherd and Benjamin Steeper, featuring an ensemble of performers from the vertical entertainment space, including Jessica Jacoby, Aaron Oberst, Candace Mizga, Jarred Harper, Vincent Elric, Rick Shepherd and Zachary B. Rist. The streamer has also bought the Nightmarish TV library of vertical horror shorts. Created by Atlanta-based filmmakers Madison Hoover and Jaime Lucero Jr., this comprises bite-sized horror stories designed specifically for vertical viewing, typically running 90 seconds or less. Titles available on the platform include Ouija , Slasher and Augmented . A deal is also in place with Echo Cell Productions, led by David Wing, and the Echo Cell Collective, an international community of horror creatives working to develop, produce and promote original vertical horror content. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & Maybe Mergers Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Christmas At Maple Hollow Inn’ Microdrama Hopes To Channel The Spirit Of Festive TV Movies Through Meta’s Series Feature
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Genre Label Vasaria Pictures Forms Pact With Vertical Horror Streamer TerrorBox Comcast’s Sky Receives Security Threat After RTE Evacuates Staff International Insider: Russell Brand Guilty; AFM Fires Up; Trudie Styler Interview View All November 6, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn' Pixie USA EXCLUSIVE: Jonas Barnes’ Pixie USA is launching Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn as one of the first microdrama to use Meta’s new Series tool. The romantic holiday drama will star Analisa Southworth Wall and Thomas King , and was developed in partnership with the Bob Evans grocery. The aim is to recreate the feel of a festive TV movie as a vertical series. Blake Studwell directs, with Michael Sokol producing. Filmed in Marietta, Georgia, the family-friendly production will comprise 20 episodes with a total running time of 38 minutes and launches on November 14, as one of vertical series Meta is testing this month, we understand. As such, it will be distributed on Facebook and Instagram, along with YouTube and TikTok. Related Stories Legal Google, TikTok And Meta Sue To Block California's Social Media Law That Restricts Addictive Features For Children News Eric Roberts, Merrick Hanna & Neela Jolene Starring In Vertical Drama 'It's My Party And I'll Die If I Want To' Wall’s credits include Picture Perfect Sister-in-Law and Mother Warrior Unleashed . King’s television credits include Tyler Perry’s The Oval and County Rescue . Studwell previously directed vertical romances Baby, Just Say Yes! and Falling for My Mafia Bodyguard . Watch on Deadline Meta is set to begin testing its new tool, titled Series, which will allow select creators to bundle vertical videos for Reels into episodes on Facebook and Instagram. Meta isn’t commenting on specific titles using the Series feature prior to its launch in certain markets on November 16. Per the synopsis, Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn follows “a determined young woman who reunites with her former flame to save her family’s inn during the Christmas season. Their last hope rests on a spectacular holiday meal for a group of hard-to-impress investors – but she cannot cook. With the kitchen in chaos and old feelings resurfacing, the pair must find a way to preserve the inn’s future while navigating an unexpected second chance at love.” Developed around food and holiday themes, the series will feature Bob Evans mashed potatoes and macaroni and cheese meals at the center of the story. It marks the food brand’s first scripted holiday season production. Ciare James, Senior Vice President and Chief Marketing Officer at Bob Evans Farms , said: “This microdrama brings our brand story to life, showing how Bob Evans holiday favorites can make a memorable meal while leaving more time to enjoy the holiday season.” “Christmas movies have an enduring appeal because they bring audiences into a world of romance, hope and possibility,” added Barnes, CEO at Pixie USA. “Vertical content is reaching tens of millions of people where they are, bringing entertainment directly to their phones. Social media is the new TV, and microdramas are helping drive that shift. “It’s an industry growing so rapidly that it’s almost hard to keep up. With Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn , we wanted to capture that festive magic in a story people can enjoy on their phones. Analisa and Thomas bring warmth and chemistry to the romance, and Bob Evans felt like a natural partner for a film about family, hospitality and the moments that bring people together.” This isn’t the first time Barnes has created a microdrama for a brand, having worked with Procter & Gamble om The Golden Pear Affair , which was developed with Native, P&G Studios and Dentsu Entertainment. Barnes previously worked at Neal H. articles.title: ‘Melania, The Series’ Gets Prime Video Release Date & Trailer
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise ‘Melania, The Series’ Gets Prime Video Release Date & Trailer Ella Langley, Tim McGraw, Miranda Lambert Among Performers For CMA Awards More Details Revealed About ‘Ellen DeGeneres Show’ EP Matthew Wright’s Sudden Death View All November 6, 2026 8:23am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Prime Video has set Friday, November 20 for the premiere of Melania, The Series, the two-episode follow-up to Brett Ratner ‘s Melania documentary. The streamer also released the trailer which you can see above. Related Stories News 2026-27 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable Documentary At ‘Melania’ Premiere, Brett Ratner And The First Lady Defend Cost Of Amazon MGM Documentary “Everybody wants to be close to power and sometimes could be very dangerous,” Melania Trump says at the opening of the trailer. It then segues to shots of Melania and Barron Trump. “I’m a mother, a wife and first lady. He’s [Barron] my priority. He will always be my priority.” At another point in the trailer, Melania Trump addresses the media. “The media, they want gossip. For me, it’s noise,” she says. The series is comprised of two episodes, the first titled “Family & Trust” and the second, “Pride & Honor.” Per the official logline, The Series reveals never-before-told stories, offering unprecedented insight into Melania Trump’s life, including the extraordinary days immediately following the 47th Presidential Inauguration. Watch on Deadline Per the episode descriptions, in “Family & Trust”, “Melania Trump sets priorities as she prepares to become America’s First Lady. But inside the White House, trust is tested, and the incoming First Lady must protect those closest to her while navigating the demands of power.” In “Pride & Honor’: “The honor of serving as First Lady comes with an immediate call to action. Another IP-led project in the works is a TV series adaptation of the 2011 movie Chalet Girl . Tenko was produced for the BBC in the UK and ABC in Australia running for three seasons between 1981-1984 and yielding a special in 1985. Starting in 1942, it followed a group of UK, Australian and Dutch civilian women held in a fictitious Japanese internment camp near Singapore. It showed how the women survived the harsh conditions, banded together and fought to survive in the prison camp. articles.title: Charter Stock Sinks As Internet Subscriber Losses Worsen; Could A Comcast Merger Be The Next Move?
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Fox Corp. Closes $22 Billion Acquisition Of Roku Online Media Pioneer Salon To Shutter: “Our Publishing Model Is No Longer Sustainable” Netflix Woos Mattel Veteran Roberto Stanichi To Lead Consumer Products and Experiences View All November 6, 2026 8:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Charter Communications Photo Illustration by Igor Golovniov/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images Charter Communications shares fell 5% in early trading Friday after the pay-TV, broadband and wireless provider reported wider internet subscriber losses in the third quarter. During the quarter, in August, Charter closed its $34.5 billion acquisition of rival Cox Communications, expanding its footprint to 45 states. Quarterly results, reported on a pro forma basis to account for the merger, showed continued erosion of internet and pay-TV customers. Wireless remains a comparative bright spot, with 1.8 million sign-ups over the past year giving the company 13.5 million wireless customers as of September 30. Related Stories News Online Media Pioneer Salon To Shutter: "Our Publishing Model Is No Longer Sustainable" News Lionsgate Quarterly Revenue Pops With Growth Across Film & TV Studios, Library The company shed 233,000 internet customers – 156,000 at legacy Charter and 77,000 at legacy Cox – in the quarter. The subscriber total sat at 34.3 million as of the end of the quarter. Wireless and satellite internet providers, including Elon Musk’s Starlink, have put pressure on major broadband players like Charter and fueled speculation about a potential Charter-Comcast tie-up. Comcast is about to split off NBCUniversal from its connectivity business, which faces similar headwinds. Watch on Deadline Along with the quarterly results, CEO Chris Winfrey unveiled plans to cut $2 billion in costs and reaffirmed a projection for $1 billion in merger-related synergies. Investors seemed underwhelmed, with Friday’s downturn in the stock price extending a 43% drop in 2026 to date. Cord-cutting continues to eat away at pay-TV levels, even though Charter’s Spectrum systems have integrated streaming services aggressively enough to stem the downturn more than many operators. Total video customers fell by 77,000 in the quarter, compared with a decline of 121,000 a year ago. The total subscriber base was 13.8 million at the end of the quarter. Total company revenue rose 9% over the year-earlier period, reaching $14.9 billion. Gregory Williams, an analyst for TD Cowen, anticipated the Friday trade in a client note earlier this week. “Investors may not get constructive until they see a resting place on broadband subscriber losses,” he wrote. “The next catalyst could be a Comcast/Charter tie-up, which may need to occur sooner rather than later given the midterm election results as a broader regulatory signal.” ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & Maybe Mergers Read More About: Comments

Season one dove headfirst into the age-old romantic trope of fake dating with music student Hannah Wells (Bright), who, in true hockey fashion, is often called Wellsy by her love interest, Garrett Graham (Cameli). “I consider [episode six] a pilot episode or a soft launch for season two and what you’re going to expect,” Kalyn previously told The Hollywood Reporter . “I was so grateful to learn from Ella and Belmont and watch those two great phenomenal actors lead season one.” Abdalla had similar sentiments, sharing her excitement for getting to work more closely with her co-star. “I truly love working with Stephen so much,” she previously told THR ahead of the announcement she and Kalyn would lead season two. “I’m excited that I get to do this with him because I trust him so much.” Abdalla, Kalyn, Bright and Cameli are joined by Antonio Cipriano, Jalen Thomas Brooks and India Fowler as series regulars for Off Campus season two. articles.title: Former UTA and FaZe Clan Execs Launch Creator Management Firm ISO
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 8:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source ISO's Darren Yan and Mike Lee ISO A pair of veteran executives from the creator space are launching new venture meant to help digital creators expand their businesses across content, music, products and live experiences. The management and representation company is called ISO, and is being launched by Mike Lee, the former head of gaming and livestreaming at UTA Creators, who is CEO, and Darren Yan, former chief talent officer at FaZe Clan, who is head of music. ISO is backed by Influence Media Partners, the music and entertainment-focused investment company. The company’s talent roster includes PlaqueBoyMax, Jasontheween, Ironmouse, Lacy, Vanillamace, Kyedae, RDCWorld, with brand clients that include Electronic Arts, Discord, Underdog and Icenova. ISO says it has more than 90 clients, with a heavy focus on livestreamers, gamers, artists, VTubers and lifestyle creators across beauty, food and other verticals. Creators are increasingly leveraging the audiences they have built through their streams and social channels to build businesses elsewhere, and at the same time brands are eager to work with creators on campaigns and original content. Firms like ISO can help connect those dots. “The next household name is already online, building an audience, and ISO was built for that talent,” said Mike Lee, CEO and co-founder of ISO. “Today’s gatekeepers are algorithms, so understanding discovery, engagement and how content travels is essential. Every creator we work with is running a real business, and our job is to give it room to grow through original IP, products, live events, and expansion into China and platforms like TikTok Shop, where most of the industry still isn’t set up to compete.” “At Influence, we look to invest in partners who bring an innovative approach to the business of culture and entertainment,” added Lylette Pizarro, founder & co-managing partner of Influence Media Partners. “Mike, Darren and the team at ISO are reimagining talent representation for a creator economy that has fundamentally transformed how audiences are built, culture is shaped and revenue is generated. ISO’s playbook directly aligns with our values and investment philosophy, and we’re excited to support their growth.” “Talent development used to be the heart of every company in the representation business. ISO is bringing it back with our model built for the new generation where musicians and creators increasingly share the same playbook: build an audience directly, then build a business around it,” said Darren Yan, co-founder and head of music at ISO. “We invest in our clients from the earliest stages across music, media, products, live events, gaming and tech, with our A&R team applying the same lens to artists by building global fandom online before the market catches on.” THR

articles.title: Emmy Rossum Named RAINN Ambassador Amid New Partnership to Deepen Public Understanding of Sexual Violence and Survivorship (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abbey White Plus Icon Abbey White Contributing Writer View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emmy Rossum Lelanie Foster Emmy Rossum has been named an ambassador for RAINN, the country’s largest anti-sexual violence organization, as the actress and nonprofit launch a new partnership focused on deepening the public’s understanding of sexual violence and survivorship. The Furious star will unite her platform as an artist and storyteller with the nonprofit’s expertise in survivor support to explore how storytelling can inform the public around the realities and misconceptions about sexual trauma and healing. The partnership aims to challenge stigma, amplify survivor voices, use storytelling to connect survivors with critical resources and encourage more thoughtful representations of sexual violence across the entertainment industry. Related Stories TV Newport Beach Film Fest: 'Furious' Star Emmy Rossum Will Receive TV Performance Award, Guest on Live Episode of 'Awards Chatter' Pod TV Why Emmy Rossum Says 'Shameless' Nude Scenes Affected Her Dating Life: "All These Preconceived Notions" “Working on Furious alongside psychologists and survivors reminded me that there is no perfect way to be a survivor,” Rossum says. “I’ve been so moved by the conversations the show has started. As we’ve seen too often of late, survivors are everywhere — from the halls of Congress to college campuses to the film industry — and this conversation belongs to all of us. Through my partnership with RAINN, I hope to turn that awareness into action: opening up conversations, breaking down stigma and helping more survivors find pathways to connection, support and healing.” The collaboration extends the connection to these issues that Rossum, among the nation’s more than 78 million survivors of sexual violence, developed while preparing for her critically acclaimed performance in Hulu’s Furious as Alice Black, an FBI agent and abuse survivor. While making the Elizabeth Meriwether-created series, production leaned on a community of consultants, including numerous survivors of sex trafficking, intimate partner violence experts, forensic psychologists, trauma therapists, FBI agents and human trafficking task force members. RAINN also served as a script consultant on the studio side during the show’s early development. “To tell these stories without re-traumatizing viewers, without explicitly showing the trauma, but instead, as Liz so cleverly did, showing the aftermath of the trauma, takes a lot of care,” the actress says. “What I’m most proud of in our show is how we demonstrated that survivors need not be innocent or likable to deserve dignity or justice. I think understanding the nuances of these crimes, understanding the struggles of survivors and how imperfect people still deserve the right to justice is important.” The announcement comes one day before Rossum will appear at Raising the Prevention Generation, an invite-only event for survivors, allies and advocates, co-hosted by WME and RAINN. The intimate brunch and sitdown in L.A. will feature Rossum; RAINN founder and president Scott Berkowitz; Jennifer Simmons Kaleba, RAINN vp, communications; Aspire Titan Academy student mental health therapist Skye Choe; and Dr. Karen Kay Imagawa, medical director of the Audrey Hepburn CARES Center at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles. The discussion will span how the adults in children’s lives can talk about sexual violence, consent and boundaries in a digital world and how everyone can turn current conversations into meaningful action. “One of the most meaningful parts of our work at WME is helping our clients turn what they care deeply about into real impact. Storytelling has an incredible power to change hearts, minds and perspectives, and Emmy’s commitment to using her voice with such care and purpose is a beautiful example of that,” says Jeanell English, head of community and impact at WME. “Together with RAINN’s decades of expertise, this partnership creates an opportunity to spark important conversations, challenge stigma and make a meaningful difference in how survivors are seen, heard and supported.” Friday’s talk will mark the first step in Rossum and RAINN’s newly minted alliance, which sprung out of a connection made during WME’s inaugural Women’s Health Summit, held in Los Angeles on Oct. 15. Rossum and RAINN chief of victim services Megan Cutter’s intimate fireside conversation “Furious? Good. Now What?” explored the ongoing myths and stereotypes that shape how sexual violence is perceived, the ways survivors respond to trauma and why survivor agency matters. “In recent weeks, calls to RAINN’s National Sexual Assault Hotline increased 73 percent,” Cutter says. “The country is having a hard and necessary conversation about sexual violence right now. Too often, what’s missing is an understanding of what survivors actually go through: that trauma responses vary, that there is no single right way to react and that healing looks different for everyone. Emmy and WME were committed to telling these stories with integrity long before this moment, and that’s what makes them the right partners to help carry this conversation forward.” The collaboration is particularly timely, arriving amid a moment flooded with national headlines and public discussions about sexual assault in the film and TV industry, on college campuses like Cornell University and the University of Chicago, as well as the campaign trail, in states like Maine, Ohio and Arizona. “ Cornell isn’t an outlier . It’s a reflection of what happens on campuses and in communities every day. The difference is that people are paying attention right now,” says Berkowitz. “[It] landed hard because it felt so real. The details differ, but for the tens of millions of Americans who’ve experienced sexual violence, this story was personal and for a lot of parents, it was a wake-up call. Nobody wants their kid to be a victim — or a perpetrator.” The partnership also comes nearly a decade after the #MeToo movement changed public discourse around sexual violence and how survivors are treated. In the years since, the movement has faced backlash and shifts in attention and momentum, but alongside the recent news about campus assaults, Rossum explains why addressing sexual assault must go beyond a moment. “#MeToo was an incredibly important watershed moment in culture. But all social movements require sustained action,” says Rossum. “Sunlight remains the best disinfectant. What happened at Cornell needs to be brought into the light . When our leaders foster a culture that threatens the safety of women, it needs to be called out directly and swiftly.” According to the actress and producer, the most impactful way she and her fellow creative community members can do that is by tackling the issues through storytelling. “There is something about taking the shame out of things by putting them on screen for us to see, warts and all. A character can reach us emotionally in a way that a PSA can’t. We aren’t just being told about something. We’re feeling it alongside someone, and that can change how we understand and treat each other,” she tells The Hollywood Reporter . “That’s the power of stories to me: It can take something that feels isolating and create a connection around it.” That’s why stories are at the forefront of her upcoming work with RAINN. “They can make us feel seen and less alone. That connection matters long after the headlines go away,” says Rossum. “No one was asking for Furious or Josephine or I May Destroy You or even Obsession , which sparked important conversations about consent. But audiences turned out because they’re phenomenal stories about something important. We need to keep telling them.” For RAINN, partnering with a storyteller like Rossum means the conversation around sexual assault, trauma and survivorship does not only have to live within a news cycle and “can reach people who’ve never thought of sexual violence as their issue and help keep this conversation going long after the headlines fade,” says Berkowitz. “The stakes of not talking about this are high. When people don’t understand consent, harm happens. When friends don’t know what to look for, they don’t step in. And when survivors don’t recognize what happened to them, or the people they confide in respond with doubt or blame, healing gets much harder,” he continues. “Sexual assault isn’t an abstract statistic. It’s happening to people we know and love and talking about it openly is how we prevent it and how we support survivors.” THR

articles.title: Robert Pattinson to Be Honored With American Cinematheque Award
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Robert Pattinson Stefanie Keenan Robert Pattinson is getting some special recognition after his very busy year. The star will be honored as the 40th recipient of the American Cinematheque Award, presented at the organization’s Beverly Hills gala on Feb. 9. In 2026 alone, Pattinson has starred in The Drama , The Odyssey , Primetime and the upcoming Dune: Part Three , and the evening will celebrate those as well as his wide-ranging two-decade career. “Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices, and remarkable versatility as an actor. From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling,” American Cinematheque board chair Rick Nicita said in a statement. “Rob is the perfect choice to receive this award and join our esteemed list of artists who not only love cinema but continue to have a deep impact on our industry. We are thrilled that his filming schedule has allowed us the opportunity to recognize his exceptional contributions to film and we look forward to celebrating his continued achievements.” Related Stories Movies Scarlett Johansson Breaks Silence on 'The Batman Part II' Role: "It Was Very Hard to Figure Out" Lifestyle Jon Bernthal Adds Another Notch on Packed 2026 Résumé by Fronting Fear of God Campaign Ryan Gosling was previously set to receive the American Cinematheque Award in a ceremony this month, but the event was rescheduled after Gosling was no longer available to accept it; Pattinson has also been busy this fall, filming The Batman Part II while taking part in the awards race. The American Cinematheque Awards Gala serves as an annual fundraiser for the nonprofit, supporting its year-round programming at the Aero Theatre in Santa Monica, Los Feliz 3 Theatre in Los Feliz and Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood. The American Cinematheque Award has previously been given to stars including Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington, Nicole Kidman, George Clooney and Michael B. Jordan. THR

articles.title: Chris Pratt Tapped for King of Comedy Award at 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chris Pratt CBS/Nickelodeon Chris Pratt has been tapped to receive the King of Comedy Award at the 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards on Nov. 14. The Guardians of the Galaxy and Parks and Recreation alum will receive the Silver Blimp statuette at the show, which is officially titled CBS Presents Nickelodeon Kids’ Choice Awards, in celebration of his career, “before facing Nickelodeon’s iconic slime,” according to the announcement. Pratt also might take home an Orange Blimp award that night as he is nominated for favorite male animated voice from a movie for his role as Mario in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. Related Stories TV Tony Awards to Air on CBS Through 2032 TV Alex Warren to Host Kids' Choice Awards, Airing on CBS for the First Time; Taylor Swift Leads Nominees Pratt next stars in Way of the Warrior Kid, an adaptation of Jocko Willink’s bestselling children’s novel that premieres Nov. 25 on Apple TV, which he also produced. “I’m incredibly honored to receive Nickelodeon’s King of Comedy Award,” Pratt said. “I spent most of my childhood trying to make people laugh to get out of trouble. Now apparently you can win awards for it. Pretty sweet deal. Comedy has always been a huge part of my life, and making people laugh is one of my favorite things in the world. Especially kids. I’m grateful to Nickelodeon and CBS for this honor. And if I get slimed, just know I’ll be sending them my dry-cleaning bill.” The 2026 KCAs will be hosted by Alex Warren . Musical performances and other celebrity appearances will be announced at a later date. Taylor Swift leads this year’s nominees with a total of six mentions, followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five apiece. Awards will be handed out across film, television, music, gaming, sports and other categories. Among the movies and series that are up for KCAs are The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Toy Story 5, Wednesday , Wicked: For Good , The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants, KPop Demon Hunters and Percy Jackson and the Olympians. In addition, producers this year have introduced three new categories: watch party: kids’ choice, favorite onscreen duo/trio and favorite clutch player of the year. The 2026 KCA ceremony will air on CBS for the first time as well as on Nickelodeon. It also will stream live on Paramount+ for Premium subscribers in the U.S., with on-demand viewing available the following day for Premium and Essential subscribers. The ceremony airs live from Television City in Los Angeles at 8-9:30 p.m. ET/5-6:30 p.m. PT. The KCAs are produced by Done + Dusted. THR

articles.title: AFM Hot Project: Jacob Tremblay, Kate McKinnon Join ‘I’m With Stupid’ (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jacob Tremblay, Kate McKinnon, Ego Nwodim, Chabely Ponce Jenna Berman, Alexandra Carillo-Vaccino, Oriana Layendecker Ego Nwodim and Chabely Ponce are set to star in I’m With Stupid , a high school comedy directed by Hannah Pearl Utt ( Cora Bora ). Upgrade is handling international sales on the project and will launch it to buyers at the upcoming American Film Market . Written by Carolina Barlow ( The Hawk ) and Peter Kelly ( Big Mouth ), the film follows a pair of directionless high school seniors from opposite ends of the social spectrum who are forced to work together to avoid the humiliation of failing senior year. Related Stories Movies Sony Pictures Classics Takes Jean-Pierre Jeunet's 'Violette' for U.S. Movies Suzanne Farwell's Starry Rom-Com 'Otherwise Engaged' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM (Exclusive) Tremblay ( Room , Wonder , Good Boys ) plays Noah, a senior with an opinion on everything but no motivation. Ponce ( Girl Group ) is Hadley, Noah’s wealthy classmate who discovers she may have interests beyond becoming a trophy wife. McKinnon ( Barbie , Ghostbusters ) will portray Principal Dunlap, the school’s deeply unpopular and increasingly vindictive administrator. Nwodim ( Return to You , Hoppers ) is Ms. Reed, the students’ unconventional English teacher, who becomes an unlikely ally in their fight to graduate. “I’m thrilled to make a movie that’s this funny but has this much heart, with my dream group of collaborators,” Utt said. Mallory Schwartz ( The Morning Show, Cora Bora ) and Jen Goyne Blake ( Joyland ) are producing. Jonathan Kier and Matt Brodlie are executive producing for Upgrade, alongside Christine D’Souza for After Hours, Marc Danon and Kyle Fox for Fox Global Capital and April Shih for Diversity Hire. “There’s a real appetite for smart, unapologetically funny comedies,” said Kier and Brodlie of Upgrade. “Hannah has a terrific ability to find genuine emotion in absurd situations, and with this exceptional ensemble, we believe I’m With Stupid has all the ingredients to become a new generation’s favorite high school comedy.” Production on I’m With Stupid is set for February/March of 2027, with Rich Delia overseeing casting. UTA Film Finance Group and After Hours are co-representing the film for domestic sales. THR

articles.title: Martin McDonagh to Receive Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (Exclusive)

The Film Awards will take place on Jan. 7, 2027, with the festival running from Jan. 7 to Jan. 18. “Martin McDonagh remains one of our most distinctive and original voices in cinema today,” Festival Chairman Nachhattar Singh Chandi says. “Over the course of his celebrated career, he has built a body of work that is humorous, timely and morally complex. Wild Horse Nine is another testament to his singular vision, and we are honored to recognize him and his extraordinary film with the Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award.” Related Stories Movies Milcho Manchevski's 'Sister Brother Manhole Cover' Wins Top Prize at Tokyo Film Fest TV Tony Awards to Air on CBS Through 2032 Wild Horse Nine stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as CIA agents who set out to Easter Island shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup to confront their dark pasts. Russell ( The Fighter ), Quentin Tarantino ( Once Upon a Time in Hollywood ) and Chloé Zhao ( Nomadland ). THR

articles.title: Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music
articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:09am PT Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music Former UTA and FaZe Clan leaders aim to shape representation for digital-native stars By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music 38 minutes ago UFC’s Event Sellout Spree Powers TKO Q3 Earnings 19 hours ago Jessica Alba Battled ‘Major Impostor Syndrome’ as She Built The Honest Company Into an Early Star-Led Business Success Story 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tyler Ash Gaming and digital media veterans Mike Lee and Darren Yan have joined together to launch ISO , a talent management firm that specializes in representing the hottest commodities in marketing and media these days: creators and livestreaming personalities. Based in Los Angeles, Lee and Yan have quietly been building ISO’s operations for about a year, with financial backing from Influence Media Partners, an investment banner that also focuses on digital-native content. The launch of the firm draws on Lee and Yan’s breadth of experience working across gaming, sponsorship and branding and artist development. The pair have also built extensive partnership and distribution connections for entertainment and media platforms across Asia including in China. Related Stories Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Lee, who was most recently head of gaming and livestreaming for UTA’s creators division, serves as co-founder and CEO of ISO. Yan, former chief talent officer at esports lifestyle firm FaZe Clan, serves as co-founder and head of music. ISO (which stands for In Search Of) at present has about 24 employees spread between Los Angeles, New York and Atlanta. The roster includes more than 90 livestreamers, gamers, artists, VTubers (aka livestreamers who use animated avatars) and lifestyle creators active in beauty, food and other highly engaged content verticals. Matt Alsberg, an alum of Sony’s PlayStation, Twitch and UTA, has signed on as ISO’s head of talent. “What we’re trying to build is something that is dedicated to the digital creator,” Lee tells Variety. Both founders have experience working at UTA and large-scale firms that are harnessing the heat of the next-generation stars of the attention economy. ISO was born out of Lee and Yan’s belief that talent representation firms have to operate very differently to support digital-native talent than they have for the past century in traditional film, TV and music. ISO’s roster at launch includes about 90 clients, including notable digital stars such as PlaqueBoyMax, Jasontheween, Ironmouse, Lacy, Vanillamace, Kyedae, jessechrisss, Angelo Marasigan, RDCWorld and more. ISO and its clients are alredy doing business with top-tier brands Electronic Arts, Discord, Underdog and Icenova, the ice cream brand known for its out-there shapes and flavors such as fried chicken. “If we really believe the next household name is going to come from the internet, then why aren’t all of our services optimized toward that internet star? We kept thinking, what if we were to actually blow everything up and we didn’t have an office and we weren’t spending millions of dollars on rent and theaters and showcases? Because our clients aren’t asking us for that,” Lee says. “There are no gatekeepers when it comes to digital media. It’s not four networks. It’s not seven channels. The gatekeepers are just the algorithms that feed your timelines. That’s what’s so incredible about working in this space.” Yan adds the pair’s proximity to explosive youth culture across Asia and in China, which has been an elusive market for so many U.S. firms, is a huge benefit to strategizing on where media and Gen Z and Gen Alpha consumption habits are headed. And it’s crucial for effective talent representation of digital dynamos. “For this generation, how they think and how they behave are not things are conditioned like a TV film actor or a sports athlete or even a music artist where they had to follow this specific pathway to success,” Yan tells Variety . “All of our clients are like, ‘Hey, we’re gonna break some eggs the way that we’re going to do it, and if you guys want to ride with us then you’re going to ride with us.’ That’s always been what we’ve always attached ourselves to. What they want when they look for partners or representation is who’s going to be able to move with us and say to our crazy ideas ‘This is possible.’ Because the talent that we work with will say, ‘Well, if it’s not you guys, then we’re going to do it ourselves. We don’t need a label, we don’t need a studio, we don’t need any of that. We have the money, we have the ingenuity, and whether or not you’re going to support us, we’re still going to build it and we’re going to win.’ ” Lee and Yan previously worked together at esports talent and marketing agencies Press X and Everyday Influencers, which were acquired by UTA in 2018. Lee and Yan then joined UTA. Yan exited UTA several years ago and was doing some consulting for Live Nation when he realized the opportunity to take popular live streamers on global tours, including in China. Yan and Lee have long-established relationships with local distribution partners that will go a long way toward helping talent make inroads in the world’s most populous country. Influence Media Partners is based in New York and specializes in developing and acquiring premium music and entertainment IP. Influence is supported by strategic partnerships with funds and accounts managed by private equity giant BlackRock. The interest in the digital native arena by one of the world’s biggest private equity firms is a sign of the times that Lee and Yan intend to capitalize on. ISO staffers gather to mark the company’s formal launch tyler ash “At Influence, we look to invest in partners who bring an innovative approach to the business of culture and entertainment. Mike, Darren and the team at ISO are reimagining talent representation for a creator economy that has fundamentally transformed how audiences are built, culture is shaped and revenue is generated,” said Lylette Pizarro, founder and co-managing partner of Influence Media Partners. “ISO’s playbook directly aligns with our values and investment philosophy, and we’re excited to support their growth.” The ISO founders see enormous opportunity ahead as the creator economy becomes more mainstream as a marketing and branding vehicle for the biggest brands (hence the interest in the arena from BlackRock). “We really have three pillars main pillars of the business: Talent driven by Mike’s team, our brand business and our music practice, which is artist management consulting,” Yan says. “With our digital native talent and with digital native advertising, we’re going to be able to bridge that gap [for marketers] and be able to drive and show more value. We were in the Twitch space 15 years ago. We’ve been fighting for experimental media budgets our entire careers,” Yan says. ISO has been established with what Lee and Yan call a policy of being “radically transparent” with their employees. The pair have developed a system of bonusing employees for success on a year-round basis, rather than doling out bonus coin once a year, with staffers receiving little information as to how the spoils were divided. The ISO founders also vow that in the effort to encourage collaboration and brainstorming among staffers, they have a formula for recognizing those contributions with bonus coin that comes out of the firm’s share of profits, not from the pool that goes to the primary representative. “The way we think about it is, every six months there is a new defecting faction out of some talent agency starting their own management company. And largely it is for very common reasons. The way we looked at it was, how do we prevent that from happening? How do we retain great talent, not just on our roster but our employees,” Lee says. “We don’t want to get to a point where we’re building this business with them, and then four or five years later they’re going to feel exactly how we felt, that we could own our own book of business and go somewhere else and make you know a lot more money that way. For us, we want to create an environment where [employees] feel like they can do that with a group of people that they trust. They’ll have stability but be making multiples of what they could make anywhere else.” (Pictured: ISO founders Darren Yan and Mike Lee) ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Bloodaxe’: Season 2 of Amazon Viking Drama Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand, Lasse Steen to Cast Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks ‘House of David’ to End With Season 3 at Amazon, Wonder Project ‘Things We Never Got Over’ Amazon Series Adds Six to Cast Loading comments...

articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:10am PT Rush Announces Sphere Residency in Las Vegas for Spring 2027 By Chris Willman Plus Icon Chris Willman Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic ChrisWillman Latest Rush Announces Sphere Residency in Las Vegas for Spring 2027 52 minutes ago The Chicks Recall ‘the Incident’ and Compare Bush to Trump in ‘Taking the Long Way’ 20th Anniversary Shows at L.A.’s Dolby: Concert Review 19 hours ago ‘Hunger Games’ Companion Album to Feature Jennifer Lawrence, Ella Langley, Tyler Childers, Mckenna Grace and 25 More 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Richard Sibbald The group Rush , which undertook a highly successful reunion tour this year, has announced a residency at Las Vegas’ Sphere for May 2027, with five dates set to take place under the banner of “Elevate From the Norm.” The 2027 Sphere shows are set for May 21, 23, 26, 28 and 30. Related Stories Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s 'Ramayana' Makers on Retelling India’s Epic for the World, as Amazon Music and T-Series Bet on A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer's Soundtrack Rhys Ifans on the ‘Frightening’ Task of Portraying Parkinson’s in ‘Onwards and Sideways’ and Learning to Wear ‘Costume’ of Disease: ‘I Really Did My Homework’ Singer-bassist Geddy Lee shared his thoughts about playing Sphere in an announcement statement. “When I first heard of Sphere, I thought to myself, ‘wow, what a shame that Rush is no longer touring, because this venue sounds tailor made for the kind of visual attitude with which we have always designed our shows.’ Normally we spend months designing the visual effects for our shows and this scenario seemed like the cherry on top of the ice cream for our design team. Gonna be so much fun.” It’s typical for any Sphere residency to stay in place for much longer than five dates, with additional shows being added indefinitely as the first ones sell out. That seems likely to be the case with Rush, as just five shows would amount to more of a mini-residency by Sphere standards. Most acts who play Sphere do it well apart from any standard touring plans, but Rush’s opening in Las Vegas will fairly quickly follow the wrap-up of their international dates in April. The group is currently still in the midst of a North American tour that will continue through Dec. 17. On Jan. 15, starting in Buenos Aires, they embark on an international leg that seems them touring steadily through what is currently scheduled to be a tour close on April 10 in Helsinki.
