articles.title: Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:30am PT Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) 32 minutes ago Rhys Ifans on the ‘Frightening’ Task of Portraying Parkinson’s in ‘Onwards and Sideways’ and Learning to Wear ‘Costume’ of Disease: ‘I Really Did My Homework’ 2 hours ago ‘Rings of Power’ Star Eddie Marsan on Playing a Power-Hungry Dwarf and Why He Once Had 2,000 Pairs of Orlando Bloom’s Elf Ears in His Attic 3 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ashley Randall Wunmi Mosaku , the Oscar-nominated and BAFTA-winning star of Ryan Coogler’s 2025 hit “Sinners,” has come aboard British documentary short “Swim Sistas” as executive producer. The film, celebrating Black women’s relationship with swimming, was directed by Catherine Joy White (“Bridgerton,” “Fifty-Four Days”), with Naomie Harris (“Moonlight”) narrating. After premiering at DOC NYC and winning several awards on the festival circuit, it has now qualified for the 99th Academy Awards. Related Stories Sky News Stands by Journalist Following Heated Exchange With Abdul El-Sayed: 'We're Proud of Our Correspondent, Who Was Doing His Job' Lady Gaga, Jack White, Boy George Lead Songwriters Hall of Fame 2027 Nominees “The story of our relationship with swimming and water has so much depth and history, complexity that is so beautifully captured by ‘Swim Sistas,'” said Mosaku. “This powerful film and its themes speak personally to me, as I know it does many others, and I could not be more excited to join as executive producer. I believe ‘Swim Sistas’ will not only move people, but change how they see the world, and I’m proud to help its message reach a wider audience, and support its next chapter.” Featuring four Black British women, “Swim Sista” follows Alice Dearing, Great Britain’s first Black female Olympic swimmer; professional rugby player and “The Traitors” contestant Jasmine Boatswain; teenage athlete Lexie Sandiford; and Roni Bruno, who learned to swim at the age of 54. Through their stories, the documentary explores what it says are the “barriers, histories and joy that shape Black women’s relationships with water.” Featuring original poetry written by White, the film sees Harris voice Mami Wata, a central poetic figure embodying “ancestral strength and hope for the future.” “Wunmi is a stunning talent. Her work carries such depth and humanity and to have her join forces with ‘Swim Sistas’ brings another dimension to a world that has always been about so much more than swimming,” said White. “We’re honoured to have Wunmi on this journey with us as we continue to elevate Black women’s voices and reshape the story of who water is for.” Added Afua Hirsch and Amandla Crichlow, executive producers and founders of Born in Me Productions: “Wunmi Mosaku is an actor of such skill and grace, who represents the beauty and power of Black women in a way that has truly universal resonance. We could not be more proud to have her as a partner on ‘Swim Sistas.’” The attachment of Mosaku — also a BAFTA TV award winner for “Damilola, Our Loved Boy” — comes as the filmmakers behind “Swim Sistas” develop plans to expand the project into a documentary series exploring Black women’s relationships with water across the U.S., the Caribbean and Africa. Also joining the film’s executive producing team alongside Mosaku is BAFTA-nominated executive producer Ash Horne (“Marion,” “The Second Time Around”). “Growing up, swimming was something I always took for granted. It was simply part of being a kid and I never really questioned that privilege. So, when I learned that 97% of Black adults and around 80% of Black children in England don’t swim regularly, it really struck me,” said Horne. “‘Swim Sistas’ is a beautiful, heartfelt and important documentary that shines a light on this disparity while celebrating community and the joy of swimming. Catherine Joy White has created something genuinely moving, and I’m incredibly proud to support the film and help bring this conversation to a wider audience.” Originally announced in Variety , “Swim Sistas” has since screened at more than 50 festivals worldwide. Its accolades include best documentary at Women X, a BAFTA- and BIFA-qualifying festival, and the jury’s choice award at the Thomas Edison Film Festival, an Oscar-qualifying festival. The film has also enjoyed a 26-cinema theatrical run, screened at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., and opened special screenings of “The Little Mermaid” and “The Shape of Water.” It was featured at the inaugural United Nations Swimmable Cities Summit in Rotterdam and is being incorporated into the French national curriculum. “Swim Sistas” is produced by Oriane Pick and Anaïs Ferrato of BAFTA-nominated Candid Broads Productions, with executive producers Hirsch (“Enslaved,” “Africa Rising”) and Crichlow (“Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul”) of Born in Me Productions, alongside White’s Forbes 30 Under 30 company Kusini Productions. ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon Remi Wolf on the Meaning Behind Her New Album ‘Mud,’ Her ‘Off Campus’ Cameo and Friendship with Hayley Williams ‘House of David’ to End With Season 3 at Amazon, Wonder Project Loading comments...

articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:48am PT The Weeknd Breaks Record for Highest-Grossing Tour by a Male Artist With $1.3 Billion By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Lady Gaga, Jack White, Boy George Lead Songwriters Hall of Fame 2027 Nominees 48 minutes ago Music Industry Moves: Jackson Wang Inks With WME; Position Music Signs Arkai to JV With Lindsey Stirling’s Label 1 day ago Justin Timberlake to Release Four-Part ‘Tell-All’ Docuseries, Featuring Janet Jackson, on Apple (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Co The Weeknd has broken the record for the highest-grossing tour by a male artist in history as his “After Hours Til Dawn” stadium tour wrapped with a final performance at TM Stadium National in Kuala Lumpur, bringing the final gross to over $1.3 billion. While there is no official touring chart analogous to Luminate (for recorded music), the tally, confirmed by tour promoter Live Nation, is the third-largest in history, surpassed only by Taylor Swift’s “Eras” tour (over $2 billion) and Coldplay’s “Music of the Spheres” (over $1.5 billion). The previous male artist record was held by Elton John’s “Farewell Yellow Brick Road” tour, with over $939 million. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues The finale concluded the Weeknd’s 17-date stadium tour across Asia this fall. articles.title: How ‘Frontline’ Turned Into an Oscar-Winning Documentary Juggernaut
articles.full_text: Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT How ‘Frontline’ Turned Into an Oscar-Winning Documentary Juggernaut Under Raney Aronson-Rath, the decades-old PBS doc series has started winning Oscars (“20 Days in Mariupol”) and appealing to younger generations online. By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest Judi Dench Tells All About Bond: It Was Daniel Craig’s Idea to ‘Have Me Killed’ 2 days ago Spike Lee Is Praying the Knicks Don’t Visit the Trump White House 3 days ago John Oliver Reviews ‘You Can See Everything’: Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans Are ‘Complete Lunatics’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source PBS/Frontline This year’s documentary Oscar race will pit a cringe comedy maestro against the most decorated documentary film producer of the past decade. While plenty of ink has been spilled over Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s form-shattering Elizabeth Holmes curio “You Can See Everything,” it would be a mistake to count out Raney Aronson-Rath. Aronson-Rath has been at the helm of “ Frontline ,” PBS ’ acclaimed investigative documentary series, since 2015. Under her watch, the program has won so many Emmys she’s lost count (it stands at 44) and launches around 20 documentaries a year. In 2024, it took home its first documentary Oscar for “20 Days in Mariupol,” a vivid and violent account of AP journalist Mstyslav Chernov and his colleagues’ time in the Ukrainian city as it withstood Russia’s invasion in early 2022. Related Stories 'Married at First Sight' U.K. Canceled by Channel 4 Following Sexual Assault Allegations Awkwafina's ‘Kate Might Die,’ ‘Outside of Cleveland’ With Alex Wolff Among Projects Selected for U.S. in Progress A few days after Chernov and his team escaped Mariupol with their footage, he and Aronson-Rath got to work on the film. “‘ 20 Days in Mariupol ’ was my debut film. [Raney] and the ‘Frontline’ team helped me practically and creatively transition from journalism to cinema, which is quite a challenge,” Chernov says, adding, “For many of us who are working on socially and politically relevant projects but cannot find a home and distributor, Raney is the last hope to get the film made and find its audience.” Oscar night was “a surreal moment” for Aronson-Rath. “People kept asking me, ‘Are you going to do more of these?!” she recalls. The common refrain was that “Frontline” couldn’t do theatrical films, and then one day it hit her: “I realized I was in charge of ‘Frontline,’ and we had the funding and distribution, so why not?” Aronson-Rath launched Frontline Features last November as a dedicated studio that premieres feature and short-form documentaries in festivals and theaters ahead of PBS airings. Its latest release is “One in a Million,” a feature doc from Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes that follows an 11-year-old girl, Israa, over 10 years as she and her family flee war-torn Syria to Turkey before settling in Germany. A powerful examination of war, immigration and the ties that bind, the film won the Audience Award at this year’s Sundance Film Festival and is poised to earn an Oscar nomination. “I was there from the very beginning. They sent me raw footage of Israa when she was 10 years old,” explains Aronson-Rath, a producer on the film. “I had a feeling that Israa’s story was going to be amazing.” On top of Aronson-Rath’s “extraordinary passion and professionalism,” Azzam is grateful that Frontline gave the project the benefit of time: “We were following real people going through major changes in their lives, which required patience, trust and a willingness to embrace uncertainty, and having that long-term commitment was essential,” explains Azzam. “Raney was always there with her unwavering belief in the film and her understanding that this wasn’t simply a story about refugees reaching Europe, but about what happens afterward: growing up in exile, searching for belonging and navigating identity.” Frontline also lent valuable “editorial experience,” Azzam maintains. Aronson-Rath’s team typically assigns investigative reporters to aid projects, conduct deep legal reviews and analyze rushes to make sure they meet their editorial standards. Aronson-Rath caught the journalism bug writing for The China Post, an English-language newspaper for expats in Taipei, after graduating from the University of Wisconsin. While attending the Columbia Journalism School, she caught a screening of Steve James’ 1994 documentary “Hoop Dreams” at Film Forum in downtown Manhattan. “It was a really transcendent moment for me,” she remembers. “I’d found the form that I love.” Years later, Aronson-Rath worked closely with James on “Abacus: Small Enough to Jail,” about a family-owned bank in Manhattan’s Chinatown that was the only financial institution to face criminal charges following the 2008 financial crisis; the doc earned “Frontline” its first Oscar nomination in 2018. “Public television has for decades tried to broaden its appeal to younger audiences, often without success,” says James. “From the day Raney took over, it was clear that she wanted to find more innovative ways to tell powerful true stories.” Frontline has, under Aronson-Rath, proven intensely popular among younger generations. Its YouTube channel has 4.8 million subscribers — eclipsing 1 billion views in July with an astonishing 422 million hours watched. It also has three features lined up for 2027, including Chernov’s next film, which Aronson-Rath will be producing. “One of the others is a film I’ve been working on for 20 years with a filmmaker named Dan Edge,” she shares, “focusing on one character we met two decades ago who came back from Iraq.” She flashes a grin. “I love a longitudinal, epic story.” ‘House of David’ to End With Season 3 at Amazon, Wonder Project ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Bloodaxe’: Season 2 of Amazon Viking Drama Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand, Lasse Steen to Cast ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon ‘Rose Hill’ Amazon Series Adds Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Dune’ Launches Arrakis-Inspired Press-On Nail Collection With Glamnetic
articles.full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. The world of “ Dune ” is getting the beauty treatment. Ahead of the Dec. 18 release of “Dune: Part Three,” Glamnetic has teamed up with Warner Bros. on a limited-edition collection of press-on nails inspired by the sci-fi franchise, marking its first foray into the beauty category. Launching Nov. 5, the limited-edition Glamnetic x Dune collection features nine nail sets drawing on the films’ characters, mythology and distinctive visual world, from the glowing blue eyes of the Fremen to the giant sandworms that roam Arrakis. The partnership marks the franchise’s first beauty collaboration, according to Glamnetic, with prices ranging from $21.99 to $23.99. Related Stories Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault in London Trial; Taken Into Custody ‘Bad Day’ Trailer: Cameron Diaz Is a Single Mom Who Accidentally Robs a Bank in Netflix Comedy Among the designs is “Spice Melange” ($21.99), featuring a translucent burnt-amber finish outlined in fine gold, inspired by the precious substance at the center of Frank Herbert’s fictional universe. “Eyes of Ibad” ($21.99) takes its cues from the Fremen’s signature blue-in-blue eyes, with iridescent cobalt chrome and an aurora-like shimmer. LIMITED-EDITION Dune x Glamnetic Collection shop now “The Maker” ($23.99) pays tribute to the franchise’s colossal sandworms through sculpted gold, amber and ridged chocolate-brown detailing, complete with a cobalt stone accent. “Reverend Mother” ($23.99) features a more elaborate combination of multicolored jewels, gold chrome, smoky mauve and black-and-gold detailing, while “Chip & Shatter” ($23.99) pairs a milky cream base with textured, crackled gold foil. The collection is the latest entertainment-inspired launch from Glamnetic, which has previously released licensed nail sets celebrating “Harry Potter,” including designs inspired by Hogwarts houses, the Marauder’s Map and the Deathly Hallows. The brand has also expanded into sports merchandise through a partnership with Fanatics, offering team-branded manicures featuring official NFL, NBA, MLB and other league logos and colors. The launch comes just over a month before “Dune: Part Three” arrives in theaters Dec. 18, bringing Villeneuve’s blockbuster trilogy to a close. The upcoming Warner Bros. and Legendary film draws from Herbert’s 1969 novel “Dune Messiah” and takes place nearly two decades after Paul Atreides’ rise to power, following the consequences of his reign as emperor and the growing threats to his rule. Timothée Chalamet and Zendaya return as Paul Atreides and Chani, alongside Florence Pugh, Anya Taylor-Joy, Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem and Jason Momoa. Robert Pattinson joins the franchise as Scytale, a central figure in the conspiracy against Paul. Villeneuve directs from a screenplay co-written with Brian K. Vaughan. The franchise has already proved fertile ground for unconventional merchandise partnerships. Ahead of 2024’s “Dune: Part Two,” watchmaker Hamilton collaborated with the filmmakers to create a futuristic wrist device worn in the film, subsequently releasing two limited-edition Ventura watches inspired by the prop. Chalamet also worked with Cartier on a custom necklace for the film’s London premiere, featuring roughly 900 gemstones in desert-inspired shades of amber, orange and blue. The Glamnetic collection offers a considerably more affordable entry point into the world of Arrakis, arriving just in time for the franchise’s theatrical finale and the holiday shopping season. The Glamnetic x Dune collection will be available beginning Nov. 5. Loading comments...

articles.title: Robert Pattinson to Receive 40th American Cinematheque Award
articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT Robert Pattinson to Receive 40th American Cinematheque Award By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest Pixar Names Jonathan Garson as President; Jim Morris Moves to Emeritus Role 16 hours ago Neve Campbell Confirms Return for ‘Scream 8’ 3 days ago ‘X-Men’: ‘Hunger Games’ Actor Ben Wang Circling Iceman Role in Marvel’s Reboot 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Stefanie Keenan Robert Pattinson will be honored as the 40th recipient of the American Cinematheque Award. Pattinson receives the award in celebration of his own two-decade career, in which he’s established himself as one of the most versatile actors of his generation. The actor will be feted on Feb. 9, 2027, at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills. “Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices and remarkable versatility as an actor,” American Cinematheque board chair Rick Nicita stated, announcing Pattinson’s selection. “From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling.” Related Stories Rhys Ifans on the ‘Frightening’ Task of Portraying Parkinson’s in ‘Onwards and Sideways’ and Learning to Wear ‘Costume’ of Disease: ‘I Really Did My Homework’ Clio Barnard's 'I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning' Bought by Kino Lorber for North America (EXCLUSIVE) In 2026 alone, Pattinson starred opposite Zendaya in the dark romance “The Drama”; played the villainous Atinuous in Christopher Nolan’s epic “The Odyssey” and portrayed “To Catch a Predator” journalist Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” which also marked the debut film from Pattinson’s production company Icki Eneo Arlo. He wraps up the year as a shape-shifting assassin in Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three.” Pattinson is currently in production on Matt Reeves’ “The Batman: Part II,” reprising his role as Batman/Bruce Wayne in the sequel to the blockbuster superhero movie. That level of dexterity is par for the course for Pattinson, who has curated a career that spotlights his range as a performer. The actor’s filmography spans his breakout roles in the “Twilight” and “Harry Potter” franchises to more eclectic fare like Robert Eggers’ “The Lighthouse”; “Good Time,” from Josh and Benny Safdie; Bong Joon Ho’s “Mickey 17”; “Die, My Love” with Jennifer Lawrence; and Nolan’s “Tenet.” “Rob is the perfect choice to receive this award and join our esteemed list of artists who not only love cinema but continue to have a deep impact on our industry,” Nicita continued. “We are thrilled that his filming schedule has allowed us the opportunity to recognize his exceptional contributions to film and we look forward to celebrating his continued achievements.” Pattinson joins a distinguished group of honorees including Michael B. Jordan (last year’s recipient and the eventual best actor Oscar winner), Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington (Pattinson’s co-star in the upcoming film “The Take”), Nicole Kidman and George Clooney, among others. To note, Ryan Gosling was previously selected to receive the 40th American Cinematheque award. But when the “Project Hail Mary” star had a scheduling conflict with the gala (originally set for Nov. 2), the event was postponed to 2027. articles.title: How Grimes’ Cameo in Theater-Bound AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Came Together (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT How Grimes’ Cameo in Theater-Bound AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Came Together (EXCLUSIVE) By Corbin Bolies Plus Icon Corbin Bolies Latest Scarlett Johansson Says ‘The Batman 2’ Role Was ‘Very Hard to Figure Out’: ‘It Gave Me a Lot of Existential Angst’ 19 hours ago Meta to Help Bring ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to 3D Screens — and Its $1,299 VR Glasses 3 days ago Utopai Studios Names Former Disney AI Leader Hans Ku as Chief Product Officer 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fable Even in the AI era, there’s still no better way to reach a favorite artist than by sliding into their DMs. Zack London, who directed the upcoming AI film “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” under his moniker Gossip Goblin, had long been a fan of Grimes , the moniker of 38-year-old experimental pop artist Claire Boucher. But he didn’t necessarily expect that love to be mutual, not until he noticed she had followed his X account and started engaging with his videos. Related Stories South International Series Festival Prizes: ’Blindspot Berlin,’ ‘The Oligarch and the Art Dealer’ Win Big 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Spins Up Massive Numbers for Sony's Quarterly Earnings Then in March, Boucher replied to clips shared on Gossip Goblin’s X account. London responded , offering her a role in a project of his. Sensing an opportunity, he then sent Grimes a direct message just expressing how much he loved her music. “We started chatting, and it was like, ‘Oh, we know a ton of the same people,’” he tells Variety last month over lunch in Chelsea, coming off several prerelease screenings of the AI film. “She was like, ‘I would love to do something with you.’ And then, it was basically, ‘Well, I wish I knew that earlier, but let’s find a way for you to be in this.’” The fruit of those DMs will bear next month in Boucher’s minuteslong cameo in “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the first AI feature set to debut in theaters. Boucher plays “Zaynith Alda” in one of the early sequences in the post-apocalyptic film, which aims to satirize humanity’s relationship with technology. Alda, a brash, demanding aristocrat who hails from the rich Halvorith family, seeks a “dreamspool” an illicit, induced experience in the world of “NiiroCradle” that lets people experience alternate realities. Boucher’s cameo — and that of YouTuber and Logan Paul pal Mike Majlak, who also makes a brief appearance — injects a dash of celebrity into the bold ambitions of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the R-rated sci-fi film trying to barrel its way past society’s aversion to AI films and into the best animated feature category at the Oscars. Fable, the AI studio behind the film, has leaned in, setting a Times Square marketing campaign featuring Boucher’s appearance. Fable The studio also hosted screenings targeting animation voting bloc members of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences across New York and Los Angeles ahead of its Dec. 4 debut, eager to try and assuage the Academy’s concerns about all things AI and urge them to consider the gory film among the likes of the critically acclaimed “Wildwood” and “Toy Story 5.” (Variety’s “Awards Circuit” does not list “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” among the Academy’s potential contenders.) “You only need to see Grimes’ brilliant performance in the film to understand how much things are about to change for animated movies,” Fable CEO Edward Saatchi said in a bullish statement. “We hope the Academy will recognize that a film that is seminal (the first AI film), wildly technically novel and (most importantly) good deserves a nomination.” Boucher declined an interview request. Her spokesperson, Mitchell Jackson, said in a statement that Boucher “appreciates indie artists using new tools to create independent art—especially in the age of big studio monopolies.” “She was particularly impressed that they had such a large team and were involving and compensating so many artists, voice actors, and musicians,” her spokesperson said. “She believes in supporting the right kind of culture around AI in cinema rather than acquiescing to the current model of having no standards.” The Zaynith Alda character was already written into the film’s nearly two-hour runtime, but Boucher’s appearance forced London and his co-writer Jacob Batchelor to adapt the role around her persona. That meant giving her the chance to help design the character, including a mechanical-looking mask that adorns Alda’s face, and nixing the British accent native to the rest of the film’s world. Once those were set, a multi-continent team of London in Stockholm, his editor and sound engineer in Romania, and Boucher and her producer in LA worked together to record her lines from her home. Is there a recording anywhere of Boucher attempting a British accent? “If there are, they’re on a hard drive somewhere,” London says. Boucher is also one of the highest-profile examples of a celebrity authorizing their likeness for an AI project, following examples such as UFC fighters in Higgsfield’s “Cully Hill Boys” and “The View” co-host Sunny Hostin licensing her image and novels to Fountain 0 to make AI adaptations — featuring her likeness — of her books. It’s a testament to celebrities’ slow embrace of AI in culture, including everything from Ben Affleck’s Netflix-owned InterPositive startup for AI tools to actors like Michael Caine licensing his voice to the AI audio firm ElevenLabs. Others, however, remain fearful that AI could exploit their likenesses without permission or compensation . It helps that Boucher has long championed AI. In 2023, she launched an AI software program called “Elf.Tech,” where fans could use her vocal likeness in their tracks so long as she received 50% of the master recording royalties, and in a 2024 PBS interview called AI an “opportunity” for artists that, with democratized access to professional tools, could see “actual talent, like, really rise to the top.” For this film, London says Boucher authorized her license for free and refused to be paid, a fact her spokesperson confirmed. “She said, ‘You guys are scrappy, just put that money towards the other actors [and] your film,’” London says, calling Boucher part of “a different class of artists that look at the big picture of what are you doing, what is the holistic statement surrounding, and not getting hung up on the process.” Watch a clip of Boucher’s appearance below: ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Reacher’ Renewed for Season 6 Ahead of Season 5 Premiere ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Toy Story 5’ Writer-Director Andrew Stanton Wants To Bring Nuance To The Conversation Between Kids & Technology
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny ‘Planted!’ Game Dev Ben Cawthorne On Digging Up Chaos In A Competitive Gardening Game ‘Tenzing’s Jennifer Peedom On Bringing The Everest Pioneer’s Story To Life — Deadline Screening Series Taraji P. Henson Encourages Artists To ‘Knock Down’ Walls, Sarah Finn Celebrates Casting Community & More At 2026 Newport Beach Film Festival Honors View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar For the better part of three decades, Woody ( Tom Hanks ), Buzz ( Tim Allen ), and the gang have kept audiences company through the ups and downs of growing up. Now, Toy Story 5 finds the franchise entering a new chapter, with Jessie ( Joan Cusack ) taking center stage and technology changing the way children play. Co-writer and co-director Andrew Stanton helps usher in a new group of characters: Lilypad (Greta Lee), a frog-framed tablet, and Blaze (Mykal-Michelle Harris), a confident young girl who marches to the beat of her own drum. Alongside the familiar faces, the new toys bring fresh possibilities to a story that still has plenty to say about childhood and the evolution of social connection. Below, Stanton talks to Deadline about developing another entry, digging deeper into Jessie’s backstory, and the cherry on top of the cake: Taylor Swift’s new pop-country single, “I Knew It, I Knew You.” Related Stories Executives Pixar Veteran Jim Morris Moving To Emeritus Position As Jonathan Garson Named New President News Disney To Undergo More Layoffs With Divisions Eyeing Up To 20% In Cost Savings DEADLINE: How did you and co-screenwriter Kenna Harris decide which new characters would join the story? And how did that ultimately influence the direction of the film? Watch on Deadline ANDREW STANTON: There are unsaid expectations with every Toy Story movie now that we’ve had several installments. I think audiences, even unconsciously, expect to meet somebody new along the way and add to the cast. We bemoan that because the cast is already so huge. I always say I have so many mouths to feed, and if I gave everybody one line, the movie would be over in one scene. So we not only have to be judicious about who we add, but also about who we let go of and who we push to the background. By the time we’re doing five, you’re thinking there may be more. I don’t get too caught up in worrying about everybody getting their fair share of time. I just let the needs of the story dictate things. Right from the get-go, I knew I wanted it to be about Jessie, and I wanted a device to represent technology coming in. That dictated Lilypad right away. In this world, I don’t buy that TVs and phones can just talk to you. There has to be something, character-wise, built in to bring them to life in the same way Forky was in Toy Story 4 . So making a frog frame around an iPad was something I came up with very early on, when I was writing by myself. Even in the first draft, I was concerned I was late to the party on this issue, given that technology has been around kids and their toys for at least 10 or 15 years. It’s only gotten more advanced and smarter, and social media and all that stuff have come in more recently. I also started thinking about those early technology toys. We all have these devices, even the computers on our desks, and they change every three to five years. They get upgraded to something else. I thought about the short life those devices have. There’s always that drawer in my house with spare batteries, rubber bands, and cords you don’t know what they’re for. When my kids were little in the 2000s, it started having things like fun calculators for kids. You don’t know how long to keep that stuff. I thought, what a horrible existence for the first generation of tech toys to go through, being played with by kids and then discarded. That was pretty early on, too. It was about creating characters to represent that first generation of technology. The story dictated the new cast. I’ve also just never grown up. Body humor still cracks me up. I was amazed to find out there hadn’t been a toilet-training toy of any sort in the history of toys. I thought, “Well, let’s introduce one and see where that goes.” Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar DEADLINE: Outside of your own experience, what did other research look like? Did you all happen to talk to other children or parents about how they interact with toys and technology? STANTON: Eventually we did. I’m a little superstitious about knowing the world’s rules or people’s opinions too soon because it starts to influence things. I like to be free to roam about the cabin any way I want for a while. I know there are going to be many years of debating this, many more voices coming in, and many more people weighing in, all meaning well. But there’s this rare window of about a year where it’s just mine, and I get to go, “Where does my mind go?” I have strong opinions based on observing children and not seeing toys played with by older kids. It just seemed to me that the window was getting younger and shorter, that little kids were playing with toys for less time. I remember playing with toys, and some of that was because I had younger siblings. I played all the way up until I was 10. That was really what I wanted to explore from an entertainment and narrative standpoint: What is that doing to the characters we’ve come to know and love over these generations when they’re just getting less time with a child? That was enough to play with for a while. But eventually, we did our own research because we have a lot of young parents who work at Pixar . We didn’t have to go outside the walls to find a large group of people sharing their frustrations and concerns about their children being introduced to technology, when they should be, and how every kid was different. It was nice to know that it was messy. Kenna and I didn’t want to make it a black-and-white binary where this was bad, and this was good, because that’s never good drama. It’s always good drama when it’s in the gray, and it’s messy. You can see the reason why you’re introducing it, and it’s not going away. Some kids are different from others. That made for really good exploration. There are upsides, otherwise, people wouldn’t be tempted to use technology. Kids are shy. Kids live in communities where there might not be anybody like them in terms of their interests, disabilities, or abilities, and suddenly they can reach other people they wouldn’t otherwise reach. Andrew Stanton DEADLINE: I think that’s one of the things that really works about the film. It doesn’t feel preachy, and it would have been easy to lean one way or the other, especially when discussing technology and how children interact with it. How did you find that balance? STANTON: It would be so easy if it were a story about technology just being bad because then nobody would do it. Everybody wants their kid to have these experiences. There are upsides, otherwise, people wouldn’t be tempted to use technology. Kids are shy. Kids live in communities where there might not be anybody like them in terms of their interests, disabilities, or abilities, and suddenly they can reach other people they wouldn’t otherwise reach. As a kid, before there was all this technology, all I wanted was to have a can and a string so I could still talk to my best friend way down the street. That impulse is in us as natural human beings and as kids. The idea of having a secret clubhouse where you can say hi to your friend, with all those innocent needs, is understandable. Technology is also so involved in how our world functions. We want our kids to know how to operate in the world. It does some cool stuff, and we all played games. We were part of the gaming culture. As ’80s kids, we all ran to the arcades. TV was always around, and everybody thought it was going to rot our brains. Maybe it did, but we all did it [laughs]. It’s complicated, and that’s what makes it interesting. The thing I cherish about growing up before all this stuff was how much boredom gave me the skills to enjoy being in my own head. That was something nobody could take away from me. I hate the thought of my kids having less access to that, of having less of that full experience. It’s like the difference between the joy of reading and making up the whole thing in your head versus seeing a movie where it’s all been decided for you. Those are gifts in life that you realize the older you get, and you hate the idea that anybody coming into the world might be shortchanged. We realized that it isn’t about technology itself. It’s a choice. It’s a choice to turn off the TV, it’s a choice to turn off the device, and it’s a choice in how you use it. That’s where we realized the universal truth. I didn’t want anybody to look at any of the movies we make, let alone the Toy Story movies, 10 or 20 years from now and feel they were so dated that they couldn’t relate to them anymore. We’ve always tried to be in the grandparent business. What we used to say is that we’re not just trying to get kids to watch our movies. We want you to like them and have them touch you in a universal and human way so much that, even as a grandparent, you go, “I have to make sure my grandkids watch this particular movie. It was one of my favorites.” Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar DEADLINE: I enjoyed the film’s new visual style, especially the imaginative playtime sketches. Talk about that aesthetic. STANTON: It seems really obvious now that we found it. We just wanted something that felt handcrafted, kid-conjured, and had an improvisational feel. It had to feel like make-believe in your head, or even when you’re vocally pretending with your friend. You’re allowed to pivot mid-sentence, and suddenly they’re all vampires [laughs]. We wanted to figure out how to make it feel like that visually. It’s sort of like theater, where a spotlight can suddenly come on, something new appears, something is removed, and you’re open-minded to the rules changing at any moment. We compared it to trying to invent a new color. Everybody pictured something a little different. But “ephemeral” and “temporal” were the words that kept coming up. So there was the chalky feel, the fact that things faded off, and the sense of a dream, where your focus was wherever things locked in, but everything else could change. Mood, color, and everything could shift. That childlike illustration-book feeling, but theatrical, was ultimately what we found. DEADLINE: Looking back at the previous Toy Story movies and thinking about Andy, we didn’t focus on his friend group too much outside the house. So, it was cool to me that Bonnie has Blaze as a companion for her. When did she come into the picture? STANTON: The friendship direction of Bonnie making a new friend evolved throughout the making of the story. In the early days, we just wanted Jessie to go to her old address, have it be rural and farm-like, and have new owners. That was it. There wasn’t going to be any connection with Bonnie and the girl who lived there. So we had free rein to ask, “Who should be there?” We wanted to make it a bit more mixed and culturally diverse, and make it feel like how the world looks to us, both emotionally and culturally. Also, [there was a desire of the animators] to conquer curly hair really badly. They wanted to do it right because the technology had changed even since Brave . So, Blaze was thought up by Kenna and [conceptualized by the art team], and we loved it. Then the character started telling us something [as we developed the story]. We worked hard to make sure Bonnie felt different, both race-wise and, more importantly, girl-wise. She wasn’t the trope of a little girl. She was a little left of center. She thought in vibrant, random ways, and she was special. But she’s shy and not brave enough socially to expose that. That’s very common for any kid: showing the real you. But Blaze is the one who does that. We thought about having Bonnie find her tribe in a person who can understand how her mind works. We thought, what if Blaze was the shining example of confidence in that kind of thinking and also being a little left of center? She was just one year older, and when you’re that young, one year older is the coolest club to be in, to be hanging out with. We became enamored with her as a character, and she quickly became the model for somebody Bonnie could connect with, admire, and be friends with, if we could just get them to meet. That ultimately turned the whole story around. The universal thing that will make this movie speak to you 10 or 20 years from now, nostalgically, is when you find that kid who doesn’t think exactly like you, but you complement each other just right. As you get older, you realize that’s one of the most valuable things you find in your life, whether you meet them in college, at a young age, or even later. Those are the things you value most. Suddenly, it became a very priceless story. DEADLINE: You mentioned that the film initially started as a Jessie-centric story. Was there ever a version of the script where Jessie was reunited with Emily, or was that always something you knew you wanted to avoid? STANTON: There was. We just knew there was power in closing that wound for her, so we didn’t know how to go about it. I did the most obvious thing in my first draft. We hid the address from the audience. It was only seen by Bullseye on the back of Jessie’s chaps, and we would always have Bullseye nudge her chaps, thinking he just wanted something like a dog. Without getting into the long plot, it became a third-act moment where he finally brought her to what she thought was Bullseye’s home, only to find out he had brought her to the address on the back of her chaps. We revealed it at the last second, and she suddenly got to witness Grandma Emily playing with her granddaughter, the baby. It was very moving, but it took a lot of mountain-moving to get there. We knew the feeling we had captured for Jessie was something to aspire to and find another way to get to, which ultimately resulted in the finished movie. We worked hard to make sure Bonnie felt different, both race-wise and, more importantly, girl-wise. She wasn’t the trope of a little girl. She was a little left of center. She thought in vibrant, random ways, and she was special. Andrew Stanton DEADLINE: I have to say, one of the things I really loved was Buzz’s relationship with Jessie. When you think about the history of Toy Story and how Buzz has always been so tough, brave, and confident, I left the theater thinking he’s a total “wife guy.” He’s completely smitten with Jessie. STANTON: Is that a term, or is that your own term? I’ve never heard that term. DEADLINE: It’s a term on the internet, so I can’t take credit for it. If a guy is really into his wife or girlfriend, you say he’s a wife guy. STANTON: I’m stealing that. But to get to your point. Nobody even questioned his behavior for five seconds. We always knew Buzz had a big heart. DEADLINE: So he’s always been a softie? Was that the idea behind the dynamic? STANTON: At least for Jessie. I think we all know there’s that person who does that to us. I don’t think he’s like that for anyone else, but I do buy Buzz when he kisses Jessie. I loved the role reversal. Jessie just doesn’t seem like the kind who’s going to lift her leg during a kiss, and neither does Buzz, but I do buy Buzz’s foot pop when he kisses Jessie. There was never even a debate that I can remember. We had spent so much time with him, like a best friend, that we thought, “Well, all bets are off on how he’s going to act when Jessie is in the room.” Jessie, I think, has always been the lead in their dancing pair. She’s always known what effect she has on him and has been gracious enough not to rub it in or squander it. She enjoys it. She enjoys playing that flirtatious game. She knows she can get Buzz’s attention and obedience without much effort, and I don’t think she ever abuses it. Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar DEADLINE: Lastly, when did Taylor Swift come into the picture? Were you involved in those conversations, and did you know where her song would fit into the movie? STANTON: To this day, it’s a pinch-me moment. I can’t believe it happened, and I can’t believe how it happened. We reached out through the proper channels about a year and a half before the movie’s release, not knowing she was deep into her Eras Tour and didn’t have the time. I didn’t even know if word got to her beyond her brother [Austin Swift] at that point. But eventually, Taylor had circled back around to our request, and as her brother tells it, she was excited, saying how much she loved the Toy Story movies. So she saw the movie at a private screening, and we got a FaceTime straight from the theater with her and her brother on the phone, and she said, “I want to do the song.” And we couldn’t believe it. It came together pretty quickly and even involved a FaceTime from Bob Iger, who was standing with Taylor Swift in the studio, telling me the song was great. She had gotten him out of his house and made him drive down to the studio [laughs]. When [“I Knew It, I Knew You”] was placed in the film, and I had heard it, it felt like kismet. It felt like Jessie’s voice. It still blows me away that it happened and that it happened the way it did. articles.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Max Goldbart , Jake Kanter November 5, 2026 6:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Russell Brand has been found guilty of rape. After two days of deliberations, the jury at London’s Southwark Crown Court delivered a verdict on seven sexual offense charges, finding the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was found not guilty on two other counts of rape and one of attempted indecent assault, which was reduced from indecent assault during the trial. Brand firmly denied all the charges, based on allegations made by six women . The charges and verdicts are detailed below. Related Stories News Russell Brand Trial: Jury Begins Verdict Deliberations News Russell Brand's Defense Argues Channel 4 Film "Poisoned Well Of Justice Deliberately" Judge Mr Justice Bennathan told Brand that he would be given a “custodial sentence of some length,” and he was remanded in custody until sentencing on Monday. A rape conviction can carry a sentence of life in prison in the UK. Watch on Deadline The verdicts were read out to silence in the courtroom after the judge told those present not to react to the jury’s decisions. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began around a month ago. It was initially anticipated to take at least six weeks but has taken less than four. Within minutes of the verdicts, BBC News reported that Brand was being investigated over further rape allegations made by two women. The Metropolitan Police said its investigation “remains ongoing.” Outside the Courthouse, the detective superintendent in the case, Andy Furphy, said Brand “used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women.” “As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement.,” he added. “I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be.” Over the past month, the court has heard from all the accusers, who have a lifelong right to anonymity. Deadline can report, however, that three of the complainants that Brand was found guilty of sexually assaulting worked in the TV and radio industry, including former employees of MTV and Channel 4. All accusers came forward after seeing allegations about Brand in a Channel 4 documentary in 2023 and reading about him in The Times. Brand’s defense argued that this documentary “poisoned the well of justice deliberately” and “fundamentally corrupted” his accusers, while having a “truly devastating effect” on Brand’s life. The prosecution said the exposé was not a “magic force” that caused six separate women to “recast” their memories, but that it had caused them to come forward and tell stories about their encounters with Brand that had “haunted them for years.” The allegations stretched from 1999 to 2009, a period that saw Brand go from being an unknown actor to, in his own words, “staggering fame” after he started dating superstar Katy Perry. Charge 1, Complainant 1: Rape Complainant 1 alleged that she was raped by Russell Brand after meeting him on the fringes of the Labour Party Conference in 1999. C1 invited Brand back to her hotel room and alleged that he pushed her onto the bed and raped her. Brand, who was not famous in 1999, argued that the encounter was consensual. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 2, Complainant 2: Attempted Indecent Assault Complainant 2, a former MTV employee, accused Brand of attempting to pull her into a toilet at the network’s London offices in 2001. During the trial, judge Mr Justice Bennathan reduced the charge from indecent assault to attempted indecent assault because there was “insufficient evidence” to support the original count. Brand’s defense was that he did not recall the incident, but denied that he attempted any non-consensual assault. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 3, Complainant 3: Sexual Assault Complainant 3 alleged that Brand “lunged and squeezed” her breasts within minutes of their first meeting in 2004 while attending the birthday party of a TV producer at London’s Nordic Bar. Brand denied sexually assaulting Complainant 3, who worked at MTV at the time. Verdict : Guilty Charge 4, Complainant 3: Rape Complainant 3 alleged that Brand grabbed her arm and dragged her into the toilets of the Nordic Bar. The woman claimed that Brand climbed onto the toilet seat, exposed himself, forced his penis in her mouth, and ejaculated. In his defense, Brand argued that Complainant 3 willingly accompanied him to the toilet, where they had a “kiss and a cuddle.” He denied orally raping the woman. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 5, Complainant 4: Sexual Assault Complainant 4 alleged that she was sexually assaulted by Brand at a radio station in 2004 or 2005. She claimed that Brand “grabbed” her, pushed her up against a wall, and kissed her “sloppily and aggressively.” Brand denied the incident. Verdict : Guilty Charge 6, Complainant 5: Rape Complainant 5 alleged that she was anally raped by Brand at his London home in 2009 days after meeting him backstage at his stand-up show, where she gave him consensual oral sex. Complainant 5 said they had consensual vaginal sex at his home,efore alleging that Brand turned her on all fours and unexpectedly penetrated her anally, removing his condom. Brand said the anal intercourse was consensual. Verdict : Guilty Charge 7, Complainant 6: Sexual Assault A former Channel 4 employee, Complainant 6 alleged that Brand demanded a massage and put his head into the area of her genitals during a workplace incident in 2009. Brand told the court that he could not recall the incident. articles.title: Final Chapter Of ‘Mass Effect’ Studio BioWare To Be Told In Super Channel Feature Doc From Fennessey Films and Score G Productions
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse JioStar’s Alok Jain On Reality TV Competition, Building Indian Formats & The End Of ‘Koffee With Karan’ ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Propels Sony Pictures To Huge Q2 Profit Boost Bri Lee’s Novel ‘The Work’ Set For TV Adaptation At Dollhouse Pictures View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Massive Effect: The Bioware Story' Fennessey Films/Score G Productions EXCLUSIVE: The final days of legendary video games studio BioWare will be told in a doc from Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie for Canada ‘s Super Channel . Massive Effect: The BioWare Story will document how the Edmonton, Canada-based games company grew from being founded in 1995 by three medical doctors – Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip – to selling 100 million copies of its role-playing games, which include Mass Effect , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , Dragon Age and Baldur’s Gate . Written and directed by Akash Sherman ( Clara ) and co-produced by Canada’s Fennessey Films and Score G Productions , the film has a unique insight into the story, with filming beginning two years before Electronic Arts announced the closure of BioWare on October 21 last month and continuing to lens throughout. Related Stories News Titan1Studios Adapting Stephen R. Bown's 'The Company: The Rise and Fall Of The Hudson's Bay Empire' As Historical Drama Series News European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members This allowed the filmmakers to capture BioWare’s finale chapter, as the news of the studio’s closure reverberated through the gaming industry. EA decided to shutter studio, which was known for its complex narratives and world building, after recent releases underperformed, and 400 jobs were cut. Watch on Deadline Muzyka, Zeschuk and Yip will feature in the film, along with a plethora of major players from the video game world. These include Douglas Reilly, Vice President of Lucasfilm Games; John Riccitiello, former CEO of Electronic Arts; Casey Hudson, game director of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect ; Geoff Keighley, creator of The Game Awards; Victor Lucas, creator of The Electric Playground ; voice actor Jennifer Hale; and longtime BioWare developers Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. “When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved,” said BioWare co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk in a statement. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.” A website has also been set up for the BioWare community to share photos, videos and how the company touched their lives for the chance to appear in the film. “BioWare’s fans have been part of its journey since the very first game,” said Scorgie. “It’s only right that they help us tell the rest of the story.” “The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes,” added writer and director Sherman. “It’s a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio’s recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction.” Canada’s Super Channel commissioned the doc, which is being planned for a major film festival run and a world premiere next year. Jhod Cardinal of Upstream Flix is handling worldwide sales. The Canada Media Fund supported production. “We are thrilled to bring Massive Effect: The BioWare Story to Canadian audiences,” said Kim Ball, EVP Content & Communications for Super Channel. “As an Edmonton-based company, we’re especially proud to celebrate BioWare’s extraordinary hometown story and the people, creativity and groundbreaking storytelling behind some of the most beloved games of a generation.” Producers Fennessey Films and Score G are behind the likes of Funny Money: The Dane Cook Story , Dolph: Unbreakable , Inmate #1: The Rise of Danny Trejo , Breaking Olympia , Singhs in the Ring and The Great Ones . articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Sony Pictures Classics Takes Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s ‘Violette’ Pixar Veteran Jim Morris Moving To Emeritus Position As Jonathan Garson Named New President ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stomping To $60M+ WW Opening, Posts Massive First Day In Japan; Will ‘Ramayana’ Upset The Lizard? – Box Office Preview View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sony Pictures Classics Sony Pictures Classics has acquired Jean-Pierre Jeunet ‘s Violette in the U.S., Latin America and Southeast Asia repping the distributor’s fourth collaboration with the French filmmaker after Amelie, The City of Lost Children and Micmacs. Violette stars Leïla Bekhti ( Once Upon My Mother, Maria Montessori ), Matthias Schoenaerts ( Rust and Bone, The Danish Girl ) and Melvil Poupaud ( Jeanne du Barry, One Fine Morning ). Based on the international bestseller Fresh Water for Flowers, Violette follows a cemetery caretaker whose peaceful life is thrown off course when a mysterious stranger shows up on her doorstep compelling her to confront her troubled past filled with hidden truths. Published in 2018 by Albin Michel in France and in 2020 by Europa Editions in the US, Fresh Water for Flowers was an instant bestseller, winning the Maison de la Presse Prize and Paperback Readers Prize. Jeunet adapted with Guillaume Laurant. The movie was produced by Mediawan’s 24 25 Films and Palomar. Related Stories Acquisitions Chase Infiniti-Starring 'The Julia Set' Acquired By Sony Pictures Classics After TIFF Premiere Acquisitions Andy Garcia's Cannes Premiere 'Diamond' Acquired By Sony Pictures Classics Jeunet said, “Valérie Perrin, the author of this magnificent novel, said: ‘I wrote it, Jean-Pierre will paint it.’” Watch on Deadline Sony Pictures Classics added, “Jean-Pierre Jeunet has a singular gift for weaving together multiple storylines with humor, pathos and that unmistakable touch of whimsy that has made films from The City of Lost Children and Amelie such magical and enduring experiences. Having shared that journey with Jean-Pierre on The City of Lost Children, Amelie and Micmacs , we’re especially delighted that Violette marks our fourth film together. It continues his lyrical tradition while also feeling completely fresh, and theatrical audiences will be enchanted by his vision of Valérie Perrin’s beloved bestselling novel Fresh Water for Flowers .” The deal was negotiated between Sony Pictures Classics and StudioCanal. Amelie was nominated for five Oscars including Best Foreign Language Film and Original Screenplay for Jeunet. With $33.2M at the domestic box office, Amelie released in 2001 remains the highest grossing French language movie in U.S./Canada. articles.title: ‘Off Campus’ Gets Season 2 Release Date On Prime Video, Confirms Returning Cast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Scrubs’ Star Sarah Chalke On J.D. & Elliot’s Big Reveal & Surprise Twist, Sean & Charlie’s Quick Exit, Ollie’s Arrival & What Comes Next ‘Red, White & Royal Blue’ Author Responds To Texas Going Blue In Midterms: “It Was All In The Binder” Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among Options Explored Post-Merger – The Dish View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Off Campus' Prime Video Great news for Off Campus fans — the hugely popular Prime Video college soap will be back sooner than many expected, with Season 2 set to premiere on April 28, 2027. That is less than a year after the May 13 release of Season 1, a very rare gap of under 12 months for a streaming series and one of the smallest on record. Related Stories News 2026-27 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery The quick turnaround for Off Campus , created by Louisa Levy based on author Elle Kennedy’s best-selling Off Campus Universe, was helped by the early Season 2 renewal in February , three months ahead of the Season 1 debut. It is set to meet a global demand for the series which, six months after Season 1 was released, remains among Prime Video’s Top 10 most viewed series worldwide, most recently at #6 for the week of Oct. 26. Off Campus ‘ staying power followed a red-hot launch, with Season 1 reaching 36 million viewers through its first 12 days to mark the third most-viewed debut season of any series in Prime Video history overall and most-viewed ever among Women 18-34. Watch on Deadline Off Campus follows an elite ice hockey team, and the women in their lives, as they grapple with love, heartbreak, and self-discovery — forging deep friendships and enduring bonds while navigating the complexities that come with transitioning into adulthood. As announced in May , Season 2 will center on the romance between Allie Hayes (Mika Abdalla) and Dean Di Laurentis (Stephen Kalyn) from The Mistake book in Kennedy’s series. Stephen Kalyn & Mika Abdalla in ‘Off Campus’ Prime Video Along with the premiere date announcement, Amazon has confirmed the cast for Season 2. As expected, coming back is the entire Season 1 series regular cast except Josh Heuston who had a one-season arc as Hannah’s (Ella Bright) crush. Those returning include Abdalla, Kalyn, Season 1 couple Belmont Cameli (Garrett) and Bright (Hannah), as well as the other two hockey players who will get their own love stories, Antonio Cipriano (John Logan) and Jalen Thomas Brooks (John Tucker). They are joined by new series regular India Fowler who will play John Logan’s romantic interest Grace Ivers. From the Season 1 recurring cast, returning are Julia Sarah-Stone as Jules, John Logan’s younger nonbinary sibling who runs the Briar gossip account; Khobe Clarke as Beau Maxwell, Dean’s friend and brother of Joanna Maxwell; and Miles Gutierrez-Riley as Hannah’s friend Dexter. They are joined by new recurring cast member Philipa Soo as Scarlett, a theatre artist who is guest directing an original play at the college’s drama department. Guest starring in Season 2 are Charlie Evans, who was introduced late in Season 1 as Dean’s high school hockey rival Hunter Davenport, and new addition Shay Rudolph as Dean’s younger sister Summer . Among those not listed for Season 2 are Chad Willett, who played Coach Jensen, the head coach of the Briar Hawks, in Season 1; Steve Howey, who recurred as Garrett’s abusive father Phil; and Chelah Horsdal as Hannah’s mother Carrie. Levy co-showruns and executive produces Off Campus with Gina Fattore. Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen and James Seidman executive produce and Annika Patton co-executive produces for Temple Hill. articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie ‘Traveller’s Hell’ Trailer: Hana Alomair’s MBC-Backed Female-Driven Thriller Breaks Fresh Ground For Saudi Cinema Makers Of Croatian-Serbian Hit ‘The Wedding’ Talk Navigating Regional Differences, Remake Interest & Sequel ‘Cinghiale’ Horror Picture With Richard Armitrage, Britt Robertson & Quelin Sepulveda Begins Filming in Tuscany View All November 5, 2026 8:46am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Francis Kaufmann Bogus U.S. film producer Francis Charles Kaufmann has been found guilty of murdering his partner and their 11-month daughter by an Italian court and sentenced to life in prison, with three years of solitary confinement. The sentence comes some 18 months after the discovery of the lifeless bodies of his partner, 28-year-old Russian national Anastasia Trofimova and their 11-month-old Andromeda in Rome’s Villa Pamphili park on June 7, 2025. Local investigators took days to establish the victims’ identities and then connect them to Kaufmann, who was travelling under the false identity of a film producer and director named Rexal Ford. During his closing argument, defense lawyer Paolo Foti requested that Kaufmann be acquitted of both charges on the grounds that there was not enough hard evidence to prove his client committed the murders. The verdict and sentence was delivered by eight judges at Italy’s highest criminal court, the prima Corte d’Assise, in Rome. articles.title: Liberty Media Acquires John Malone’s Super Voting Stock After Founder Received Outside Offers
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill ‘The Odyssey’ Powers Record Q3 For Imax, Stock Jumps, CEO On Platform’s “Power And Potential” Resurgent Box Office Drives AMC Theatres’ Record Q3; CEO Says Chain Has Finally Recovered Snap Swings To Profit As SPECS Set To Roll Out; Stock Takes A Hit View All November 5, 2026 8:49am Add us as a Google Preferred Source John Malone at Paley Center in NYC Courtesy of The Paley Center for Media Liberty Media has acquired all shares of super voting Series B common stock held by founder John Malone in exchange for low and no-vote shares. The swap came after Malone received a number of unsolicited offers from third parties for his stake, the company said, at which point “Dr. Malone and Liberty Media began discussing a transaction in which Liberty Media would instead acquire such shares.” The move knocks the financier’s voting power in Liberty down from 48% to 3%, and no holder of Liberty Media common stock now holds more than 9% of voting power. Malone, who founded the company in 1999, will step down as chairman emeritus but remain a senior advisor. Liberty’s investments have shifted over the years with Formula 1 and Moto GP its main assets currently. Related Stories News John Malone Says Trump Administration Told Netflix They Had "No Chance" Of Getting Regulatory Greenlight For Merger With Warner Bros. Discovery Executives Elon Musk & Larry Ellison Will Join Forces To Boost Both Starlink And Skydance, John Malone Predicts The deal better aligns “John’s voting power with his economic ownership of Liberty Media while avoiding the potential transfer of a significant voting position in Liberty Media to a third party in a transaction in which other Liberty Media shareholders would not participate,” said Chase Carey, chair of a Special Committee Liberty convened to explore the transaction. Watch on Deadline Liberty CEO Derek Chang declined to give any details around the offers when asked on a call with analysts after the company’s quarterly earnings. “I continue to have great confidence in Liberty Media’s management team and fully support them and Liberty Media’s strategy,” said Malone in a statement. “The Transaction allows me to increase my economic ownership of Liberty Media while distributing voting power more broadly among Liberty Media’s other shareholders.” Board chair Robert Bennett said it simplifies Liberty’s capital structure “and will give us flexibility as we enter our next chapter … We look forward to continuing to benefit from John’s counsel for years to come.” In specifically laying out the transaction benefits, Liberty said it will “reduce the ability of the Malone Holders or successors thereof to exercise significant influence over matters submitted to Liberty Media’s shareholders for a vote … and eliminate the risk that the Malone Holders’ significant voting power could be transferred to a third party in a transaction in which other Liberty Media shareholders do not participate; and potentially broaden the institutional investor base in Liberty Media’s shares.” For good measure, Liberty also authorized a rights plan through November of 2027 to “promote stability” after the transaction. The move makes it harder for any person or group to acquire a significant voting position or obtain control in the company without board involvement. articles.title: ‘The Bend In The River’ Trailer: In Robb Moss Oscar Contender, Friends Reunite For Possibly Final Journey Down The Colorado
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Meryl Streep On How Fellow Oscar Winner Introduced Her To ‘My Undesirable Friends’ Documentary: “I Was Just Absolutely Entranced’ Magnolia Pictures To Qualify ‘Just Look Up’ For Oscars; Documentary Examines Climate Activist (And Standup Comedian) Michael Greenberg Doc Talk Podcast: Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival’s Ken Jacobson On State Of Nonfiction Filmmaking, Competitive Oscar Race And More View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: One of the most acclaimed documentaries of the year – nearly 50 years in the making – arrives on Netflix December 4. The Bend in the River , the Oscar-contending film directed by Robb Moss , marks the culmination of a cinematic project that began in the late 1970s with Riverdogs , which documented a rafting trip that Moss took with his friends down the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon. Those friends were in their 20s at the time, carefree and often clothing-free as they enjoyed life with the vitality and insouciance of youth. Moss documented another rafting trip with those friends in 2003’s The Same River Twice , his chums then in middle age. The new film finds the group rafting again, as river currents and the progress of time draw them closer to old age. Related Stories News Matthew McConaughey In 'The Rivals Of Amziah King'; Green Day-Inspired Road Trip Comedy 'Nimrods' -- Specialty Preview Documentary In 'The Bend In The River,' Friends Head Down The Colorado Again On Cinematic Journey Stretching Back Over 45 Years - Doc Stories Watch the trailer for the film above. Third River Films “The film interweaves moments from the distant past with those of the recent present,” notes a release, “taking viewers back-and-forth through time and inviting personal reflections on the inexorable flow of aging and the unfinished project of living.” In addition to his work as a filmmaker, Moss has taught film at Harvard University for over 30 years. Among his former students: Lance Oppenheim ( You Can See Everything ), two-time Oscar nominee Joshua Oppenheimer, Oscar nominees Yance Ford, RaMell Ross, and multiple Emmy nominee and Sundance Film Festival award winner Lauren Greenfield. Some extraordinary collaborators worked with Moss on The Bend in the River, including producers Lisa Remington (Oscar winner for The Only Girl in the Orchestra ) and Kristin Feeley, director of the Sundance Institute’s Documentary Film and Artist Programs. The film’s executive producers include Oscar winners Frances McDormand and Joel Coen as well as Oscar-winning producers Shane Boris ( Navalny ) and Jeff Reichert ( American Factory ). Moss received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Woods Hole Film Festival in Massachusetts. The Bend in the River earned the Artistic Vision Award at the Big Sky Documentary Film Festival in Montana and it won two awards at DOC LA, including Best Documentary and Best Editing, the latter award recognizing the work of Jeff Malmberg. It is set to screen at DOC NYC on November 12 after making that festival’s shortlist of the year’s best feature documentaries (DOC NYC calls it “a masterful meditation on the eternal, the temporal and the inevitable.”). Barry Wasserman stands behind an image of his younger self in ‘The Bend in the River’ Third River Films The Bend in the River screened at the 2025 edition of Doc Stories in San Francisco. At a Q&A there, Moss spoke about his approach to the filmmaking. “It’s not really built out of biography, ‘This happened and that happened,’” Moss said. “People had extraordinary lives, biographically, that aren’t in the film. And it seemed when there were scenes like that that had too much biography, it’s like the film flattened. But the whole thing had to move more… the dynamic of something going downstream. It just had to keep bouncing forward even as it went backwards and forwards. The beginning of the piece had to be very clear what we were up to, that there were going to be multiple timeframes. [But] there’s no saying there’s multiple films, there’s no saying there’s multiple timeframes, there’s no dates, timestamps, there’s no voiceover, there’s no music to cover up cuts.” Watch the trailer for The Bend in the River above. It just got better. Pattison will be the recipient of the 40th American Cinematheque Award, a milestone celebration taking place February 9, 2027 at the Beverly Hilton. Related Stories Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Tonys, Guilds & More Below The Line Hollywood Music In Media Awards Nominations: ‘Michael,’ ‘The Odyssey’ & More With a career spanning more than two decades, Pattinson has established himself as one of the most distinctive actors of his generation, moving seamlessly between independent cinema and major studio productions. In 2026, Pattinson’s versatility was showcased when he starred in no less than four films, all so vastly different from one another that the only commonality between them was him. From a happily engaged turned spiraling groom opposite Zendaya in A24’s darkly funny The Drama to the playfully villainous Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster The Odyssey to his critically acclaimed portrayal of journalist Chris Hansen in the psychological thriller, Primetime to a shapeshifting ‘Face Dancer’ assassin in the upcoming Dune: Part Three , Pattinson’s range has been on full display. Pattinson is currently in production on Matt Reeves’s The Batman Part II , the sequel to 2022’s highly successful The Batman . Watch on Deadline PRIMETIME, Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen, 2026. © A24 / Courtesy Everett Collection American Cinematheque Board Chair Rick Nicita announced the selection by stating, “Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices, and remarkable versatility as an actor. From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling. Rob is the perfect choice to receive this award and join our esteemed list of artists who not only love cinema but continue to have a deep impact on our industry. We are thrilled that his filming schedule has allowed us the opportunity to recognize his exceptional contributions to film and we look forward to celebrating his continued achievements.” In 2025, Pattinson starred in and executive produced Die, My Love , alongside Jennifer Lawrence. Additionally, Pattinson starred in Bong Joon Ho’s Mickey 17 , with Steven Yeun, Naomi Ackie and Toni Collette. Other notable credits include Christopher Nolan’s Tenet , Robert Eggers’ The Lighthouse , opposite Willem Dafoe, and Josh and Benny Safdie’s Good Time . Robert Pattinson is Antinous in ‘The Odyssey’ Universal Pattinson gained industry attention at 19 years of age when he joined the Harry Potter franchise in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and is also known worldwide for The Twilight Saga . For four decades, the prestigious American Cinematheque Award has been designed to recognize extraordinary artists whose talent, vision, and contributions have made a lasting impact on cinema. Their passion and filmography not only exemplify excellence in filmmaking but also reflect the cinematic artistry and breadth of American Cinematheque’s programming, which bridges film history to its future and celebrates the theatrical experience. The award has celebrated an impressive roster of filmmakers and performers, including among others Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington, Nicole Kidman, George Clooney, and last year Michael B. Jordan who received the honor before going on to win the Best Actor Academy Award. The 40th Annual American Cinematheque Award Gala will be executive produced by Rick Nicita of RPMedia, along with Madelyn Hammond and Javier Infante of Hammond Infante Productions. It serves as an annual fundraiser for the non-profit organization, supporting its year-round programming at the Aero Theatre in Santa Monica, Los Feliz 3 Theatre in Los Feliz, and Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood.
