articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Mike Johnson To Step Down From House Republican Leadership After Democrats’ Blowout Victories In The Midterms Midterm Elections: Amid The Blue Tsunami, A Night Of Many Firsts Nithya Raman & Karen Bass In Dead Heat As L.A. Mayor Vote Counting Continues In Nailbiter Election View All November 4, 2026 6:50am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: New Hampshire Democratic Senator-elect Chris Pappas, Michigan Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, Georgia Democratic Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms and Senator-elect James Talarico Getty Images Democrats won up and down the ballot in the midterms , and votes are still being counted on what could ultimately be a 75-seat House majority and 54 or more seats in the Senate. There also were many firsts, reflecting the party’s diverse coalition that helped them score victories even in deeply red states. Related Stories Politics Midterm Elections: Mike Johnson To Step Down From House Republican Leadership After Democrats’ Blowout Victories Politics Hollywood Celebrates Midterm Results: “The Blue Wave Made Landfall, And Now The Red Wedding Begins,” Says Jimmy Kimmel Among them: The first Black woman governor Keisha Lance Bottoms , the former mayor of Atlanta, won a sizable victory over Republican Rick Jackson. In her victory speech, she recalled visiting the grave of her great-great grandmother, who was born in 1845, 20 years before emancipation. “I know I am standing on shoulders made of steel,” she said. The first openly gay man elected to the U.S. Senate Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH) won election to the U.S. Senate in New Hampshire by a significant margin defeating Republican John E. Sununu. “Win, lose or draw, I am the luckiest guy because I am married to a man I love,” Pappas said in his victory speech after embracing his husband. Watch on Deadline The first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate Abdul El-Sayed emerged the winner after a race filled with drama — including national attention to primary rival Haley Stevens’ endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in the race’s final days. In his victory speech, El-Sayed noted that it would be JD Vance who would be swearing him in in January. Vance characterized him as an extremist and Trump called him a jihadist. “Donald, I know you struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator,” El-Sayed said.

articles.title: Trudie Styler Talks Journey To Directing ‘Up Against It’ & ‘The Reception’ Back-To-Back: “I’m In A Happy Place”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie WTFilms Boards Italian Alps-Set Comedy-Thriller ‘The Dregs’ With Maddie Phillips & Stephen Lang – AFM Tinto Brass Dies: Italian ‘Caligula’ Director Was 93 Pierfrancesco Favino First Look In Marco Bellocchio’s Sergio Marchionne Bio-Pic ‘Falcon’ Unveiled – AFM View All November 4, 2026 7:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Trudie Styler on the London Underground with cinematographer Dante Spinotti during the shoot of Up Against It Andrew Cooper Trudie Styler arrives at the London offices of Maven Screen Media , her joint production company with Celine Rattray , bearing gifts: bottles of organic extra virgin olive oil. Featuring Styler and husband Sting ’s names on the label, they are the last of a batch made from the 2025 olive harvest at Villa Il Palagio, their beloved 16th Century estate in Tuscany. She is not here to talk about her long love affair with Italy, however, but rather back-to-back directorial feature film credits Up Against It and The Reception as well as her and Rattray’s commitment to championing female-driven storytelling. Related Stories News Jean-Claude Van Damme Returning To Martial Arts Roots In Yakuza Action Pic 'Katana' For Jeremy Zag & The Veterans -- AFM News Chris Jericho To Star In Creature Horror 'I Am The Teeth', Epic Launches Sales For AFM London-set romantic comedy Up Against It stars Antonio Banderas and Eva Birthistle as warring divorced couple Alvaro and Saffron, who are forced to reconnect when their only daughter Rose is struck down with cancer, an illness she had previously battled as an infant but has no memory of. It received a buzzy world premiere in Toronto. Watch on Deadline The Reception , revolving around a chaotic wedding party and featuring Jeff Daniels, Guy Pearce, Sabrina Impacciatore in the cast , is on the cusp of shooting in Scotland when this interview takes place, with cameras now rolling since late October. The features, being sold by Beta Cinema at the upcoming AFM , mark the latest chapter in a producing and directing career that began in the early 1990s when then actress Styler came to the conclusion that combining motherhood and repertory theatre or being on set was going to be a tall order, especially with Sting on the road touring. “I decided to give acting a pause,” she says, revealing that she called Oscar-winning Chariots of Fire producer David Putnam for advice. “I said, ‘Could we have a meeting, because I want to know something about being a producer, and if I’ve got it in me to be one, and if you think I’ve got it in me to be one’,” she recounts. “He was my great mentor in how to be a producer and getting IP… he described it as putting pans on stoves,” she says. “It wasn’t a bad concept… it was sort of like when there’s a bit of heat around one project, keep the others simmering, but really go all in for the one that is showing some heat.” Her first producer credit was 1993 documentary Boys from Brazil , sparked by Styler seeing Brazilian transvestites working as prostitutes in the Bois de Boulogne in Paris and then wondering about their back stories. She tapped John-Paul Davidson to direct. The pair met during a trip to the Amazon in the early days of the Rainforest Fund which Styler co-founded in 1988 with Sting to protect rainforests and their indigenous people. The resulting work would air as part of the BBC’s now defunct documentary Under the Sun strand. “It got like about 5.5 million people, which I was told was a good number, although it I got castigated by the fourth estate for making something in such poor taste,” says Styler. Davidson would go on to direct and produce the travel shows of Micheal Palin and Stephen Fry, while the fund has since raised more than $45 million for 300 indigenous driven projects across three continents. Her next project Moving The Mountain , was directed by Michael Apted (then fresh off 35 Up ) and took its title and cue from a book by exiled Chinese student leader Li Lu chronicling China’s 1989 pro-democracy protests and their brutal ending with the Tiananmen Square Massacre. He had been introduced to Styler by a friend shortly after his arrival in the U.S. in late 1989 after escaping China where he was wanted by the authorities. “I met him that winter and he’s been in my life ever since,” recounts Styler. “Now he has a big hedge fund company.” She enlisted Apted as a director after bumping into him on a flight on the way to New Orleans to join Sting in the city. “I said, ‘Oh, coincidence!’ And he said, ‘No, I’ve actually come to see your husband about a project’… I said, ‘Ah well, can I talk to you about my project’,” she recounts. Styler remains banned from China to this day due to the film, which played a raft of festivals including the Berlinale and won an IDA award. She would go on to produce a dozen documentary and fiction features under her Xingu Films banner, named after Xingu Park in Brazil, before going on to launch Maven with Rattray in 2011. Styler also earned kudos for her championing of emerging directors, with Xingu Films getting behind Guy Ritchie ’s 1998 breakout first feature Lock Stock and Two Smoking Barrels and follow-up Snatch (2000), as well as Duncan Jones’ Bafta-winning debut Moon (2009), for which she was also Bafta nominated, among others. She recalls being approached by Ritchie’s then rookie producer Matthew Vaughn , who knocked on the door of her home out of the blue. “Matthew had the native wit and charm and the brain to be able to manifest pretty much what he wanted. He said, ‘I want you to meet Guy. He wants to meet you. By the way, you know his father’, and I was like ‘I do?’” She discovered that Guy Ritchie’s father is John Ritchie, the advertising exec known for producing the iconic “Happiness a cigar called Hamlet” ads, who she had convinced to create a campaign for the Rainforest Fund. “When I met Guy, he asked, ‘So what did you think of my script?’ I replied, ‘Even if I thought it was really stupid, I would have done this to help you because your dad helped me’,” recalls Styler, suggesting that what Vaughn and Ritchie lacked in experience they made up for in chutzpah. “It was a seminal moment… those young bloods were going to do it no matter what.” Xingu’s filmography also includes Styler’s feature directorial credit on the 2002 documentary Sweatbox , co-directed with Davidson, going behind the scenes at the Walt Disney studios and the making of the animation The Emperor’s New Groove at Disney, in which Sting was involved as chief songwriter. Styler would break into fiction feature directing in 2018 with Freak Show, an adaptation of James St James’ best-selling novel, starring Bette Midler and Alex Lawther, before returning to documentary in 2023 with Posso Entrare? An Ode To Naples . Up Against It Up Against It Maven Screen Media She continues to tap into her process as a documentary producer and director for her fiction work. For Up Against It , she spent time with NHS oncologists, notably at the Royal Marsden Hospital in London, in preparation for the film, which hinges around the fact that the best shot at survival for Alvaro and Saffron’s daughter Rose is the conception via IVF of a so-called “saviour sibling” with matching T-cells. While the premise sounds dark, the film is not, with Styler bringing a celebration of life; love and moving on, while holding on, to the big screen, reminiscent of Working Title classics such as Love Actually or Four Weddings and a Funeral but more complex. “TIFF was sort of amazing because I wasn’t prepared to have the applause, and people weeping, and also really roaring with laughter… In Up Against it , you do laugh as much as you’re touched and moved… that’s why I love cinema as a shared experience,” she says. Styler directs from a screenplay by Camille Griffen, based on an original story by Chloe King who wrote a first draft after being inspired by a segment on the NBC’s Today Show. Citing her research and discussions with oncologists, Styler says that around four saviour siblings were created in Europe last year but that the practice is being superseded by developments in paediatric oncology and CAR T-cell therapy, which uses a patient’s own white blood cells to fight cancer “I didn’t connect with it through the cancer story as much as that of the couple,” reveals Styler. “The couple split up because of Rose’s cancer. It seemed counterintuitive that you would break up when your child was in desperate need of you both, but then I spoke to oncologists who said that the path to a cure amongst families who have got a long cancer protocol in their lives, often requiring the mum to stay in hospital with the child, can put an enormous strain on the marriage.” Although the story was born out of a U.S. news item, Styler opted to transpose it to the UK where she has a better grasp of the health system. “I don’t know enough about it to get into the weeds of what universal medical care is there, but I do know a lot about the NHS, so I thought I’m just on better ground and safer ground,” she says, With two sisters who worked as nurses, one specialized in intensive care for babies, and the other in women’s health, Styler also has a deep respect for the staff throughout the NHS. “They’re not paid that well. They do many, many more hours a week than many other professions do… I felt that in the movie it was important to really include them,” she says. Styler adds it was also a joy to bring London to life on the big screen, describing the film as a love letter to the city, where she was based in the early years of her career as an actress. “I wanted it to look beautiful and diverse… it’s full of so many nations. And at its best, I think it’s a glorious city,” she says. “Because I don’t live here all the time now, I think I have a great nostalgia for it, and all it gave me when I was 18, 19, and I started to live my life as an actor, and that’s all I’d ever wanted to be.” “Through my kind of rose-tinted eyes, it’s the city that really gave me the love of arts that I have. I remember going to see Ian McKellen and Judi Dench in their Macbeth at the Donmar Warehouse and how brilliant and simple it was,” she continues. “My agent at the time, Elspeth Cochrane, was Ian’s agent. She managed to purloin me a ticket and when I saw that, ‘I was like, oh God, I really want to be at the RSC and do this.” The cast and crew for Up Against It taps into Styler’s network built over her 50-year career and life on the celebrity circuit with Sting. Antonio Banderas, Trudie Styler and Úrsula Corberó on set of Up Against It “I knew Antonio in the 1990s when he was married to Melanie [Griffith]. Then for a long time, our paths did not cross. I was living in New York, and he came to live in England for a bit,” she says of her connection with Banderas. “I’d been thinking who could play Alvaro because he’s not to everybody’s taste with his sexist remarks… somehow Banderas is one of those transcendent actors in that whatever he does, he remains lovable.” She recounts how a month after she sent the screenplay to his agent Manny Nunez, the actor requested a Zoom call in which he said he loved the part but requested one tweak. “He said, ‘I really love the script, but what I cannot be is a barrister called Peter.’ I said, ‘Of course, we will tailor make it to you,” she recalls, with Peter then becoming larger-than-life conductor Alvaro. Further cast include Úrsula Corberó ( Money Heist ) and Arinzé Kene ( The Pass, Lee ), as Alvaro and Saffron’s new partners, who become unwitting peacekeepers in the IVF process overseen by the real-life Human Embryology Authority, as well as Forest Whitaker, as NHS oncologist Doctor Augustus Abara, with Richard E. Grant, Mickey Sumner and Selana Tan also putting in appearances. Eden Hamilton ( The Railway Children Return ) plays Rose. Styler’s connections with Whitaker go back to 2013, when she was a coproducer on Christmas musical A Black Nativity , in which he co-starred alongside Angela Bassett and Jennifer Hudson, with the film shooting on location in New York’s Saint John the Divine cathedral. When Whitaker revealed he was not happy with his hotel, Styler invited him to stay at her New York apartment instead. “He said, ‘I never do that kind of thing.’ I said, ‘Well, the offer’s there.’ Later in the day, he asked, “Are you serious about me coming to stay at your apartment? I’d be really quiet.” I said, ‘Forest, it’s not a small apartment. There’s plenty of room’. My kids had gone to college, or they were working elsewhere… and Sting was on the road. I said, ‘It would be lovely to have your company’. We’ve called each other roomie ever since,” she recounts. After accepting the Up Against It role, Whitaker requested time with an oncologist for a briefing on Rose’s treatment to understand the real-life protocols around treating cancer. Styler’s award-winning crew, featuring editor Walter Fasano ( Call Me By Your Name ), Dante Spinotti ( Heat, L.A. Confidential ) and late multi-Oscar nominated Ghandi and Blue Planet composer George Fenton, is also the fruit of long connections. She has known Spinotti since the 1980s, working with him on films such as Mario Orfini’s Cinecittà-shot 1988 film Fair Game ( Mamba), in which she starred as a woman locked in an apartment with a deadly snake by her deranged computer scientist husband. He previously worked on Freak Show and Posso Entrare? and is also the cinematographer for The Reception . The interview takes place just days after Fenton’s unexpected death at age 76 in early October . Styler is caught off guard by the mention of his name and looks visibly pained by the thought of his passing, with the interview pausing momentarily. Styler, who is still reeling from his death, explains her friendship with Fenton goes back to a 1978 theatrical production of Hamlet at the Belgrade Theatre in Coventry in which she played Ophelia and he oversaw the music. “I was 23… He wrote my songs for Ophelia and through the years we just sort of ran into each other, and then this year I had nine months with him, composing that very beautiful score, seeing so much of him, and it’s like we recaptured those days in 1978, I think it was just before he did Gandhi .” “Spending those nine months with him was a sheer pleasure and also did a lot for my confidence, with him encouraging me and saying, ‘When you played Ophelia, I came to your first night. I thought it was a really stunning performance, and now you’re a director. You go on and direct as much as you want because you’re good.’” Maven & Backing Female Driven Storytelling Producer Piers Tempest, Trudie Styler and Celine Rattray at the TIFF Up Against It premiere Getty Images While revelling in her time behind the camera, Styler remains committed to Screen Media, her joint female focused banner with Rattray. Launched in New York in 2011, with offices in London, the company moved its main base to the UK capital in 2025. When Rattray first approached Styler in New York with the idea of working together, she had been mulling a move back into acting despite the then recent success of Moon. “She said, ‘Well, have a think about it’, and I said, ‘If we do it, it’s going to be something that’s niche and focuses on something missing in the film industry… what’s missing?’ We both look at each other and go, ‘Us?’” “Seventeen years later, here we are, making films that have pushed the needle on women in film above and below the line, and we’re very proud of what we’ve done.” The slate to date has included Andrea Arnold’s American Honey (2016) as well as Sundance prizes winners Novitiate by Maggie Betts and The Kindergarten Teacher by Sara Colangelo, with more recent credits including Scarlett Johansson’s Cannes-selected Eleanor The Great, Gurinder Chadha’s Christmas Karma , and Katie Holmes’ romantic comedy Happy Hours , which debuted in Tribeca in June. Men are not excluded with the company also getting pictures such as Guy Nattiv’s’s Skin (2018) and Mark Meyers’ Human Capital (2019). Styler cites figures collated by the Center for the Study of Women In Television and Film for the top 100 grossing U.S. films of 2025 showing that women accounted for 26% of producers, 20% of editors, 20% of writers and 11% of directors. “Since we’ve been more based in the UK, 90% of our films have been female directed,” she says proudly, highlighting the contrast. Additionally, 80% of Maven’s films since 2020 have had women in the leading role, while 70% were written by women. Styler acknowledges that it remains an uphill battle for women to achieve gender parity in the film and TV industries, says she remains optimistic for the future. “I do feel that the demographics are behind us. When I look at my grandchildren, we’ve got eight. I see that they are incredibly well informed, and they are no pushovers. And I do think it will get keep getting better and that storytelling will be more female driven,” she says. “I have to think like that because the alternative is to give up and retire and swing in a hammock or something, but I don’t have that in me. I’ve got lots of energy, and I love doing what I’m doing. I’m a grandmother, and I’m 72… I feel it’s my time to do what I want, and I’m really not afraid of saying what I think to anybody about this situation.” “Celine and I will continue to push on female-driven stories written by women, with women cinematographers… and wherever we can populate the films with diversity and women we will do it because the industry needs it and the world needs it. We need narratives that are more balanced. Otherwise, we are telling so many male action movies that really don’t have a beating heart.” On her own personal journey as a director, she says it is too early to say what comes next after Up Against It and The Reception , but admits she is in her element right now. “I don’t know now how many more films I’ll direct. Antonio said to me, ‘You seem so peaceful when you’re directing, the set’s so quiet, you never raise your voice.’ It’s because I’m actually in a happy place with myself and I’m so grateful to all these collaborators that are part of this.” Antonio Banderas, Eva Birthistle and Trudie Styler on the set of Up Against It Andrew Cooper Bass & Raman In Dead Heat For Mayor As Counting Continues Elected California Governor In Rout Of Ex-Fox News Host Steve Hilton Jean-Claude Van Damme Returns To Martial Arts Roots In Yakuza Action Pic Sky-ITV: Competition Bodies Get Greenlight To Probe $2.2B Deal Read More About: Comments

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Holocaust Drama ‘The Night Of Broken Glass’, With Clive Owen, Mélanie Laurent & Alexander Pettyfer, Gets North American Deal Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger & Nico Greetham Join Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell In ‘Survive: The Game’ Indie Film Fund Archetype Media Finance Launches With Nicolas Cage & Lucy Hale Films Among First Projects View All November 4, 2026 7:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (l-r) Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger, Nico Greetham Ruth Crafer/Faye Thomas/Luke Fontana EXCLUSIVE : Isabella Pappas ( Stranger Things: The First Shadow ), Heidi Berger ( Ludwig ) and Nico Greetham ( American Horror Story ) have joined the cast of Scout Taylor-Compton’s Survive: The Game , currently filming in Gipuzkoa, Spain. The trio rounds out the lead ensemble opposite previously announced stars Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander and Rohan Campbell. The film is shooting in Spain’s Basque region. The synopsis reads: “When a group of friends unearth an ancient board game inside a secluded cabin with a violent past, each roll of the dice brings a deadly fate to life, and the only way to survive is to finish the game.” Related Stories News Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton's Horror Movie 'Survive: The Game'; Filming Underway In Spain News Riccardo Scamarcio, Heidi Berger, Marco Palvetti & Nikesh Patel Join Cast Of Puglia-Shot Wedding Action-Thriller 'White Tide' - AFM Taylor-Compton is directing from a script she wrote with Michael Kennedy. The film is being lensed by Andy Patch, with editing by Bryan Shaw. The film is produced by Randy Wayne and Talia Bella under their Rebellium Films banner, Tom O’Connell and Scout Taylor-Compton of Building Blocks Productions, and Amy Covell of Red Phoenix Productions. Watch on Deadline Executive producers include Leire Apellaniz of Sr. y Sra., Mark Albela, Michael Kennedy and Dauntless Productions. U.S. casting is by Jonathan Clay Harris, CSA, and European casting is by Luci Lenox. Pappas, who next stars in Apple TV+’s Neuromancer and previously led ITV’s Finding Alice , will appear alongside Berger, who recently starred in Disney+ and Hulu’s House of the Owl and BBC’s Ludwig . Greetham, known for his Broadway work in Newsies and his turn opposite Meryl Streep and Nicole Kidman in Netflix’s The Prom , as well as roles in Ryan Murphy’s American Horror Story , completes the new cast additions. Pappas is repped by 42, Untitled Ent, and Lucy Popkin. Berger is repped by Conway van Gelder Grant. Greetham is repped by CAA, Independent Artist Entertainment, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman. articles.title: Bri Lee’s Novel ‘The Work’ Set For TV Adaptation At Dollhouse Pictures
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Kartik Aaryan To Star In ‘Ladaku’ With Kabir Khan Directing; Worldwide Release Date Set For 2027 ‘Colin From Accounts’ Maker Easy Tiger Adapting Dervla McTiernan Novel ‘Three Reasons For Revenge’ As TV Series ‘Black Snow’: Travis Fimmel Is Back On Cold Case Trail In Teaser For Season 3; Premiere Date Set In Australia View All November 4, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Work' is being developed for TV Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Bri Lee ‘s Australian bestseller The Work is getting a TV adaptation. Dollhouse Pictures – the Sydney-based production collective led by Rose Byrne, Krew Boylan, Shannon Murphy and Jessica Carrera – landed the screen option on the novel following a negotiation with rights holder UTA. Published by Allen & Unwin, The Work is set between New York, Brisbane and Sydney and follows Lally, an ambitious New York gallerist, and Patrick, a Sydney-based junior antiques appraiser, two young professionals, both desperately trying to establish themselves in the contemporary art world. Related Stories News Rose Byrne's Dollhouse Pictures Teams With Foundation Media Partners On Film Adaptation Of Anh Do's Novel 'Wolf Girl' Casting Rose Byrne's First Production From Her Dollhouse Pictures, 'Seriously Red', Underway; Will Star With Bobby Cannavale, Krew Boylan & More Per the synopsis, “When they meet, their chemistry is instant, beginning a turbulent long distant relationship. As their personal and professional lives become increasingly entangled, they begin to question if their love can survive distance, ambition and their cut-throat workplace.” Watch on Deadline Screenwriter Hannah Lehmann , who created and directed Snap original series Two Sides , is creating the TV series, with Lee and Carerra the executive producers. Screen Australia is supporting development. “I’ve always admired Bri Lee’s writing and her willingness to question power, privilege and the institutions that shape us,” said Carrera. “What excites me about The Work is its seductive world, where everything has a value and the rules are constantly shifting. At its heart is a complicated relationship that asks what if the person you desire most is also the person who costs you the most. Hannah Lehmann brings a sharp and assured voice to the adaptation.” Dollhouse’s productions include Dolly Parton biopic Seriously Red . Other titles on the slate include the first adaptation of Anh Do’s Wolf Girl , which we first reported on in October 2024. Lee said The Work had found “a production and writing team that are committed to making this show properly gutsy, hella sexy, and seriously funny.” She added the novel “was always so cinematic in my head, and Dollhouse Productions are going to take the words off the page and build a magnetic, can’t-look-away spectacle. Hannah is a genius who understands these characters’ deepest fears and desires.” Lee is represented by UTA and Grace Heifetz at a4 Literary. Her other books include non-fiction titles Eggshell Skull , Beauty and Who Gets to Be Smart , and literature publication News & Reviews . Her second novel, Seed , was published last year. articles.title: Toni Collette To Star In TV Adaptation Of Norwegian Dramedy ‘Pernille’ For Apple
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Toni Collette To Star In TV Adaptation Of Norwegian Dramedy ‘Pernille’ For Apple Sharon Horgan’s ‘Youth’ Renewed For Season 2 At HBO Sandy Frank Dies: Legendary Distributor & ‘Name That Tune’ Producer Was 97 View All November 4, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Toni Collette/Pernille Christian Hogstedt/Netflix Toni Collette is to star in Apple ’s latest dramedy. The Hereditary star is fronting Lenni , a comedy drama based on Norwegian series Pernille , also known locally as Pørni . The streamer has greenlit the series from Nine Perfect Strangers producer Made Up Stories and Homeland producer Keshet International . Lenni follows a divorced social worker who, after a family tragedy, tries to protect her loved ones from the rough-and-tumble of life. Per the logline, the series is a darkly comedic mystery about family – what it means to have one, to lose one, to pull one apart. Lenni, a child welfare worker and divorced mother of two, spends her days fighting for other people’s families while her own is in a constant state of hilarious chaos. The season follows Lenni through a new case, where the stakes couldn’t be higher as her work and personal life collides. Related Stories News Apple FYQ4 Revenue Tops Forecasts On iPhone Sales As New CEO John Ternus Steps Up News Netflix Taps Former Apple Exec Steve Wilson To Lead Podcast Acquisitions It also stars Ciarán Hinds, Dan Wyllie, Josh McKenzie, Celeste Barber, Genevieve Hegney, Arka Das and Wayne Blair. Watch on Deadline Lenni is based on Pernille , which was created by Henriette Steenstrup. The original ran for three seasons on Viaplay with its final two seasons airing on Netflix. Lenni is directed by Bad Sisters’ Dearbhla Walsh and adapted by Sarah Scheller ( Strife ). It is currently being shot in Sydney, Australia, supported by Screen NSW’s Made in NSW Fund. Exec producers include Collette, Scheller, Walsh, Steenstrup, Bruna Papandrea, Steve Hutensky, Katie Amos, Avi Nir, Keren Shahar, Bård Fjulsrud and Tanya Badendyck. Collette is represented by CAA, United Management, Finley Management and Jackoway Austen Tyerman Wertheimer Mandelbaum Morris Bernstein Trattner Auerbach Hynick Jaime LeVine Sample & Klein. articles.title: Holocaust Drama ‘The Night Of Broken Glass’, With Clive Owen, Mélanie Laurent & Alexander Pettyfer, Gets North American Deal
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Holocaust Drama ‘The Night Of Broken Glass’, With Clive Owen, Mélanie Laurent & Alexander Pettyfer, Gets North American Deal Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger & Nico Greetham Join Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell In ‘Survive: The Game’ Indie Film Fund Archetype Media Finance Launches With Nicolas Cage & Lucy Hale Films Among First Projects View All November 4, 2026 8:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clive Owen in 'The Night Of Broken Glass' first look International Film Trust EXCLUSIVE : Quiver Distribution has acquired the North American rights to The Night of Broken Glass , the historical drama based on true events, directed by Oscar-winning filmmaker Stefan Ruzowitzky ( The Counterfeiters ). As we’ve previously reported, the film from Dor Film, Benaroya Pictures and The Launch Company stars BAFTA and Golden Globe winner Clive Owen ( Children of Men ), Mélanie Laurent ( Inglourious Basterds ) and Alexander Pettyfer ( The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare ). Related Stories News Jean-Claude Van Damme Returning To Martial Arts Roots In Yakuza Action Pic ‘Katana’ For Jeremy Zag & The Veterans — AFM Casting Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger & Nico Greetham Join Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell In ‘Survive: The Game’ Written by Jonathan Frank, Scott Mann, Uli Edel and Julius Grützke, Quiver will release the film theatrically in North America on January 29. Historical thriller The Night of Broken Glass , based on the events of Kristallnacht, is “set in Berlin, in November 1938. Following the assassination of a German diplomat in Paris, Nazi propaganda exploits the incident to unleash a wave of violence against the Jewish population. As mobs storm Jewish neighborhoods and places of worship, Police Lieutenant Wilhelm Krützfeld (Owen) and his partner, Kai Lehmann (Pettyfer), investigate the murder of a Jewish doctor amid the escalating chaos. With orders to stand down as the city descends into violence, Krützfeld finds himself increasingly torn between his duty to the regime and his own sense of right and wrong. Over the course of one harrowing night, he must confront his conscience, find the courage to act on his convictions and decide whether he is willing to risk everything to do what is right.” Watch on Deadline “ The Night of Broken Glass is a powerful and gripping film about a defining moment in history, and the courage it takes to stand against injustice. With antisemitism once again on the rise around the world, this story feels particularly urgent and relevant. Stefan Ruzowitzky has crafted a compelling thriller that reminds us how quickly hatred can take hold, and how the choices of individuals can make a difference. As we mark International Holocaust Remembrance Day, we are proud to bring this timely and important film to theaters across North America,” said Quiver Co-Presidents Jeff Sackman and Berry Meyerowitz. “Making The Night of Broken Glass was an opportunity to revisit a defining moment in history and examine the human choices made in its midst. I wanted to approach the story with respect for the historical realities while exploring the characters and the decisions they face. I hope the film encourages audiences to reflect on how prejudice and hatred take hold, and on the importance of standing against injustice,” added director Stefan Ruzowitzky. IFT handles international sales. Bass & Raman In Dead Heat For L.A. articles.title: Voltage Pictures Gets ‘Nervous’ Around The World – AFM
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘La Bola Negra’ Caliente At Box Office With $43M Worldwide, Becomes Spain’s Top-Grossing Local Pic Of 2026 Blumhouse & Atomic Monster Unveil New Name For Combined Studio Lionsgate Teaming With Sony To Make Destin Daniel Cretton’s ‘Naruto’ View All November 4, 2026 8:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Nervous' Voltage EXCLUSIVE: Voltage Pictures has taken global rights (sans Korea) to the Sarah Bolger -starring psychological horror thriller Nervous , written and directed by Abner Pastoll ( A Good Woman Is Hard to Find , Road Games ). Sales are beginning on the title at the American Film Market. The pic also stars Ko Asung ( Snowpiercer , The Host ) and Sungsoo Yune ( Smugglers , Live Stream ). Voltage The plot: Desperate to save their crumbling marriage, Sarah and her husband relocate to the Korean countryside, where they discover a mysterious vinyl record that plays only silence. After listening, she loses the ability to hear men’s voices, plunging her into paranoia and hallucinations. Increasingly isolated and drawn to an enigmatic female neighbor, Sarah struggles to distinguish reality from nightmare. Is she losing her mind, or is something far more sinister at work? Related Stories News Trudie Styler Talks Journey To Directing 'Up Against It' & 'The Reception' Back-To-Back: "I'm In A Happy Place" News WTFilms Boards Italian Alps-Set Comedy-Thriller 'The Dregs' With Maddie Phillips & Stephen Lang - AFM The movie was shot in and around Seoul, with the project a South Korea-UK co-production from Story Robot and February Films, in association with Superbe Films and MAP, and in association with Solaire Partners and Central Investment Partners. Watch on Deadline The film is produced by Junyoung Jang and Pastoll, who also directs from a screenplay co-written with Richard Hobley. EPs are Guillaume Benski, Youngmin Kim and Sangjin Lee. The original score is composed by Matthew Pusti. “ Nervous represents the kind of bold, elevated horror that continues to resonate with global audiences,” said Alexandra Cocean, President International Sales and Distribution at Voltage Pictures. “Abner has crafted a provocative and deeply unsettling film that combines sophisticated psychological storytelling with striking visuals and an inventive use of sound. We are excited to screen the film to our buyers at AFM .” “ Nervous began with a simple but very unsettling idea: what happens when you can no longer hear the person closest to you?” said Junyoung Jang. “We wanted to explore that through sound and silence, creating something intimate, disorientating and cinematic. We’re thrilled to be partnering with Voltage to bring the film to audiences around the world and, for a film about silence, we’re excited to make some noise!” Nervous reps a reunion between Pastoll and Bolger following their collaboration on A Good Woman Is Hard to Find , which earned Bolger the Best Actress award at Screamfest. Nervous made its world premiere FrightFest 2026 as the opening-night film. It recently earned two honors at the 2026 Screamfest Horror Film Festival in Los Angeles, including Best Musical Score for Pusti and the inaugural ScareScore Biometric Best Picture Award. The movie is set to play MOTELX – Lisbon International Horror Film Festival, Fantasy Filmfest in Germany, Screamfest in Los Angeles, and the Festival International du Film de La Roche-sur-Yon in France, where it was selected for the Prix Variété competition. Additional selections include Belgium’s Razor Reel Flanders Film Festival, Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival in Estonia, and Japan’s YAMI Tokyo Horror Film Festival. articles.title: Nick Hall Strikes Producing Deal With Vice Studios
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Toni Collette To Star In TV Adaptation Of Norwegian Dramedy ‘Pernille’ For Apple Sharon Horgan’s ‘Youth’ Renewed For Season 2 At HBO Sandy Frank Dies: Legendary Distributor & ‘Name That Tune’ Producer Was 97 View All November 4, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nick Hall Trevor Paul/Vice EXCLUSIVE : Nick Hall , who has exec produces series including The White Lotus and worked at companies including HBO, Amazon and A24, is getting into business with Vice Studios . Hall has struck a non-exclusive producing partnership with the company to develop and produce scripted projects through his Hallogram banner. It comes just over twelve months after the youth-skewing hipster media company hired former Paramount and Amazon exec Amy Powell as President of Vice Studios and landed a $75M credit facility to fill out its programming slate. Related Stories Executives Nick Hall Joins A24 To Oversee Creative For TV News Amazon MGM Studios Readies Guy Ritchie & Rob Williams London Crime Drama ‘Capital’ With Vice Studios & Jack Tar Pictures Attached As part of the deal, Hall will exec produce two projects currently in the works at Vice. Watch on Deadline He will exec produce the TV adaptation of Anika Jade Levy’s debut novel Flat Earth , which Levy is written with Pen15 co-creator Sam Zvibleman, and workplace comedy Work Husbands, which is loosely based on the real-life relationship of Gen Z marketers Nate Jones and Ziad Ahmed. In addition to exec producing season one of The White Lotus , which landed him an Emmy win in 2022, Hall has produced series including Luca Guadagnino’s We Are Who We Are for HBO and Sky Atlantic and FX’s The Shards as well as French-language series Icon of French Cinema , which was co-produced with A24 and Arte. After starting his career as an assistant at UTA and in comedy at Warner Bros., Hall spent seven years at HBO before moving to Amazon, where he oversaw comedy, drama and YA series. After a producing pact with HBO, he spent a year working as a TV executive at A24 . The move marks the latest programming move for the Gangs of London producer since Fortress Investment Group, Soros Fund Management and Monroe Capital acquired it out of bankruptcy for $225M in 2023. Projects include Capital , a crime drama series from Guy Ritchie in development at Amazon MGM Studios UK, scripted drama series in development with Pablo Torre about sports ownership, extreme wealth and corruption, and an adaptation of the video game franchise Payday with Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson. “Nick has a rare combination of great taste, strong instincts and the conviction to take creative risks,” said Amy Powell, President of Vice Studios. “He has an incredible ability to recognize and champion original voices and material that others might overlook. I’ve known Nick for many years, and I’ve always admired his commitment to filmmakers and stories that challenge expectations. His sensibility is a natural fit for Vice, and I’m excited to see what we create together.” Nick Hall added, “I feel incredibly fortunate to have worked with some of the most trailblazing leaders and culture-defining companies in television. I’m grateful for the opportunity to continue that tradition with Amy and Vice.” Hall is represented by attorney Jared Bloch. Bass & Raman In Dead Heat For L.A. articles.title: Comedian Gianmarco Soresi Sets First Solo Netflix Special ‘God Forbid’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt ‘The Invited’ Series Inspired By Wendy Webb Novels In Works From Impossible Dream Entertainment & Wall To Wall; Helen Black & Jeff Howard Scripting Milo Hutton, Booboo Stewart & KaDee Strickland Board Horror Thriller ‘The Thing In The Hall’ Paul W.S. Anderson Sets Film Adaptations Of Kevin J. Anderson Books ‘Nether Station’ & ‘Nether Vortex’ View All November 4, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Gianmarco Soresi Derick Smith EXCLUSIVE: Gianmarco Soresi has announced that God Forbid — his second full-length stand-up special and first for Netflix — is set to premiere globally on December 3. Filmed over a sold-out run at Chicago’s Thalia Hall, the special navigates Soresi’s aspirations and anxieties around marriage and fatherhood, his skepticism about society’s substitutes for religion, and the double-edged sword of taking mental health seriously. This follows Soresi’s self-released 2025 hour Thief of Joy , which was widely praised as one of the year’s best. The special did powerhouse numbers on YouTube with more than 1 million views in its first week and 6M+ all time. Soresi returns to Netflix after showcasing in their series Verified Stand-Up . Related Stories News 'Trinity' Sets Release Date At Netflix; First Look & Trailer News 'La Bola Negra' Caliente At Box Office With $43M Worldwide, Becomes Spain's Top-Grossing Local Pic Of 2026 God Forbid is written and performed by Soresi, directed by Eric Abrams, and executive produced by Soresi, Tovah Silbermann and Matthew Vaughan for Rotten Science. Watch on Deadline Soresi told us, “After over a decade of doing stand-up comedy , I’m thrilled to finally release a comedy special that I didn’t have to upload myself.” Named one of Deadline’s Comedians Ready to Break Out In 2025 — and subsequently, one of our Comics Who Won 2025 — Soresi is a rising star comic based in New York City who’s known for his astute societal observation and spry, energetic stage presence. A performer with roots in musical theater, he pursued acting first before finding his footing as a stand-up, capturing millions of followers across platforms and building a major touring business within a decade. Soresi has been seen performing on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , The Late Late Show with James Corden , Comedy Central, Don’t Tell , and was selected as a JFL New Face in 2022. He hosts the popular podcast The Downside with Gianmarco Soresi , as well as the recurring NYC show Theater Adult , and this August, released the new crowd work hour, He Don’t Miss! . Currently on his global The Misery Loves Tour, spanning 30 cities across eight countries with a majority of sold-out shows, Soresi is repped by by WME, Mosaic and Cohen Gardner. articles.title: ‘Red, White & Royal Blue’ Author Responds To Texas Going Blue In Midterms: “It Was All In The Binder”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among Options Explored Post-Merger – The Dish Chanel Pysnik Departing As Head Of Nonfiction For Prince Harry & Meghan Markle’s Archewell Prods. Netflix Orders ‘Prep’ YA Series Based On Book From ‘One Day’ EP Nicole Taylor & Gloria Sanchez Prods. View All November 4, 2026 8:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Taylor Zakhar Perez in 'Red, White & Royal Blue'; U.S. Sen.-elect James Talarico Amazon Studios/Getty Texas made history Tuesday night during the midterms when James Talarico became the state’s first Democratic Senator since 1988, defeating Republican Ken Paxton. The flip may have come as a shock for many, but Red, White & Royal Blue fans saw it as a prophecy coming to life. In author Casey McQuiston ‘s popular 2019 novel and Prime Video’s 2023 film adaptation, Alex Claremont-Diaz ( Taylor Zakhar Perez ) is the son of America’s first female president, Democrat Ellen Claremont, played in the film by Uma Thurman, who is facing a tough reelection. Related Stories News Midterm Elections: Democrats Take Control Of Congress, Riding Big Wins In Texas, Michigan, Georgia & Maine Politics Midterm Elections: Amid The Blue Tsunami, A Night Of Many Firsts In a 14-page memo, aka the Texas Binder, Alex laid out an ambitious political strategy to turn his home state of Texas blue. It looked like a long shot, but he got a chance to implement it. In the end, the vote came down to Texas, which defied projections by going blue, securing Ellen a second term. Red, White & Royal Blue fans flooded social media after Talarico was announced as the winner, touting “the Alex Claremont-Diaz impact” on his victory. “It was all in the binder,” McQuiston wrote in response to Vulture’s IG post featuring a photo of Zakhar Perez as Alex with the caption “History, huh? #iykyk.” At Deadline’s Contenders Television held during the last election year, 2024, we asked Zakhar Perez and Red, White & Royal Blue producer Sarah Schechter which they think we’ll see first in our lifetime: an openly gay British prince or Texas going blue again? ( Red, White & Royal Blue follows the romance between Alex and a British Prince, played by Nicholas Galitzine, who comes out as gay.) “That is an excellent, excellent question. I really hope for both, I really just hope for both,” Schechter said back in April 2024 when Joe Biden was still the Democratic Presidential candidate. Added Zakhar Perez, “I think Joe needs to read Alex’s memo.” (You can watch the exchange towards the end of the video below.) Biden and his replacement Kamala Harris may not have read the memo, but Talarico clearly did. The Red, White & Royal Blue sequel, Red White & Royal Wedding, has been shot and is awaiting a release date by Prime Video. Bass & Raman In Dead Heat For L.A.
