articles.title: Johnny Depp on His One Condition to Return as Jack Sparrow for ‘Pirates of the Caribbean 6’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All November 3, 2026 6:18am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Johnny Depp and Orlando Bloom in 'Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl.' Walt Disney/Courtesy Everett Collection Johnny Depp is open to reprising his role as Captain Jack Sparrow should Pirates of the Caribbean return but for one reason. In an interview with Entertainment Tonight , the actor explained what would be his motivating factor to don the pirate hat again. “If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they are going to top off the Pirates franchise… the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note,” the actor said. Related Stories TV A Royal Surprise: 'The Remarried Empress' Releases One Day Early on Disney+ and Hulu TV 'Dancing With the Stars' Disney Night Makes Magic (3 Perfect Scores!) as Group Dances Return, Another Celeb Departs: See the Scores, Who Went Home He continued, “I will go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything. Doesn’t matter… if it’s Jerry, I trust him. We have a deep friendship.” Depp headlined the five Pirates of the Caribbean films that released from 2003 to 2017. Bruckheimer, who produced all five previous films, previously told The Hollywood Reporter in 2022 that they were “getting very close” with Pirates 6 and even had a “very good script.” The producer also noted that Pirates would be rebooted “so that is easier to put together“ given “you don’t have to wait for certain actors.” The last Pirates of the Caribbean movie, Dead Men Tell No Tales , was released was in 2017 and starred Depp, Javier Bardem and Kaya Scodelario, as well as returning franchise cast members Geoffrey Rush , Orlando Bloom , and Keira Knightley . Bruckheimer has been candid about work on a new Pirates film which would have Jeff Nathanson writing the script. Another reported film, penned by Christina Hodson from Birds of Prey , was to star Margot Robbie . In her Vanity Fair 2022 cover story Robbie said of the film, “We had an idea and we were developing it for a while, ages ago, to have more of a female-led — not totally female-led, but just a different kind of story — which we thought would’ve been really cool, but I guess they don’t want to do it.” However, Bruckheimer has said he still intended on getting a reboot and Robbie‘s film made: “We hope to get ’em both made, and I think Disney agrees they really want to make the Margot one, too,” Bruckheimer told Entertainment Weekly. “I think he’s cracked it,” Bruckheimer also told EW of Nathanson’s script. “He’s got an amazing third act. We just gotta clean up the first and second and then we’ll get there. But he wrote a great, great third act.” Bruckheimer previously told EW that he would welcome Depp to return to the role and had conversations with the actor about it. “It’s a reboot, but if it was up to me, he would be in it,” Bruckheimer said. “I love him. He’s a good friend. He’s an amazing artist, and he’s a unique look. He created Captain Jack. That was not on the page; that was him doing a little Pepé Le Pew and Keith Richards. That was his interpretation of Jack Sparrow.” THR

articles.title: Mark Lazarus: MS NOW Not Experiencing the Viewer “Fatigue” Lachlan Murdoch Complained About
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All November 3, 2026 6:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source MS NOW's new Times Square studio MS NOW MS NOW doesn’t have that viewer “fatigue” problem Lachlan Murdoch was going on about. Versant CEO Mark Lazarus was teed up with the word in a question asked Tuesday by a member of the analyst community. The analyst himself was teed up by a phrase Murdoch, the Fox CEO, used on his own company’s quarterly earnings conference call . “Yesterday, Fox called out some viewership fatigue on news leading up to the midterms,” Morgan Stanley’s Sean Diffley said during the Q&A portion of this morning’s Versant third quarter earnings call. “I’m curious how you would describe what you’re seeing most recently on MS NOW.” “We’re not seeing currently not seeing any fatigue with our audiences,” Lazarus responded. “Our audiences are active and vibrant and growing for MS NOW, and for that matter, with CNBC. I think it’s a testament to the quality of our product, to the voices that we have on there, and to the trust that our viewers have in our brands and in our talent. But we’re showing growth, and we have for…many months in a row on MS NOW, and that’s encouraging.” It was a fair shot to take following the TV ratings excuse Murdoch introduced just 24 hours earlier. “What we are seeing is some viewer fatigue, where our viewers have gone through an incredible news cycle last year with the inauguration, the Charlie Kirk tragedy, DOGE, flooding, it was an incredible news cycle last year,” Murdoch said, comparing what is currently happening to the 2006 midterms, when President George W. Bush was midway through his second term. “Those viewers are not switching to another news channel, they are just fatigued and watching slightly less television overall. We have seen this playbook, and we know how to move through it.” Murdoch has his own fair shot chambered for Laz: Fox News Channel is still beating CNN and MS NOW combined in viewers. Murdoch quipped on his call that Fox News really shouldn’t really consider CNN and MS NOW its “peers” given the ratings chasm between first and second place in cable news. At times, FNC’s Nielsen numbers rival those of the major broadcast news brands, Murdoch pointed out. Today is Election Day — get out there and vote. THR

articles.title: Sony Partners With Lionsgate on Destin Daniel Cretton’s ‘Naruto’ Movie (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit Plus Icon Borys Kit Senior Film Writer View All November 3, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Naruto' Courtesy of Crunchyroll Logo text Lionsgate has partnered with Sony Pictures for its high-profile feature adaptation of Naruto . The deal, which came after competitive, multi-studio bidding, will see Sony co-finance the movie and take on international distribution of the live-action feature film that is based on the manga by Masashi Kishimoto that grew into a global entertainment brand. Lionsgate has now officially greenlit the project, which is the follow-up feature for Destin Daniel Cretton , who his coming off the $2.5 billion success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day . Cretton is writing the script and will direct and produce. Production slated to begin in spring 2027, with Lionsgate continuing to oversee the film’s development and production and handle domestic distribution. Related Stories Business Lionsgate Inks Deal With Meta to Bring New 'Hunger Games' Movie to VR Glasses Movies 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' First Reactions That Sony’s motion picture group, headed by Tom Rothman, would come out on top seems almost pre-ordained. Cretton in September signed a three-year first-look producing deal with the studio, signaling a strong relationship with his Brand New Day partner. And Sony, which is headquartered in Japan, is also the home of Crunchyroll, the popular and arguably largest streaming service that focuses on anime. “With their deep expertise in manga and anime and global distribution prowess, Sony Pictures is a perfect partner for Naruto , and we’re thrilled to join forces with Tom Rothman and his team to bring this extraordinary property to audiences around the world,” said Lionsgate Motion Picture Group chair Adam Fogelson in a statement. “We share an enormous ambition for Naruto and a commitment to making this a truly global cinematic event that stays true to what millions of existing fans love and invites so many more to embrace what makes it truly special. Fogelson added, “I’m tremendously proud of Erin Westerman and James Myers for their work developing this film and bringing Destin aboard, and of Helen Lee-Kim for securing Sony as our international partner. Ari Arad, Tetsu Fujimura, and our producing team also deserve huge thanks for their hard work and support.” Stated Rothman, Sony’s Motion Picture Group CEO and chairman, “Lionsgate has done a masterful job in putting together an A-level adaptation, and we are honored to be chosen as their partner. Not to mention, we had a sweet success this summer with Destin and are delighted to be back in his capable hands.” Naruto is the coming-of-age story of a young and enthusiastic ninja named Naruto Uzumaki who wants to grow up to be the leader of his ninja village but also happens to have the spirit of a nine-tailed demon fox inside him. The story was serialized in Japan’s popular Weekly Shonen Jump from 1999 to 2014 and later spawned a couple of popular animated series that ran for years on Cartoon Network and Disney XD. Naruto sits in a rarefied tier of entertainment properties that have achieved an extraordinary global reach, enduring popularity, and cultural impact. Kishimoto’s manga has sold more than 250 million copies across over 60 countries and territories, growing into a multibillion-dollar franchise. The anime adaptation has reached audiences in more than 145 countries and territories. “As a longtime fan of Naruto , I’ve always loved that beneath the extraordinary action is a story filled with heart, humor, and humanity. Kishimoto-sensei created a world where unlikely heroes do extraordinary things, and that’s what makes it so special,” said Cretton in a statement. “Lionsgate has been an incredible partner, and I’m thrilled to reunite with the fantastic team at Sony. Together, we’re committed to capturing everything fans love about Naruto while introducing it to a whole new generation.” Avi Arad, Ari Arad and Emmy Yu are producing for Arad Productions. Cretton is producing alongside Jeyun Munford through his company, Hisako. Charles Melton is the only actor on board to star and is said to be playing Kakashi Hatake, the elite ninja mentor figure to the main character and his friends. The search for the actor to inhabit Naruto is currently underway. Erin Westerman and James Myers are overseeing the project for Lionsgate. THR

articles.title: British Celebrity Loses Legal Bid to Prevent Publication of Identity and Sexual Misconduct Allegations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Media set up outside London's High Court on Oct. 8, 2026 Courtesy of Getty Logo text A judge has ruled that an unnamed British celebrity facing allegations of “inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women” can be named in the press, but will remain anonymous while an appeal is lodged. The man had sought an injunction to prevent two news organisations, ITN and Guardian News and Media, from publishing his identity, over fears that he would be “highly likely” to kill himself. He maintained that the suicide risk is not attributed to any wrongdoing but because of what his lawyers described as “trial by media.” Related Stories Business Tokyo: Industry Insiders Skeptical of Bold Japanese Government Plans for Overseas Content Sales Push Business Tokyo: Japan's New Production Incentives Risk Doing as Much Harm as Good In a judgment that came Tuesday, Justice Nicklin rejected the injunction request and said: “The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make.” According to BBC News , London’s High Court heard that the celebrity denies that he abused “his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them.” Lawyers for ITN and the Guardian said his suicide risk could be mitigated and that there was no basis “to restrain the publication of public interest journalism.” Justice Nicklin had previously said there was “significant public interest” in the proceedings and that “this is a difficult and important case… The court must determine it fairly, on the evidence and legal submissions.” The British press have been warned against publishing any details that could identify the celebrity. Sara Mansoori, the lawyer representing the celebrity, told the judge in written submissions: “This is not a case where an individual has spuriously raised ‘mental health’ concerns in the face of an impending publication that they do not wish to occur… The claimant has attempted suicide twice as a result of these matters, been hospitalised for months, been the subject of involuntary detention and been examined by multiple — now more than 10 — doctors.” Mansoori also said the man “has no intention of returning to public life.” THR

articles.title: Pierce Brosnan Supports Callum Turner Being Cast as James Bond: “So Strong…”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Pierce Brosnan in 1995's 'Goldeneye.' United Artists/courtesy Everett Collection Logo text Former James Bond star Pierce Brosnan gave an enthusiastic shout-out to Callum Turner in his quest to become the next 007. During an interview with Vanity Fair , Brosnan was asked about the current “conversation” around the subject of Bond — presumably referring to media coverage about the actors reportedly being tested to take over the iconic role. The MobLand actor was very diplomatic in his answer, generously praising the field of young stars who are up for the part. Related Stories Movies Jack Lowden Is Tight-Lipped on Those Bond Rumors: "I'm Not Going to Add to the Noise" Movies Lowden, Turner or a Dark Horse: One James Bond Casting Test Has Nothing to Do With Acting Yet he did give a particular hat tip to Turner, whom he worked with on the 2017 film The Only Living Boy in New York . “Oh, I’m just an audience member now,” he said. “I’m just the man in the street who is eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history. All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men. Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.” Brosnan also had praise for Dune director Denis Villeneuve helming the new Bond film. “I think we are going to be blown away,” he said. “[Villeneuve] is such an iconoclastic director. His work is visionary, and his stealth and imagination of camera work and storytelling is so visceral and sensuous. It’s going to be great. It’s going to be truly magnificent.” As reported by The Hollywood Reporter , the actors testing for Bond include Turner and Slow Horses star Jack Lowden. Going into last weekend when auditions were set to take place, Lowden was the favorite in prediction markets. Since then, for whatever reason, Turner has surged ahead. Lowden recently reacted to his Horses co-star, Gary Oldman, suggesting the actor would get the role. “It’s all very flattering,” Lowden said to British GQ . “It’s nice to be mentioned — for any role — and I’m just not really going to add to the noise. It’s very nice, and Gary’s a sweetheart — it’s particularly lovely, coming from someone like him. But I don’t really listen to it.” Previously, Brosnan reacted to his MobLand co-star Helen Mirren blasting the Bond franchise for being sexist, noting, “She let them have it” and admitted, “Yes, there’s a certain agreement there. But there’s a certain world and room to move within the proscenium arch of what [Bond creator and author] Ian Fleming put down. So there’s always going to be conflict.” Mirren had said of the decades-old franchise, “I never liked James Bond. I never liked the way women were in James Bond. The whole concept of James Bond is drenched and born out of profound sexism.” Villeneuve is directing the new Bond outing, with Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing and overseeing the franchise for Amazon MGM Studios, which bought out the creative rights from the Broccoli family in February 2025. THR

articles.title: Should California Subsidize Noah Wyle’s ‘The Pitt’ Pay?
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Winston Cho , Katie Kilkenny November 3, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Noah Wyle in 'The Pitt' season three. Warrick Page/HBO Max For nearly 20 years, California has drawn a line between subsidizing pay for people in front of the camera and the workforce behind it. When the state started writing checks to Hollywood in 2009, the thinking was that the purpose of tax credits for films and TV shows would be to create jobs and juice the overall economy. That hasn’t changed through four iterations of the program across three governors. Its refusal to offset a production’s salary for, say, Tom Cruise, has made it an outlier among the 39 states that offer production incentives and is probably the biggest reason why it’s losing its grip as the filming capital of the world. Now — in a major pivot from its historic position that allowing productions to count so-called “above-the-line” spending toward expenditures for filming subsidies would be irresponsible — California is doing the math. Select lawmakers have come to a not-so-surprising conclusion among industry insiders: the state can no longer afford not to. “We’re still not competitive,” says Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur, a key legislator who has been working with Hollywood proponents to fine-tune the state’s incentive program. The idiosyncrasy to California’s film and TV tax credit program has been leveraged by competing states and foreign countries to coax productions into leaving. Now, Gov. Gavin Newsom is trying to fight back. On Monday, Newsom announced another major expansion to the program that, if passed, would increase the annual credit from $750 million to $1 billion and allow a portion of pay for actors, directors and producers to qualify, among other changes. Supporters have been clamoring for these costs to be counted for years, arguing that drastic changes must immediately be implemented to rescue production in California. Despite a record number of titles getting tax credits, production levels in Los Angeles, a barometer of shooting levels in the state, have continued to drop the last two quarters. The region saw a nearly 5 percent decrease in shoot days from June to September compared to the same period last year and an 11 percent drop compared to the previous quarter, according to the latest report from permitting office FilmLA issued last month. The total is 36 percent below the five-year average, highlighting the fierce competition between states and other countries to host Hollywood. Economists, however, remain skeptical about the value of filming subsidies, particularly whether they generate enough jobs and business activity to justify the cost. The Legislative Analyst’s Office said last year that the tax credits indeed increased production activity but that there’s weak evidence indicating that it benefits the state’s overall economy. The latest changes announced on Monday could throw more fuel onto the fire of whether taxpayers should be footing the bill for studios, some of which are engaged in major layoffs even as executive compensation remains sky high. Those same studios, it should be noted, have made a choice to go elsewhere, chasing cost savings. Take the example of the HBO Max hit The Pitt , which actually does shoot in California, on the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank. California is projected to give Parallax TV Productions, whose parent is Warner Bros. Discovery, nearly $49 million in subsidies across the series so far for shooting the show in-state. More than half of that figure will come for the filming of season three, after former Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav saw his total pay package soar to $165 million for 2025 and exit the company with more than half a billion dollars from the studio’s merger with Paramount. Additional layoffs are underway at the combined company, which made just 15 movies combined that filmed in the country over the last two years. While there haven’t been substantive discussions on the issue, Zbur says talks so far have acknowledged that taxpayers shouldn’t be subsidizing compensation for executives or A-listers. He draws a distinction between those two groups and other talent, several of whom he says are “barely getting by and only make family-supporting incomes.” It’s unclear how legislation could be drafted to account for that distinction, though something like a hard cap on individual salaries could be feasible. “There’s been some amount of consensus that we don’t want to allow tax credits for studio executives who are making a lot of money or star actors,” Zbur says. For years, New York, like California, had reservations about subsidies for above-the-line expenditures. But in a major expansion of the program last year, it eliminated a $500,000 cap on those costs. It’s a significant reason why California is poised to lose its title as the filming capital of the world, with New York drawing big-name titles at a much faster pace, according to industry tracker ProdPro’s latest quarterly snapshot, which noted that the state saw a 87 percent increase in production spend in the quarter compared with California’s 17 percent uptick. For California, the change is mainly aimed at drawing big-budget TV shows back to the state, where production in the category is roughly half below historical norms. Across its run, TV titles can accumulate substantial above-the-line costs since they employ a recurring cast, multiple writers, showrunners and producers in a single season. “The competitive reality is clear,” says Stephen G. Weizenecker, a partner at Barnes & Thornburg who handles tax incentives and financing for productions. “States trying to maximize production spending have included above-the-line costs to win the biggest films and television series. By excluding these costs, California has effectively been offering a smaller credit on the productions that it most wants to keep.” Still, questions will inevitably be asked about whether California taxpayers are on the losing side of the bargain. Hawaii in 2024 issued 32 productions $38 million in tax credits, according to a state economic report . Those titles paid $112 million in total wages, the report said, with above-the-line pay accounting for roughly $36.3 million. But just $11.7 million of that went to Hawaii residents; the remaining $24.6 million went to workers outside the state. The figures suggest that expanding tax credit eligibility to cover talent compensation could direct a substantial share of subsidies toward talent who don’t live in the state, raising questions about how much of that spending ultimately benefits the local economy. A major talking point will likely also revolve around California helping pay star salaries for productions that would’ve shot here regardless of the change. Take The Pitt again: If the series was already going to film in California for future seasons, the state will effectively be subsidizing an expense that didn’t influence the production’s location decision. The show already saw the size of its credit nearly double for the third season. Now, it’s probably in line to get even more. And with Newsom leaving office in the new year, it’s an open question on whether his successor in Sacramento will have the same enthusiasm for supercharging the state’s Hollywood tax credit. Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra has been cautious and specific about how he would deploy tax credits if elected. He’s favored expansion based on an “ongoing assessment of where we are losing work: post-production and VFX, independent productions, episodic television at scale, and whatever gaps the data reveals” — in other words, he wants to increase the tax credit, but carefully, and based on specific data. Meanwhile, he has not mentioned above-the-line costs. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to a spokesperson for Becerra on Newsom’s announcement. His rival, Republican Steve Hilton , on the other hand, clearly wants a major tax credit boost. In a move that’s even more aggressive than Newsom’s, he’s called for California to uncap its Hollywood tax credit entirely and include above-the-line costs as eligible expenses. (But, it’s worth noting, as of this writing, Hilton lags behind Becerra in several polls.) Regardless of which candidate wins the governorship, such legislation would face difficult questions in Sacramento, especially at a time when the state is still reeling from federal funding cuts. The optics of including above-the-line costs in a $1 billion annual tax credit fund during a period of serious affordability concerns would be, to say the least, tricky. Any legislators carrying such a bill would need to convince their colleagues in multiple parts of the state where Hollywood has less sway of the wisdom of such a move. But it’s clear that something needs to change to bring production back to Hollywood’s historic home. Could including above-the-line costs in incentives lure sets back? While not being able to do so previously is one of a much larger patchwork of complaints that producers tend to reel off about shooting in L.A., supporters seem to be suggesting that at this point it’s worth trying anything feasible to curb the flight of production. “We’ve made important progress but we can’t rest on our laurels,” Zbur says. “We need to continue focusing on the tax credit program to make sure we’re truly competitive.” THR

articles.title: Josh O’Connor Calls Bond Speculation “Incredibly Bizarre Pinch Me Moment”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:51am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Josh O'Connor for 'Disclosure Day' press in 2026 Courtesy of Getty Logo text Josh O’Connor is the latest star to play coy on the reports — including those from The Hollywood Reporter — that he is in the running for the role of James Bond . The Crown , Knives Out and Challengers actor was said to be screen-testing to replace Daniel Craig as Ian Fleming’s iconic MI6 agent. Among the small group of actors also in contention are Callum Turner and Jack Lowden . The Scottish Slow Horses star weighed in just this week on the speculation , telling British GQ : “Oh, Christ… It’s all very flattering. It’s nice to be mentioned — for any role — and I’m just not really going to add to the noise.” Related Stories Movies Pierce Brosnan Supports Callum Turner Being Cast as James Bond: "So Strong..." General News British Celebrity Loses Legal Bid to Prevent Publication of Identity and Sexual Misconduct Allegations The 36-year-old O’Connor, who also led Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day earlier this year, was opening the new Everyman Theatre in his hometown of Cheltenham, England, on Tuesday. He was probed about the Bond reports and admitted: “To be considered in that same sort of bracket is extraordinary.” He described the news as “such an incredibly bizarre pinch me moment… even being uttered in that same sentence and being considered for something like that. But I am afraid,” he continued, “there is nothing to say beyond that.” Toward the end of October, THR heard word that screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios’ James Bond film, directed by Dune ‘s Denis Villeneuve and written by Peaky Blinders mastermind Steven Knight, would be taking place in London imminently. While Jack O’Connell, star of Sinners and 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple , was rumored to be in the mix, sources confirmed this is not the case. Euphoria alum Jacob Elordi is also not testing. Also on Friday, in a new interview with Vanity Fair , former Bond himself Pierce Brosnan weighed in on the debate . “Oh, I’m just an audience member now,” he said. “I’m just the man in the street who is eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history.” The MobLand actor did say he admired all of the actors on the proposed list, but shouted out his Only Living Boy in New York co-star in particular. “Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong,” said Brosnan. “They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men. Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.” Nina Gold, the woman who cast Lowden in his Emmy-nominated role as Slow Horse ‘s River Cartwright, is also leading the search for Craig’s successor. She also happened to cast O’Connor in his breakout role (as Prince Charles in The Crown ). We await further news. Callum Turner, over to you… THR

articles.title: Cinemark Won’t Screen Brad Pitt’s ‘Cliff Booth’ Movie Over Netflix’s Demands, CEO Says
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:58am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Brad Pitt in Netflix's 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' Netflix Two theater chains are refusing to screen the upcoming sequel to Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood . Cinemark and Regal have decided against giving any of their Imax screens to The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , which has Brad Pitt reprising his role as a fearless stuntman in a movie written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher. The decision effectively makes Cliff Booth exclusive to AMC among the major chains. During Cinemark’s third-quarter earnings call early Tuesday, CEO Sean Gamble explained that the company decided against running the film due to Netflix ‘s very short release window — which ends just two weeks before the title shifts to streaming — and not wanting to establish a precedent that could come back to haunt the chain in future negotiations. “The Cliff Booth situation is an interesting one,” Gamble said. “We book all of our films on a case-by-case situation. In that particular situation, we always look at things through a long-term lens and how certain precedents and things we might do could affect longer-term industry dynamics. In this particular case, we don’t believe the proposed release model is constructive for the broader theatrical ecosystem, and it’s not aligned [with] what’s of the greatest interest in our theaters.” Gamble also added that keeping The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping on its Imax screens during Thanksgiving is a sold play due to the film’s strong advance sales. Cliff Booth will debut in theaters on Nov. 25, then hit Netflix on Dec. 23. For Netflix, which has traditionally resisted filmmakers’ efforts to secure theatrical releases for their movies, the film actually represents a first — the first time the streamer has released a movie in Imax. The slot was originally supposed to go to Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew , but the movie was pushed to February, where it will have a far more generous seven-week theatrical window. Cinemark Holdings posted higher revenue and earnings compared to a year ago, seeing total revenue rise to $1.05 billion versus $857.5 million in the same period of 2025. Gamble predicted the theatrical window could actually widen despite the rise of streaming. “We’re going to continue to see [the window] grow, especially since the commitments were a minimum of 45 days and beyond that many of the larger films continue to have windows of 60-plus days,” he said. “As we turn the corner into 2027, we’re going to see that window continue to expand a bit, especially as additional studios join in.” Etan Vlessing contributed to this report . THR

articles.title: GQ Expands Men of the Year Footprint in L.A.
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Adam Baidawi attends the GQ Men of the Year Awards at London's 180 Thames on Nov. 18, 2025. (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) GQ ‘s Men of the Year footprint in Los Angeles is growing — with some A-list names in tow. A marquee franchise for the Condé Nast publication, Men of the Year will be celebrated at three events this month in a showing that will mark the mag’s most ambitious run in the annual rollout. And this time it’s being steered by global editorial director Adam Baidawi, who took over in February 2026 after longtime editor Will Welch departed for a role working for Pharrell Williams in Paris. GQ has drafted Chris Rock , Andrew Garfield and Matt Damon to serve as Men of the Year co-hosts for their respective work in Misty Green, Artificial and The Odyssey . The three cover stars will bring some star power to the 31st installment of the series, which will also feature fellow honorees like GQ’s director of the year Denis Villeneuve for Dune: Part Three and designer of the year Michael Rider of Celine. Related Stories Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards Lifestyle Bob Iger Stresses Value of Communal Cultural Experiences in World "Rife With Disruption and Polarization" at PAC NYC Icons of Culture Gala As for those events, the Men of the Year celebration kicks off Nov. 10 at the recently opened Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, where GQ will host Villeneuve with a champagne reception, a live recording of GQ’s “One More Question” interview series fronted by senior special projects editor Zach Baron and a VIP screening of Dune: Part Two ahead of the franchise’s final bow on Dec. 18. Next up will be a “Breakouts” house party at the Sheats-Goldstein Residence on Nov. 11. The soiree wil host and toast the mag’s 13 Breakouts of 2026, a roster of boldfaced names across film, TV, music, comedy and podcasting. (The list will be published on GQ.com on Nov. 9.) And last but not least: the anticipated Men of the Year bash will return to Chateau Marmont on Nov. 12. An intimate dinner honoring the GQ’s cover stars will open the night and feature some starry (and filmed) toasts from special guests who will fete their friends. Then, after dessert, the action turns up a notch for the annual Men of the Year party that will once again host VIPs across entertainment, fashion, sports and culture. “This year’s GQ Men of the Year honorees have delivered extraordinary performances and propelled the cultural conversation of 2026. We wanted to meet that creative ambition with some of our own. Expanding to three events in Los Angeles — something brand new to Men of the Year — gives us the space to celebrate their work, get into the ideas behind it and introduce the talent we think everyone needs to watch next. It’s an ambitious new chapter for a tradition we love,” Baidawi tells The Hollywood Reporter in a statement. THR

articles.title: ‘Starlog’ Magazine Returns with First Cover in 17 Years
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Aaron Couch Plus Icon Aaron Couch Film Editor View All November 3, 2026 8:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Star Log returns with a new cover (right), 50 years after its first issue (left). Starlog The last time there was a new edition of Starlog magazine, J.J. Abrams’ Star Trek was still weeks away from hitting theaters, Robert Downey Jr. was just scratching the surface of Tony Stark’s potential on the set of Iron Man 2 , and George Lucas was still years away from selling Lucasfilm to Disney. In other words, it’s been a minute. But 17 years after publishing its final issue in April 2009, Starlog is back with a new edition, which arrives Nov. 13. The magazine launched in 1976 and gained a fanbase for being one of the few places to get reliable news and interviews about geek culture. It launched with a cover focusing on Star Trek , one of its key areas of expertise, but the magazine’s editors and writers also pioneered coverage of Star Wars . (The new issue chronicles some of the rumors it put out a year before the movie opened). In all, Starlog published 374 issues and more than 25,000 pages. Related Stories Lifestyle GQ Expands Men of the Year Footprint in L.A. Movies Cinemark Won't Screen Brad Pitt's 'Cliff Booth' Movie Over Netflix's Demands, CEO Says The new iteration will publish one issue a year under editor in chief Annalee Newitz, a founding editor of io9 . In addition to the film and TV-focused features Starlog was known for, the new Starlog will also delve into futurism, as the cover from Gabriel Yeganyan highlights. The opening story of issue No. 1 looks at the viability of humans farming crops on planets outside of Earth, for example. “Science fiction and fantasy give us a sandbox to reimagine our world, and Starlog is your invitation to play along,” said Newitz in a statement. “We’re honoring the fannish legacy of the original magazine and bringing it into the future with hopeful, awe-inspiring, and scientifically grounded explorations of where humanity could go next.” Starlog The revival was announced earlier this year, and includes a podcast hosted by Jordan Hoffman, a veteran journalist who has contributed to The Hollywood Reporter , as well as its weekly Lodestar

articles.full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 7:00am PT Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE) By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’ 31 minutes ago Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Magical Realist Tale ‘6TM’ and ‘Searching for SmarterChild,’ About One of the Earliest Chatbots, Win Top Industry Awards at Ji.hlava Festival 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Getty Olga Kurylenko (“Quantum of Solace,” “Oblivion,” “Black Widow”) and Alex Pettyfer (“Magic Mike,” “The Butler,” “The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare”) are set to star in crime thriller “Breakwater,” which has been boarded for world sales by WestEnd Films . The film, directed by Luc Walpoth (“In Tandem,” “Dead Money”), is set to begin production in April 2027. WestEnd will launch sales at the upcoming American Film Market. Related Stories Box Office: 'You Can See Everything' Beats 'Clayface' for No. 1 With $11.4 Million in Sleepy Halloween Weekend 'Ghosts: The Possession of Button House' Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win Set in a sun-soaked coastal paradise, “Breakwater” follows two women desperate for a way out. Iris (Kurylenko) is trapped in a toxic marriage, while Daya is a bartender desperate to escape her dead-end hometown. A chance encounter brings them together, and they hatch a plan to blackmail Iris’ sadistic husband Avery (Pettyfer) aboard his luxury yacht. But what seems like the perfect escape quickly spirals out of control. Stranded on the high seas, with nowhere to run and no one to trust, Iris and Daya find their carefully laid plan turning into a fight for survival. The film is produced by Kurt Wimmer (“The Beekeeper 1 & 2,” “Law Abiding Citizen,” “Point Break”), Jib Polhemus (“The Mechanic,” “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider,” “The Expendables 2”), Hannah Leader (“Mary,” “Freud’s Last Session,” “A Visit to Grandpa’s”) and Tad Daggerhart (“Black Lotus,” “Coyotes”), who also penned the script (“Expend4bles,” “Black Lotus”). Production in Malta will be overseen by Malta Film Service, led by partners Jean Pierre Magro and Vadim Fortunin. Walpoth said: “’Breakwater’ is a Mediterranean neo-noir thriller about lust, greed, betrayal and the desire to escape. Set against a gorgeous coastal backdrop, the film contrasts sun-drenched beauty with the darker tensions beneath the surface. Visually, I want to create a world that feels both sensual and unsettling, building from simmering suspense into a propulsive, high-stakes thriller as plans unravel and loyalties shift on the open sea.” Maya Amsellem, managing director of WestEnd, said: “’Breakwater’ is a gripping thriller with a fantastic cast in Olga and Alex and a hugely experienced creative team behind it. Luc has a distinctive cinematic vision for the film, blending the atmosphere of classic noir with the pace and intensity of a contemporary thriller. We’re delighted to be teaming up again with Jib Polhemus on such an exciting project, and look forward to introducing the film to buyers at AFM .” WestEnd’s wider AFM slate includes new supernatural horror “Sketchbook,” starring Woody Norman and Billie Piper (shooting early 2027); Tim Blake Nelson’s “The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd,” starring Amanda Seyfried and Scoot McNairy (screening at AFM); “A Visit to Grandpa’s,” starring Academy Award winners Anthony Hopkins and Catherine Zeta-Jones (in post-production); “Margot & Rudi,” a romantic drama directed by Anthony Fabian, starring Naomi Watts (in pre-production); action-thriller “Scorpion,” starring Pettyfer and Owen (in post-production); high-concept thriller “Ignition,” starring Maisie Williams; and “Unspeakable,” a horror from Corinna Faith, starring Eliza Scanlen and Essie Davis (in post-production). articles.title: Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars
articles.full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 7:20am PT Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars 1 hour ago Versant CEO: MS NOW Not Suffering From ‘News Fatigue’ Like Fox News 2 hours ago Versant Sees Q3 Profit Drop Despite Upticks in Non-TV Operations 5 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rose Wong for Variety Scott MacFarlane has traded in the desk once sat behind at CBS News on Election Night for something more direct — livestreamed midterms coverage for the progressive outlet MeidasTouch. He won’t have someone manipulating a Magic Wall or Big Board. He won’t be introduced by swelling orchestral music. And he won’t be competing with colleagues for precious minutes of airtime. MacFarlane will be ready to talk to followers via streaming channels starting at 7 p.m. Tuesday. Related Stories Korea Box Office: Anime Phenomenon 'Chiikawa' Remains Unstoppable as Yeon Sang-ho Thriller 'Paradise Lost' Debuts Box Office: ‘Street Fighter’ Scores $13 Million Debut as ‘You Can See Everything’ Opens at No. 2 With $5.5 Million on Friday At a traditional TV outlet, says MacFarlane, his contribution would have been curated by producers. This year, he says, “the voice we get to use is my voice. I am going unscripted, without a teleprompter, just telling people point blank what’s happening.” Dozens of independent journalists will do the same. Coverage of returns on Election Night has long been dominated by the nation’s big TV-news outlets . This year, however, so-called “ creators ” — indie journalists and non-traditional experts — want their own piece of the audience. In addition to the MeidasTouch stream, which will feature MacFarlane along with former MSNBC host Katie Phang, former NBC News political guru Chuck Todd will hold forth with colleague Chris Cillizza in a live stream they call “The Projection.” It will appear across YouTube, X, Substack, Decision Desk HQ’s Votes portal and Noosphere, one of many new subscription platforms that offers access to the work of expert journalists. Piers Morgan , whose Uncensored company won millions in funding late last yea r, is traveling from London to host several nights of coverage in the nation’s capital. Jim Acosta and Katie Couric , two popular former mainstream TV anchors, will team up to host a live stream from the University of Virginia, and have booked guests including Rahm Emanuel, Pete Buttigieg and Tara Setmayer. Don Lemon, the former CNN anchor, will greet guests such as Joy Reid and Hunter Biden while presiding over a show in a New York City bar. Even staid CSPAN is getting in on the craze, and plans to simulcast hours of coverage from progressive outlet The Young Turks and conservative commentator Patrick Bet-David. Despite some of the hosts’ mainstream roots, many of them think they can bring viewers something the legacy outlets cannot. “This will be Murdoch-Ellison-free coverage,” says Acosta of the show he and Couric plan to put on, making a direct nod to the ownership of Fox News by the Murdoch family and the control over CBS News and CNN now enjoyed by the Ellison family , which controls the newly formed Skydance. “Katie and I are free to let it rip.” The ability to speak frankly and with little corporate oversight isn’t the main reason pundits and independents are gathering. Many of these people see a big opportunity to generate subscriptions, advertising and revenue — and to draw bigger audiences to their various outlets in an era when the economics of media are decidedly in flux. “I think this is a precursor to what we are going to see in two years, with more audiences coming to platforms like ours, along with more top-tier guests, and more newsmakers,” says Rashida Jones, who was named CEO of Morgan’s company in March after a stint running MSNBC. Advertisers were eager to sponsor Morgan’s shows from Washington, D.C., she says. A good Election Night showing by Morgan, she says, can only generate new audiences and business. Will there be enough of both to help all these companies thrive? About 58% of U.S. adults see social media as a key means of staying current with the news cycle, according to a recent Pew Research Center survey. Approximately 13% indicated social media was the most important way to get news. When Pew issued a similar survey in 2022, 43% of Americans said social media was an important way they got news, and 5% said it was the most important. “The crowd’s going to keep on growing,” says Jones. “This is the turning of the corner of that audience coming to digital-first platforms.” The independents aren’t the only ones who see a growing opportunity. Mainstream media is also seeding the ground. Fox Nation, the Fox News streaming outlet, will run a three-hour live special led by the team behind the popular Ruthless podcast . Josh Holmes, one of the co-hosts, says he will likely not drink alcohol even though the event will take place in front of a crowd in a Washington D.C. bar. “We will try to keep a sense of humor about topics that people often get sort of negative about, and then we always provide what we think is an under-the-hood look at serious topics,” says Holmes. The team doesn’t see the livestream as competing with Fox News coverage led by Bret Baier, Martha MacCallum and Bill Hemmer, says Holmes. “Wwe are supplementing that, trying to give some perspective.” Several “Ruthless” members have jobs as strategic political advisers and can offer unique insights. NBC News this year is launching its first vertical-video program, led by anchor and correspondent Gadi Schwartz. He will be on the ground in Texas and will talk with various NBC News journalists based in different parts of the country. The program will “really look at a more conversational approach to how the night is unfolding,” says Catherine Kim, NBC News’ executive vice president of editorial, and will play out not only on the company’s social media feeds, but also Schwartz’ own. Independents who once had a strong foothold in legacy media may have the best chance of surviving. Couric and Acosta booked their own guests and are taking a strong hand in designing the look and feel of their Election Night program. “We both worked for a long time with legacy media, and I think it made the transition to a digital platform much easier for us, because we came in with a built-in audience to a certain extent,” says Couric. “We want to have both of our audiences intersect and come together on Election Night, and it will be hopefully good for both of us.”’ The duo say they know which elements of news presentation to keep and which to jettison. Delivering important information is in. Doing it in an overly formal way is not. “We want to make it unlike what the networks are doing,” says Acosta. “We are not going to be overly stilted and scripted and all of that stuff. This is much more freewheeling.” And, potentially, blunt. Couric says she can say things that NBC and CBS would never have allowed her to state when she worked for them on programs like “Today” and the “CBS Evening News.” “I think we are liberated,” says Couric. “I don’t think our hands are tied in the way that network anchors are with their corporate overlords breathing down their necks.” And since the program will be done on their own terms, Couric and Acosta can also relax — well, at least a little bit. “We are going to be much more casually dressed than I was when I did election coverage for CBS,” says Couric. “There might be an open bar,” says Acosta. ‘Thirteen in Gaza’ Acquired by Koudéta Films for France Ahead of Doha Film Festival New Japanese Animation Prize Named Nippon Anime Awards, Sets First Ceremony for November 2027 MS NOW Has 2026 Midterm Elections Coverage: Here’s How to Watch Election Night Results Live Online Free Elena Maganini, Film Editor on ‘Dexter,’ ‘Henry, Portrait of a Serial Killer,’ Dies at 70 Emraan Hashmi’s Musical Horror Film ‘Rooh’ Adds Tips Films and Tips Music (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Vote for America 2026:’ Here’s How to Watch Newsmax’s Midterm Election Special Online for Free Loading comments...

articles.title: Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada’s Bitcoin Creator Movie ‘Satoshi’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 7:24am PT Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada’s Bitcoin Creator Movie ‘Satoshi’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE) By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest ‘Thirteen in Gaza’ Acquired by Koudéta Films for France Ahead of Doha Film Festival 3 hours ago John Travolta Set for Torino Film Festival Award Ahead of ‘Propeller One-Way Night Coach’ Screening (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago First Vatican-Produced Film Submitted to Oscars Boarded by Hollywood Ventures Group (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty/Biscuit Media A new feature film titled “Satoshi,” about Bitcoin’s pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto, is set to be directed by Jason Zada (“The Forest, “Terrarium”) with backing from former NBA champion and tech investor Tristan Thompson . The plan is to start shooting in Saudi Arabia and Los Angeles in spring 2027. Tristan Thompson — who is known in the tabloids for sharing two children with Khloé Kardashian — will produce “Satoshi” alongside Enderby Entertainment principals Rick Dugdale and Dan Petrie Jr. Related Stories How 'You Can See Everything' Became a Surprise Box Office Hit (and Likely One of the Biggest Docs of All Time) Box Office: 'You Can See Everything' Beats 'Clayface' for No. 1 With $11.4 Million in Sleepy Halloween Weekend “Satoshi” is among the first projects under a multi-picture deal between Enderby Entertainment and Saudi Arabia’s Yellow Camel Studios production company. The plan is to shoot the film at JAX Film Studios, a state-of-the-art production complex in the Saudi capital city of Riyadh. The creator of Bitcoin, whose identity and invention remain secret, is also the subject of the Doug Liman-directed film “Bitcoin” (aka “Killing Satoshi”) which has a cast including Casey Affleck, Pete Davidson, Gal Gadot and Isla Fisher. “Bitcoin,” which is currently in post, has sparked controversy for using AI to create the movie’s sets and lighting, having been reportedly filmed in just 20 days inside a “gray box” studio in London. Also on board “Satoshi” as producers are BDE Ventures founder and Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies pioneer Brian D. Evans, as well as actors Aaron Arnold (“Splitting Image”) and Austin Arnold (“Splitting Image,” “Altcoin Daily”), according to a statement from Enderby Entertainment. “Satoshi” will examine the origins of Bitcoin, which was created in 2008 in the wake of the global financial crisis as a way to circumvent traditional financial institutions. Zada and Nate Atkins (“Take This Lollipop”) partnered on the shooting script, based on an original screenplay by Cam Cannon (“Zero Contact”). Zada, who is the founder of the AI-native studio Secret Level, is currently in production on the AI hybrid horror feature “Terrarium.” However, while AI will be used as a tool in making “Satoshi,” AI is “not the main focus of how the film will be made,” according to a rep for the film. “This is a traditional film production, including on-location filming, etc.,” the rep stated. The “Satoshi” logline reads: “A troubled FBI agent partners with a charismatic defense attorney under federal pressure to unmask Bitcoin’s elusive creator, Satoshi Nakamoto — plunging into a high-stakes crypto thriller of government overreach, personal demons, and a mystery that still defies the world.” “Bitcoin wasn’t born in a boardroom. It was released as open-source code by someone who chose to disappear,” Dugdale said in a statement. referring to the ongoing effort to unmask the mysterious Satoshi Nakamoto, author of the bitcoin white paper which laid the theoretical foundations for modern digital currencies. “We’re not interested in a sanitized version of that story,” he added. “We’re bringing in people who understand the code, the culture and why it mattered from the beginning.” “Jason has been pushing the edges of how films get made, and with the support of the Saudi kingdom we have the room to do this properly,” the “Satoshi” producer continued. Commented Thompson: “We are entering a new financial era where money moves at the speed of the internet, value flows seamlessly across borders and entirely new systems of ownership and exchange are emerging. Satoshi sparked a movement that is fundamentally reshaping how the world thinks about wealth, freedom and financial power.” Evans underlined that “for years, the traditional media has misunderstood Bitcoin and the people who built it,” and pointed out that this film “isn’t about unmasking Satoshi. It’s about getting the narrative and story right for the world to finally see.” Enderby Entertainment was founded in 2006 and has previously produced “Blackway,” starring Anthony Hopkins, Julia Stiles and Ray Liotta, which premiered at Venice in 2015; Ben Kingsley-starrer “An Ordinary Man”; “Night Hunter Henry” with Henry Cavill, Ben Kingsley and Alexandra Daddario; and the three-film anthology based on Swedish writer Hakan Nesser’s “Intrigo” trilogy of novels. Zada is repped by UTA and Dante DeSario at Collage. articles.title: Nicole Taylor, Country Singer in Triplet Trio Taylor Red, Dies at 35
articles.full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 7:58am PT Nicole Taylor, Country Singer in Triplet Trio Taylor Red, Dies at 35 By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Funko Launches New ‘Harry Potter’ Mystery Collectibles Ahead of HBO Series 31 minutes ago Nicole Taylor, Country Singer in Triplet Trio Taylor Red, Dies at 35 32 minutes ago Josh O’Connor Describes Bond Rumors as ‘Incredibly Bizarre Pinch Me Moment’: ‘To Be Considered Is Extraordinary’ 1 hour ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nicole Taylor , a country singer and one-third of the identical triplet trio Taylor Red , which built a massive following on TikTok and Youtube, has died after a battle with breast cancer. She was 35. Taylor died Sept. 28 at her home in Nashville, Tenn., according to a statement on the group’s website. Her sisters and bandmates, Nika and Natalie Taylor, announced her death in an emotional video posted Monday, Nov. 2. Related Stories Box Office: 'Street Fighter' Aims for $30 Million Opening, 'You Can See Everything' Could Score $8 Million Start Box Office: ‘Clayface’ Lands at No. 1 with $10.4 Million Debut, ‘You Can See Everything’ Adds $6.14 Million on Friday “We are heartbroken to announce the passing of our sister Nicole Taylor,” Nika said in the video. “We honestly thought she’d be healed here on earth, but now she’s healed in heaven.” Nicole was diagnosed with an aggressive form of stage 3 breast cancer in 2022. Although she initially responded well to chemotherapy and was declared to have no evidence of disease, the cancer eventually returned and progressed to stage 4. Doctors gave her three months to live following the diagnosis, but she lived for another year. “She tried not to live in fear, remained really hopeful,” Natalie said. “She traveled, she tried to live life, she worked really hard, she tried to have fun.” Born and raised in southern Mississippi, Nicole formed Taylor Red with her identical triplet sisters, Nika and Natalie. The siblings began performing together in 2010 under the name Red Roots, releasing three albums before rebranding as Taylor Red in 2018. Known for their genre-blending country music and tight harmonies, the sisters played guitar, banjo, fiddle and mandolin. The trio later found a new audience on social media, where their synchronized performances, musical covers and comedy bits helped them amass millions of followers. In 2020, Variety featured Taylor Red in a report examining how female country and pop groups were using TikTok to build audiences outside traditional industry channels, alongside acts like Avenue Beat and Four Diamonds. Their 2021 song “Country Money” became one of their best-known releases. In their tribute, Nika and Natalie remembered Nicole, the oldest member of her sisters by minutes, as their “fearless leader” and best friend. “Nicole, the oldest of us three sisters, will be greatly missed,” they wrote on the group’s website. “She was our leader and our best friend. We are heartbroken, but we know she is in Heaven and will see her again.” The sisters said Nicole remained devoted to her Christian faith throughout her illness, continuing her exercise, travel and work even while undergoing treatment. The family has held a private funeral service. In lieu of flowers, fans are encouraged to make donations in Nicole’s memory to Samaritan’s Purse, one of her favorite charities. articles.title: Funko Launches New ‘Harry Potter’ Mystery Collectibles Ahead of HBO Series
articles.full_text: As HBO prepares to bring audiences back to Hogwarts this Christmas, Funko is getting in on the magic with a new collection of “Harry Potter” mystery figures , including a chance to uncover an ultra-rare collectible. The new “Harry Potter” POP! Mystery collection features six characters from the original film series: Harry Potter , Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley, Luna Lovegood and twins Fred and George Weasley. Each four-inch vinyl figure comes in blind-box packaging, meaning buyers won’t know which character they’ve received until they open it. Each box also includes a corresponding collectible POP! card. Related Stories Box Office: ‘Street Fighter’ Scores $13 Million Debut as ‘You Can See Everything’ Opens at No. 2 With $5.5 Million on Friday 'Ghosts: The Possession of Button House' Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win Funko x Harry Potter Pop! Mystery Box SHOP ONLINE $14.99 Priced at $14.99 each, the figures have equal one-in-six odds of appearing in a standard box. Collectors also have a one-in-72 chance of discovering a special Mystery Chase figure, with an even rarer one-of-one Worldwide Chase potentially hidden in the collection. The release is part of Funko’s recently introduced POP! Mystery line, which taps into the growing popularity of blind-box collectibles. Previous collections have featured characters from “KPop Demon Hunters,” “One Piece” and Warner Bros. horror franchises. Funko has also introduced a buyback program for eligible one-of-one figures, offering collectors $10,000 in exchange for verified rare finds. The latest “Harry Potter” merchandise arrives ahead of HBO’s highly anticipated television adaptation of J.K. Rowling’s bestselling book series, which is scheduled to premiere Dec. 25 on HBO and HBO Max. The new series will introduce a fresh generation of Hogwarts students, led by Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley. The cast also includes John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape and Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid. The first season will adapt “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone,” with Francesca Gardiner serving as showrunner and executive producer and Mark Mylod directing multiple episodes. HBO is already developing a second season based on “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets,” with Kit Harington recently announced as Gilderoy Lockhart. The HBO adaptation marks the franchise’s first major live-action television retelling, more than two decades after Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint first brought the central trio to the big screen. The original eight-film franchise, released between 2001 and 2011, remains one of the highest-grossing film series of all time. Funko’s new “Harry Potter” POP! Mystery figures are priced at $14.99 per box. Loading comments...

articles.title: BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’
articles.full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 8:11am PT BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’ By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’ 45 minutes ago Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Magical Realist Tale ‘6TM’ and ‘Searching for SmarterChild,’ About One of the Earliest Chatbots, Win Top Industry Awards at Ji.hlava Festival 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Speaking about an editing error that triggered a $10 billion defamation lawsuit pursued by President Donald Trump against the BBC , the broadcaster’s deputy director-general Rhodri Talfan-Davies said Tuesday that “a lot has changed since then.” Talfan-Davies said there were two issues about the BBC’s handling of the controversial episode of investigative show “Panorama.” “One was the actual edit itself, and second, and I think probably more profound in the end, was the BBC’s sluggishness in its response,” he told journalists at a Broadcasting Press Guild lunch. Related Stories Korea Box Office: Anime Phenomenon 'Chiikawa' Remains Unstoppable as Yeon Sang-ho Thriller 'Paradise Lost' Debuts 'Ghosts: The Possession of Button House' Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win He outlined the measures that the BBC had implemented to address these issues, which included his own appointment in June 2026. “A lot has changed since then. There’s been a reform of the editorial standards committee, which has been led by Caroline Thomson. The role of the deputy director-general has been created precisely to grip those types of moments and make sure that we get to quick, timely decisions,” he said. He added that the BBC had “instigated over the last 12 months what we call ‘Final Gate’ processes on our most contentious programs.” Explaining what these “Final Gate” processes were, he said, “It means that before you commit to transmission or broadcasting, all the key players involved in the title, including editorial policy, including compliance execs in each of the key genre, they get in the room and they go line by line through the key risks of the program. So there is a really diligent and thorough assessment of the program before it airs.” He cautioned that he couldn’t guarantee that “there won’t be future issues in an organization that digs deep and delivers big investigations … I mean, I’m not naïve.” However, he added, “I do think the processes and controls put in place in the last 12 months put us in a much stronger place.” Talfan Davies, who is a journalist by training, recalled his reaction when he heard of the editing error. “I thought it was a mistake,” he said. Prompted by Variety to expand on that, he said, “Well, I don’t think there was anything malign in it. Right? I think the edit as it stood in the program created a mistaken impression about what precisely was said in that moment by the President, and we caught that issue. It was a BBC review that identified the issue. The real problem was we then didn’t act quickly to put the issue to bed, to be transparent about what had happened, and to apologize for it.” Questioned about whether there was an issue with the culture among BBC journalists that may have caused the editing mistake, he responded, “No, because I think if you look at the wider program, the whole program, you’ll see the extreme care that has been taken in terms of the balance of perspectives and viewpoints in the program. I just think that one edit was problematic.” Asked if he felt it was more likely that the BBC would be able to win the case in the U.S. than six months ago, he said, “Well, I think the key next moment is the decision by the Florida court on whether it has the jurisdiction to even decide this. I think our case on that is very strong, but I’m not in the business of second guessing judges. But we have put our best foot forward in terms of setting out the arguments about why we don’t think it should be heard in a U.S. court, and we’ll wait to hear what the judge says.” Moving onto other issues, Talfan-Davies was asked about accusations of left-wing bias at the BBC by right-wing politicians like Nigel Farage. Talfan-Davies explained what his response would be if Farage were in the room making that accusation. “I’d say two things. Firstly, it’s not my experience at the BBC. I’ve worked in many newsrooms. The discussion is robust, and the conversation is pretty open-minded in terms of different perspectives,” he said. “What I would say is that whilst I don’t see that evidence of bias, you always have to constantly review how you’re doing. “One of the parts of my role is to make sure, as an executive team, we up the ante in terms of how we robustly review our editorial performance. It’s one thing to look at audience metrics, but you also need to really closely scrutinize and be rigorous about how you’re delivering, if you like, your ‘public mission.’ It’s one of the areas that I’m discussing with [the BBC’s director general Matt Brittin], and we’ll say more in the coming months about how we really up the ante on that.” ‘Elsinore,’ ‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’ and ‘Animol’ Lead British Independent Film Awards Nominations Versant Sees Q3 Profit Drop Despite Upticks in Non-TV Operations Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars MS NOW Has 2026 Midterm Elections Coverage: Here’s How to Watch Election Night Results Live Online Free BTS, Katseye Drive Hybe to Record Quarterly Revenue and Profit ‘Okinawa Saudade’ Director Matsubayashi Yoju on a 10-Year Journey Tracing Brazilian Dancers’ Island Roots Loading comments...

articles.title: Disney To Undergo More Layoffs With Divisions Eyeing Up To 20% In Cost Savings
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro , Nellie Andreeva November 2, 2026 7:29pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Walt Disney Studios Exterior Gilbert Flores/Getty Images The Walt Disney company is laying the groundwork for more cuts, with thousands poised to be impacted. According to sources, the new round of layoffs will be made across multiple divisions, including TV networks and the motion picture studio, at varying amounts. As is customary in the run-up to staff reductions, managers of the affected teams have been given targets, with some asked to achieve as much as 20% in annual cost savings, we hear. Disney declined to comment on the latest cuts, first reported by Bloomberg, whose exact timing is unclear. Related Stories Executives Utopai Studios Names Former Disney AI Exec Hans Ku Chief Product Officer News 'Star Wars' Voices & Sounds Made Available To Gamers And Creators By Tech Firm Voicemod There have been ongoing layoffs at Disney throughout the year following Josh D’Amaro taking over as CEO from Bob Iger on March 18. In April, 1,000 roles would be eliminated, followed by several hundred in July, with Pixar and National Geographic among the divisions most affected . Watch on Deadline The process accelerated in August when the entertainment conglomerate extended a Voluntary Early Retirement Offer to longtime executives. That process has now been completed, with some sources indicating that more eligible managers opted for the package than anticipated. The VERO was always considered a precursor to layoffs. “This is one of several actions we’re taking to reshape our organization, including involuntary staff reductions that have already begun in some areas and will continue into next year,” Disney EVP and Chief People Officer Sonia Coleman wrote at in memo back in August. Since then, a couple of hundred employees were laid off in late September , largely in areas such as tech and HR, and last week, another 100-200 employees in its Experiences division were pink slipped, the majority of them at Disney’s Imagineering campus in Glendale. “I think like all of our similarly situated competitors, and certainly all of our competitors in the tech industry, there is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured,” Dana Walden, President and Chief Creative Officer of The Walt Disney Company , said about the continuous layoffs during Bloomberg’s Screentime conference last month. “Technology set their sights on our business, and we must survive and thrive and grow. That’s what we’re going to do.” D’Amaro has put a focus on cost reductions since ascending to the top Disney job earlier this year. At the most recent Disney earnings call, he spoke about using some of the savings to invest in growth areas. “When our teams work smarter, we can serve more people across our parks and digital platforms and do it more cost-effectively,” he said. “That frees up capital to reinvest aggressively in what drives long-term value: new content and next generation guest experiences, as well as technology infrastructure that keeps Disney at the forefront of entertainment.” Disney’s global head count stood just north of 230,000 as of the end of the most recent fiscal year. articles.title: New Anti-Harassment Laws Lead To Questions From UK Film & TV Industry
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max John Leeson Dies: Actor Who Voiced Iconic Role In ‘Doctor Who’ Was 83 Ex-YMU Global Entertainment Boss Launches London Agency Repping Creators Including Topjaw’s Jesse Burgess Russell Brand’s Defense Argues Channel 4 Film “Poisoned Well Of Justice Deliberately” View All November 3, 2026 1:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty EXCLUSIVE: Big UK production groups and studios have been busily preparing for new anti-harassment laws that will impact the film and TV industry, but questions remain. Last Friday, UK-wide legislation came into force that means employers are now liable for harassment of their staff, cast and crew by third parties. Employers must take “all reasonable steps” to prevent harassment, the law now states, and claims can be made up to six months after an incident takes place. The legislation is part of the UK’s much-discussed Employment Rights Act, one of the ruling Labour Paty’s flagship pieces of reform. Related Stories News International Insider: European TV In Peril; Venice & TIFF Latest; Mercedes Ron Interview News International Revenues Of $2.1B Boost British TV Makers, Census Finds, As Pact Warns BBC Must Avoid "Managed Decline" The adustment has led many big production houses and studios to update their harassment policies in preparation, we are told. “These changes give victims much stronger legal protections,” said the government when the legislation, which applies to all industries, came into force. Watch on Deadline In practice, this change means that if cast or crew are harassed during a production by a third party, be that an agent, someone on location or even someone who has nothing to do with the project, the production company or studio could now be liable for the claim. “This is a significant change,” said Elizabeth Peyton-Jones, who runs The Talent Trust, which takes real-time reaction data from crew working on productions. “As an employer, you can’t now say, ‘I can’t control what other people do.’ You have to take responsibility. And the duty of care reaches beyond the set.” Producers we spoke with were mostly aware that the legislation was coming in and have been preparing, but they still have questions over just how far this duty of care reaches. Peyton-Jones used the example of a wrap party, where people who didn’t work on a project could be invited and incidents could happen. Would the producer then be liable for the actions of that third party? “Wrap parties are an interesting example because they are informal,” she added. “People have been working together for a long time; stress and exhaustion are high. If someone doesn’t speak up until long after production has wrapped, and if nothing was time-stamped and no action was taken, then a production company can’t simply say it didn’t know. It should therefore have a mechanism for people to raise concerns.” Deadline understands at least one large production outfit considers wrap parties, late-night working and staying in hotels as part of its risk assessments. “Where does the buck stop?” Other examples floated to Deadline that require clarity include incidents that take place on the street when crew are doing vox pops, harassment on transport on the way to-and-from a set, or situations where crew have to accompany third parties for filming. The vision behind the legislation, communicated by the government last week, is that “whether a passenger harassing a bus driver, a waiter being intimidated by diners, or a shop worker dealing with abuse from customers, reforms will ensure that unacceptable behaviour is not treated as part of the job.” Max Rumney, the deputy CEO of producer trade body Pact , which represents hundreds of UK indies, said the question of “where does the buck stop?” is confusing his members, and he doesn’t feel he has all the answers from government. “In many ways this is a law for environments that are slightly different to ours,” he explained. Pact’s legal chief sent a note to all members last week, which Deadline has seen, urging them to “update their anti-harassment and bullying policies, if you have not already done so, to ensure that you remain compliant with the law.” We are also told that training body ScreenSkills has updated the anti-bullying and harassment module on its training passport in line with the legislation. This all feels necessary. Just a few weeks ago, a survey from UK arbitration service Acas found that two-fifths of employers across all industries were unaware of these changes in law. Making things more confusing is the fact that the law has technically come into force but detailed guidance will only be available from early 2027. Deadline understands the UK’s Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, and Digital, Culture, Media and Sport have both been prepping the industry, meeting with trade associations, hosting webinars and pushing employers to update their policies. The departments wouldn’t be drawn on specific examples of when an employer would be liable for harassment or not. We spoke with big production groups in the UK who said they have been preparing for the change but wouldn’t come on the record to discuss further. One HR executive at a big player said they had updated contractual terms for future productions in order to account for the new third-parties law. Of course, some indies are much smaller, often one-or-two-person bands, and many don’t have HR departments, which could lead to issues with the new law. Movies are often run by production outfits only created for that particular project before being shut down. If an incident takes place on one such movie but is only reported months afterwards, the responsibility could fall on a company that has just been dissolved. Pact’s Rumney, however, reckons bigger productions will be more problematic. “Small indies make smaller productions and they know how to do these things,” he added. In the UK film and TV industry, harassment remains a huge topic, in part due to high-profile instances of allegations in recent years. The anti-harassment legislation came into force on the day a prosecuting barrister delivered closing arguments at the Russell Brand trial, for which the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. Brand denies all allegations and says all relationships were consensual. Those we have spoken with rejected the idea that the new law will lead to a flood of harassment complaints, with many barriers that prevent the industry’s majority freelance workforce from making claims still in place. “I think there will still be resistance [to complaining],” said Peyton-Jones. Talent Trust research has previously pointed to a “silence gap” on UK productions. A report recently found 40% did not feel respected or treated with dignity on a production and yet more than three quarters (76%) didn’t feel they could speak up without worrying about unfair repercussions. Many concerned industry folk are hopeful the “silence gap” will begin to close now that the long-expected CIISA anonymous whistleblowing service has launched . The new harassment laws could contribute to a further closing of the gap, but this feels a bit of a way off.
